title: Project identity derived from a mutable path (id = sha256(path)) forced a delete/copy/re-key cascade on every move — making ids immutable and detecting moves via a git-tracked anchor removes the migration entirely, but every direct path-hash call site has to be found and re-pointed by hand
summary: ProjectStore.generateProjectId(path)=sha256(path): every folder move minted a new id, forcing relocateProject delete/copy/re-key + orphaning Assistant hibernation. #11285 makes ids immutable, detects moves via a git-tracked .daintree/project.json anchor, adds mintProjectId collision guard + resolveProjectIdForPath; WorkspaceHostEventRouter/PullRequestService.ts:379 remain unmigrated.

summary: test

title: A security gate patched into the file an issue names can still leave other platforms unguarded: Electron's OS file-open ingress forks per-platform (macOS open-file vs Windows/Linux argv scan), and a latest-wins preload replay buffer silently drops concurrent cold-launch events
summary: PR #11283 (issue #11280) fixed unguarded .dntr plugin install by building electron/setup/archiveInstallIntent.ts, but the issue named only electron/setup/openFileInstall.ts (macOS open-file); Windows/Linux double-click ran a fully independent implementation in electron/lifecycle/appLifecycle.ts (installDntrPath, pendingDntrPaths, isValidDntrArchive) with no shared call site. Also fixed: electron/preload.cts's _eventBusBuffered replay Map collapsed to latest-wins, silently dropping all but one .dntr archive on a multi-file cold launch; new _eventBusFifoReplay set makes plugin:archive-install-intent accumulate. Lesson: audit every platform ingress path before trusting a bug report's file pointer, and distinguish ambient replay signals from discrete decision queues when wiring preload event-bus replay.

title: data-no-dnd only opts out sensors written to check it — a nested raw TouchSensor still arms a drag — and a ref written+read during render is a real repaint hazard, not just a React Compiler nag
summary: PanelHeader.tsx/TabButton.tsx: data-no-dnd is a convention checked only by DndProvider.tsx's NoDndMouseSensor/NoDndTouchSensor (isNoDndTarget); the tab strip's separate tabSensors DndContext uses raw upstream PointerSensor/TouchSensor which ignore it entirely, so a long-press in a tab rename field still armed a drag until a manual e.stopPropagation() touchstart guard was added. Separately, DeletedWorktreeCard.tsx held a countdown value in a useRef written and read during render (9 React Compiler errors, compiler-budget:critical 13->4) — a real repaint hazard since ref writes schedule no re-render; fixed via the 'adjust state when a prop changes' pattern (derived holdKey + conditional setState), reaching clean CompileSuccess. Contrasts with #10426's legitimate ref-at-render use-no-memo cases.

title: Path-containment allow-lists must enumerate real state via git worktree list, never predict it from a config pattern — and the raw list still needs vetting: bare entries grant the object store, stale prunable records plus path reuse make an on-disk .git check the last line of defense
summary: systemShell.ts assertPathAllowed guarded shell.openPath/EditorService.openFile with predicted worktree parents (collectWorktreeParentDirs + pathPattern), over/under-admitting at once (#11277). Fix: collectTrackedWorktreeRoots enumerates GitService.listWorktrees() per project, excluding bare entries, filesystem-root paths, and stale prunable records missing an on-disk .git.

title: A type's doc comment is not the runtime contract: FileChangeDetail.path says worktree-relative but electron/utils/git.ts stores absolute, and panel.worktreeId is a stale stamp, not a fact about where the file lives
summary: electron/utils/git.ts's addChange writes absolute paths into FileChangeDetail.path though the type docs claim worktree-relative, breaking changesMap equality lookups; file.openPanel also stamps panel.worktreeId from the active worktree, wrong when rootPath resolves elsewhere. Fix: path.ts's toWorktreeRelative/isPathInside normalize paths; FilePane derives worktree by deepest-path containment.

title: A staged diff's new side is the index blob, not the working-tree file — reading disk shows content the diff was never generated from, so verify a fetched source against the diff's own hunk lines rather than trusting the diff kind
summary: Diff panel Full file view (#11268): staged diff new side is the git index blob, not disk -- reading disk shows post-stage edits as verified context. fullFileAvailability.ts limits full-file reads to working-tree/unstaged; DiffViewer.sourceMatchesHunks verifies each hunk's new-side lines land at newStart before trusting fetched source, else falls back to changed-lines-only.

title: Deleted-worktree auto-close countdown must charge only observed time, not wall-clock: a cached WebContentsView still reports visible, and Chromium throttles hidden windows to exactly the sweep's own 1Hz interval
summary: sweepDeletedWorktreeCleanup (src/store/deletedWorktreeCleanup.ts) trashed live agent terminals on thaw because expiresAt was a wall-clock timestamp stamped at deletion; a cached WebContentsView never flips document.visibilityState (src/lib/viewCacheState.ts, #11212) and a minimized window's timers throttle to exactly 1Hz, this sweep's own interval, so hidden did not mean paused. Fix: rows arm unarmed, charge only observed time via lastSweepAt gap-crediting (MAX_OBSERVED_SWEEP_GAP_MS), and holds (drag/confirm/working-agent) pin remaining time with capped durations instead of re-arming to full TTL each tick. Regression introduced by #11237's original countdown; arc also includes #11266 (grouped rows) and #11275 (rescue-follow selection).

title: bottom-0 on an absolutely positioned child resolves against the padding edge, not the border box, so it can never visually merge with a sibling border-b — and swapping that border for a painted div silently vanishes under forced-colors
summary: DeletedWorktreeCard.tsx ghost rows drew a doubled bottom rule: border-b paints the border box, sibling bottom-0 countdown bar resolves at the padding edge one border-width above — no z-index fix works. #11265 merges into one 1px track, fixing a forced-colors border/background regression (CanvasText/Highlight). Regression of #11237.

title: AssistantContentMirror's sync must fail closed on stale-but-still-present destinations (deleted content that survived removal) yet fail open on merely-missing ones — and an unreadable source directory is not the same as an absent one, or retirement decisions get made on state never actually read
summary: AssistantContentMirror.syncAssistantContent (electron/services/AssistantContentMirror.ts) mirrors user commands/skills into help-session dirs before every Codex/Claude/Copilot assistant launch. #11258 replaced one blanket try/catch with a three-way failure taxonomy: AssistantContentSyncResult.staleFailures (deleted/superseded content that survived removal — fails HelpSessionService.provision() closed via HelpSessionError USER_CONTENT_SYNC_FAILED) vs omittedSkills/failedCopies (merely missing new content — warns, launches anyway). Splits absent (ENOENT/ENOTDIR, safe to retire) from unreadable (EACCES/EIO, unprovable, must throw) via isAbsentError/WalkState.unreadableDirs. Writes the ownership manifest as a superset before mutating, compacts to verified reality after an lstat-based destFileState pass, so a crash mid-sync stays safe and successfully-removed paths are never re-claimed later. Also fixed HelpSessionError's typed code never surviving Electron's contextBridge (dead MCP_NOT_READY/etc branches in production) via the same message-prefix encode/decode pattern already established in #6116/#8583 for AppError/GitOperationError.

title: Content-sized dialogs collapse-then-expand across a lazy()/Suspense swap because a layout effect fires one frame too late — the height must be pinned synchronously inside the triggering event handler, and a release timeout just reschedules the same collapse
summary: FilePane's markdown source/rendered toggle inside PanelDialogHost/AppDialog (max-h-[85vh], no min-height) remounts the subtree, so MarkdownViewer's lazy()/Suspense skeleton (no height floor) collapses then re-expands the dialog. Fix: useHeightHold pins minHeight synchronously in FilePane.handleViewModeChange before the Zustand setFileViewMode dispatch (a useLayoutEffect in the new subtree fires one commit too late). Release waits for MarkdownDocument's onRendered first-commit signal plus two requestAnimationFrames (layout then paint), never a timeout — an earlier 4s deadline was deleted in review because releasing mid-load reproduces the same collapse on a delay. min-height as a floor needs no ResizeObserver: content only grows past it or settles once.

title: h-full silently collapses to auto under a flex parent with indefinite height, so a panel needs flex-1 min-h-0 at every wrapper between the layout host and the pane root, invisible ones included
summary: ContentPanel.tsx, ContentFadeIn (registry.tsx), and ReviewPane.tsx used h-full alone: fine under grid block cells, collapses to auto under PanelDialogHost.tsx's flex-column BodyScroll (max-h-85vh) — panel sizes to content, scroller never overflows, dialog clips it (#11254). Fix: flex-1 min-h-0 alongside h-full at every wrapper, incl. ContentFadeIn.

title: Forge provider migrations silently drop non-functional behaviors of the concrete method they replace — the second confirmed instance, after #9061 dropped caching, is #11251 dropping required-check enrichment
summary: GitHub forge plugin: PR dropdown (listPRsImpl, coarse statusCheckRollup via LIST_PRS_QUERY/mapListCIStatus) and worktree sidebar (getCIStatusesImpl, deriveRequiredCIStatus, required-check-aware) computed CI status via two separate pipelines, so a green rollup masking a failing required check read passing in one surface and failing in the other. Legacy GitHubPRs.listPullRequests enriched with required checks; the forge-provider migration re-homing listing into readOps.listPRsImpl silently dropped that behavior, same shape as #9061 dropping caching/dedup in forgeProvider.runQuery. Fix: enrichPRPageWithRequiredStatus routes list enrichment through existing getCIStatusesImpl (shared derivation, shared prRequiredStatusCache, 4s budget via Promise.race, open-rows-only, degrade-to-coarse on rate-limit/reject), and removes a one-way mutateCacheEntries patch in WorktreeStoreContext.tsx that only wrote the renderer forgeResourceCache, never main's forgePRListCache.

title: Built-in plugin renderers compile into the host bundle, not a plugin:// asset — folding forge slots into contributes.views needs a new build boundary, and a manifest-only middle path was already tried and reverted
summary: src/registry/builtinPluginRenderers.ts serves plugin UI (bulk-create dialog, issue selector, settings tab) via eager import.meta.glob into the host bundle (package.json sideEffects-pinned), unlike contributes.views which lazy-imports a plugin://{id}/{path} bundle via PluginViewContent.tsx — no such asset exists for built-ins, blocking issue #11244's fold. A reverted contributes.builtinViews draft broke PluginManifest typecheck, broke external slots-using plugins, and was circular vs slots. Merged fix instead: builtinViewRegistrations.test.ts source-scans plugin.json forgeProviders.slots refs against registerBuiltinView(id, ..., {pluginId}) calls in renderer/index.ts(x), catching dropped refs and pluginId ownership mismatches that silently left disabled plugins' UI on screen.

title: Dialog-presented panels: the store, never the component, must own an ephemeral record's create/destroy — React 19 StrictMode double-invokes mount effects, and a single-slot dialog stack self-defeats the moment a dialog opens a dialog
summary: panelDialogStore/PanelDialogHost (#11247, #11249, #11252): ephemeral dialog-panel records must be created/destroyed via store actions (openPanelDialog/pushPanelDialog), never mount effects, since React 19 StrictMode double-invokes them. Single-slot store self-defeated when a dialog review hub opened a child diff dialog; fixed via dialogStack:string[] + expectedParentId compare-and-swap.

title: An empty worktree list means 'host not ready', never 'zero worktrees' — treating [] as authoritative turned a boot race into compounding persisted corruption
summary: panelRestorePhase.ts getKnownWorktreeIds: truthy-empty-array bug read a resolved-but-empty worktree.getAll() (host-not-ready boot race, #8827) as confirmed-zero-worktrees, re-homing every saved panel onto activeWorktreeId and persisting the corruption across restarts. Fixed via a length-check guard plus gating cleanupOrphanedTerminals PTY-kill on worktree-known checks.

title: A grid panel kind that skips ContentPanel silently loses click-to-focus — and moving it back in creates a duplicate focus-registry entry that clobbers the first with no error
summary: PluginViewHost mounted plugin panels in a bare div with usePanelRootFocus (delivery) but skipped ContentPanel handleClick→onFocus() (selection): clicks left focusedId stale, so Cmd+W closed the wrong terminal (#11228). Fix routes through ContentPanel outside ErrorBoundary/Suspense, drops the duplicate usePanelRootFocus call — the focus registry Map silently clobbers duplicates.

title: Plugin archive install hung forever past a 64KiB entry: Node 24.16's Readable.pause/resume no-op regression met fd-slicer's raw destroyed-flag stream-end, and only an app-side inactivity abort could catch it
summary: extractPluginArchive piped yauzl entries via stream.pipe with no timeout; installPlugin awaited it under a lockfile lock. Node 24.16 Readable.pause/resume no-op-on-destroyed regression met fd-slicer's raw destroyed-flag stream-end, stranding the last chunk past 64KiB highWaterMark, hanging forever. Fixed: Electron 42.7.0, yauzl 3.4, 30s inactivity abort.

title: Blanking core.hooksPath to disable repo hooks sets a RELATIVE path — git-lfs self-installs against its own cwd, littering every new worktree root
summary: electron/utils/hardenedGit.ts set core.hooksPath= (empty) to block repo git hooks (#3742). Empty is a relative path -- git-lfs resolves it against its own cwd when self-installing hooks, and git worktree add cwd is the new worktree root, so post-checkout/commit/merge/pre-push littered every LFS worktree (#11226). Fixed with an absolute app-owned userData/git-hooks dir.

title: A file-size cap must match how the content is consumed, not the source of the bytes — and a pre-read stat() is advisory, never the real ceiling
summary: electron/setup/protocols.ts readContainedDaintreeFile shared a single 512KB DAINTREE_FILE_MAX_BYTES cap across daintree-file:// and daintree-html://, blocking normal-sized images (decoded as pixels, not strings) with silent 413s that looked like viewer bugs. Fix: maxBytesForFile() raises the cap to 25MB (DAINTREE_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES) only for raster MIME types, gated by an allowLargeImages boolean per caller (viewer=true, scriptable daintree-html preview=false, SVG excluded via separate sanitizing files:read path) plus a post-read buffer.length re-check since fs.stat() is advisory (TOCTOU grow-after-stat; O_NOFOLLOW only blocks final-component symlink swaps, not size changes). Generalizes: size caps must key on downstream consumption model and caller threat model, not a single blanket constant; pre-operation checks need a post-operation re-check.

title: xterm's WebGL glyph atlas is a module-global cache with eviction gated on a static Daintree never set — the fix is capping maxTextureSize, not touching app-side disposal
summary: Project-view renderer memory grew 50-135MB/hr streaming agent truecolor output (#11210), never recovering on close. Root cause: addon-webgl's module-global CharAtlasCache (ownedBy ref-counting) plus a FourKeyMap glyph cache that never evicts since maxTextureSize sat at hardware max. Fix: TerminalWebGLAtlasCap.ts caps it at 1024, wired from TerminalWebGLManager.ts.

title: document.visibilityState never flips for a cached child WebContentsView — every hidden-view CPU gate built on it alone is dead code, and only an explicit main IPC lifecycle signal can catch it
summary: Electron perf trap: ProjectViewLifecycleController.deactivateEntry caches backgrounded project WebContentsViews via removeChildView + view.setVisible(false), neither of which flips document.visibilityState (Chromium tracks occlusion at the BrowserWindow level only, not per child view). TerminalReconciliationWatchdog, TerminalReflowController, and TerminalWriteController all gated periodic/rAF work on visibilityState, so cached views kept running at 4.5% CPU / 3300 wakeups-sec, and the watchdog issued real forceReflow/ensureWebGL repairs against hidden panes. Fix: src/lib/viewCacheState.ts, a renderer singleton fed by main's app:view-cached/warm-activated/revealed IPC, latched in electron/preload.cts to survive cold-switch subscription races; must AND with (not replace) the visibility check, gate every call site not just timers, clear on warm-activated not revealed, and never touch the byte-stream ingest path.

title: Tier-2 memory reclaim looked broken because it was never measured — tier1's cooldown made the logged delta a no-op bracket, and tier2's own actions ran after the last sample
summary: electron/services/ProcessMemoryMonitor.ts: issue #11211 read 9 reclaim deltas (0,6,0,29,0 MB) as proof tier1/tier2 levers are weak. Actually tier1's 5-min cooldown zeroed the before/after bracket, and tier2's own actions ran after its last sample — never measured. Fix: per-tier settle-resample bracket + action counts; rejects clearTextureAtlas()/GC-nudge as new levers.

title: A code-split chunk is not an entry: the host React import map pointed at vendor-react's private cross-chunk exports, and the fix (`export * from` a CJS package) emits nothing without explicit names
summary: vite.config.ts's hostImportMapPlugin mapped all five React specifiers at vendor-react's code-split chunk -- Rolldown's private cross-chunk exports, not React's public API -- breaking every build since v0.15.0 when plugins called useState (#11208). Fix: hostReactFacadePlugin emits per-specifier entry chunks with explicit named exports, guarded by a generateBundle check.

title: getAnimations() excludes finished fill-mode:backwards animations — WAAPI cancel()/play() silently no-ops on exactly the spent entries you're trying to replay
summary: ContentGridEmptyState.tsx launcher entry (fill-mode-backwards, app:view-revealed) needs JS replay on project switch (persistent WebContentsView, no remount). WAAPI getAnimations()+cancel()/play() silently returns empty for finished backwards-fill animations — dead replay, no error. Fixed via animationName reset+reflow restart; corrects #11209's cold-view hypothesis.

summary: test summary

title: PtyPool disposed only half of its onData/onExit listener pair, and the undisposed half leaked on the acquire path — the one code path nobody audits because it looks like success, not cleanup
summary: electron/services/PtyPool.ts disposed onData's dataDisposable everywhere but left onExit's disposable unstored, leaking on acquireByKey's success path; same gap in connection.ts's close listener. Also a pre-1.2.0-beta.14 node-pty macOS kqueue fd leak. Fixed via exitDisposable, disposePooledListeners, closeHandler, node-pty bump, FdMonitor calibration; fds +60/run to 0.

title: A new sandboxed protocol document inherits two invisible collisions with the trusted app shell: the global CSP webRequest overlay silently overwrites its per-document CSP, and Electron 42's COEP credentialless blocks it from ever rendering as a frame
summary: electron/setup/protocols.ts daintree-html:// preview scheme (#11198, fixed by #11200): Electron 42/Chromium 148 routes protocol.handle responses through session webRequest.onHeadersReceived, so the global CSP overlay (setupWebviewCSP, applyDaintreeAppCspToSession, mergeCspHeaders in electron/utils/webviewCsp.ts) silently overwrote the token-scoped per-document CSP unless explicitly bypassed via isDaintreeHtmlPreviewUrl. Separately, the app document's Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: credentialless (electron/utils/appProtocol.ts, vite.config.ts) blocks embedding any iframe whose response lacks a matching COEP header, producing a blank white iframe with no CSP console error, shipped broken because PR CI never runs the covering E2E spec that would have caught it.

title: A settled null in a tri-state error field reads as falsy: guarding a mount-fetch effect with `!error` instead of `error === undefined` spins an infinite fetch loop on the exact success case that produces no data
summary: pulseStore.ts getError returns string|null|undefined (undefined=never fetched, null=settled no-commits). ProjectPulseCard and new ProjectPulseStrip (#11197, closes #11194) guarded mount-fetch with `!error`, true for both, so a no-commits repo loops fetchPulse/git.getProjectPulse forever, no visible error; fixed to `error === undefined`.

title: Raising Chromium's max-active-webgl-contexts without re-deriving the fleet-flip thresholds left two independently-tuned guards drifting — the terminal grid force-flipped to DOM with GPU headroom to spare
summary: environment.ts raised Chromium's max-active-webgl-contexts to RAM-tiered 24/28/32, but TerminalWebGLConfig.ts/resourceProfile.ts's DOM-flip thresholds stayed at the old 16-cap values, flipping the terminal grid to DOM at ~13 panes with GPU headroom free. Fix: webglContextBudget.ts single-sources switch + per-profile thresholds; RESOURCE_PROFILE_CONFIGS Omit-typed to block stale literals.

title: The dock preview's X routed "close" through trashPanelGroup(), so dismissing a floating preview silently armed a 20s TTL that killed the process behind it
summary: Dock preview's close button (usePanelHandlers.ts surface==="dock" branch) called trashPanelGroup() instead of the existing non-destructive closeDockTerminal() setter (terminalFocusSlice.ts), silently arming TerminalRegistry's 20s TRASH_TTL_MS (shared/config/trash.ts) auto-kill setTimeout with zero UI signal a clock started. Fix routes dock dismiss to closeDockTerminal before the trashedRef double-fire latch (DockedPanel survives collapse/reopen so ordering matters), keeps Alt+Click force-close via removePanel, and updates PanelHeader.tsx copy/aria-keyshortcuts ("Dismiss preview" vs "Close session"). Lesson: delayed-destruction traps hide behind innocuous-sounding actions (trash/park/archive) reused across surfaces with different destructive semantics; docs/architecture/destructive-action-safeguards.md's D0 "safe" label doesn't travel across call sites.

title: Version-monotonic release gate must treat new==live as a per-platform skip, not a failure — and the skip has to gate the verify steps too, or a non-reproducible re-tag rebuild false-fails one step later
summary: Release gate scripts/ci/check-version-monotonic.mjs failed re-tags of an already-published version identically to real downgrades, red-building platforms that had already shipped v0.26.0. Fix: tri-state outcome (new>live publish, new==live skip via exact string identity not semver.eq so build-metadata variants still fail closed, new<live fail), skip_upload output gates all four R2 upload+verify steps in .github/actions/publish-daintree/action.yml (not just upload) because re-tag rebuilds aren't byte-reproducible and unconditioned verify-r2-uploads.mjs/verify-r2-metadata.mjs would false-fail on sha512/Content-Length mismatch one step later; idempotent website-notify webhook stays ungated.

title: A UI pointer must share the scope of the data it indexes: global maximize fields against a worktree-scoped grid blanked the screen, and nothing detected the mismatch because existence-only validation can't see scope
summary: usePanelStore's maximizedId/maximizeTarget/preMaximizeLayout are flat globals; ContentGrid.tsx's worktree-scoped grid blanks when the trio points at another worktree's panel and lookup falls through to null. validateMaximizeTarget only detects deletion, not scope drift. Fix: maximizeByWorktree Map in worktreeStore.ts, atomic writes, pre-write resolveMaximizeForWorktree.

title: Tailwind core's delay-*/duration-* utilities compile to transition-delay/-duration, which tw-animate-css keyframe animations never read — the animation silently plays with zero stagger and no class-name test can catch it
summary: ContentGridEmptyState.tsx launcher stagger: Tailwind v4's delay-*/duration-* utilities compile to transition-delay/-duration, never read by tw-animate-css's animate-in/@keyframes animations, so a delay-* stagger fires every section at once with no class-name signal of failure; fix sets --tw-animation-delay/-duration directly plus fill-mode-backwards on non-zero delays.

title: Root-level animation:none for the theme wipe also kills the browser's default view-transition crossfade, and the manual replacement needs a monotonic intent counter — scheme-id equality can't detect a hover preview
summary: index.css animation:none on ::view-transition-old/new(root) disables the UA crossfade too, so runThemeCrossfade (appThemeViewTransition.ts) drives its own WAAPI opacity fade. A stale mutate callback's injectSchemeToDOM({immediate:true}) cancels a newer pending rAF write; fixed via themeIntentSeq (appThemeStore.ts) since selectedSchemeId misses hover previews.

title: A bare transition-opacity className silently replaces a cva's whole transition set under tailwind-merge (same conflict group, consumer wins), and motion-reduce:transition-none over-removes fades WCAG 2.3.3 never asked to remove
summary: ForgeStatPill.tsx/AppDialog.tsx reduced-motion arc: tailwind-merge treats a bare transition-opacity and Button cva's multi-property transition as one conflict group, so the consumer class replaces (not narrows) the cva's set, killing hover-tint/press-scale; fix spells out transition-[opacity,background-color,scale]. motion-reduce:transition-none also over-kills opacity, which WCAG 2.3.3 never required removed.

title: ProjectViewEvictionController's LRU pool treats every project view as equally safe to destroy, but destroying the Daintree Assistant's view kills its whole PTY process tree with no recovery — fixed with a hard floor, not the cheaper detach-instead-of-kill, because the MCP session pin is a deliberate security boundary
summary: ProjectViewEvictionController LRU-evicted a live Daintree Assistant WebContentsView, killing its PTY tree via revokeByWebContentsId -> gracefulKill -> ProcessTreeKiller (#11157). Fix: evictStaleViews hard-floors on getAssistantBackend binding + PtyClient.hasTerminal liveness; detach-instead-of-kill rejected (MCP pin is a security boundary, #7509).

title: A hook that never unmounts makes its module-level cache effectively permanent: useResolvedForgeProvider's resolutionCache needed every mutation source enumerated, not a lifecycle reset, and fs.watch's silent failures needed a stat-fingerprint backstop
summary: useResolvedForgeProvider's module-level resolutionCache (keyed by projectId) never invalidated on git-remote changes because the toolbar component lives in Daintree's persistent per-project view and never unmounts; combined with PullRequestService's #9997 sticky no-match cache, adding a git origin left forge PR pills hidden until reload. Fix (#11161/#11155) threads a narrow GitFileWatcher onGitConfigChanged signal through WorkspaceService (debounced getRemotes probe, signature diff, 5-min stat-fingerprint backstop for fs.watch's silent degradation) to a scoped sys:forge:remote-changed / forge-remote-changed event pair that invalidates only the affected project's cache entry, without widening sys:worktree:update and reopening #9997's 17k-spawn/day spin, and without letting remote URLs (which can carry credentials) cross the IPC bridge.

title: Option+Arrow word jump needed a rewrite, not a passthrough: xterm's CSI modifier arrows aren't bound by default shells, and the fix has to dodge alt-buffer TUIs and key-repeat ordering to work
summary: XtermAdapter.tsx attachCustomKeyEventHandler: macOptionIsMeta only rewrites character keys, not arrows, so Option+Left/Right emit xterm's CSI modifier sequences (\x1b[1;3D/C) which zsh ZLE and bash readline don't bind, leaving word-jump dead despite Option+B/F working via \x1bb/\x1bf. Fix (getOptionWordJumpSequence in terminalWordNavigation.ts) rewrites the raw KeyboardEvent to meta sequences, gated live per keypress on terminalInstanceService.getAltBufferState (so full-screen TUIs that decode CSI arrows themselves are untouched), resolved inside the event.repeat branch before chord/keybindingService resolution (so held keys keep firing without leaking into pending-chord state), and manually replicates notifyUserInput/stableOnInput since return false bypasses xterm's onData. Also corrects the framing: this matches iTerm2's opt-in Natural Text Editing preset, not either terminal's shipped default.

title: Writing focusedId paints the highlight but moves no DOM focus — and Chromium's moveBefore preserves focus into aria-hidden containers
summary: panelFocusRegistry/usePanelRootFocus/DockPanelOffscreenContainer: focusedId only paints a highlight — arrow nav, Cmd+1..9, focusNext/Previous, agent-state cycling, worktree restore wrote it without claiming DOM focus. moveBefore preserves focus into aria-hidden dock-parking containers on close. Fixed via usePanelRootFocus, blur-before-park, checking document.activeElement not isOpened.

title: A global type-anywhere rescue must commit the keystroke to state before consuming the event, and refuse rather than guess the target
summary: src/lib/typeAnywhere.ts + useTypeAnywhere: global capture-phase keydown listener routes stray printable keys into an agent draft, committing terminalInputStore.setDraftInput before preventDefault so a failed reveal/focus never loses the keystroke. resolveRescueTarget refuses ambiguous candidates rather than guessing; reads composedPath()[0] (shadow DOM), getModifierState('AltGraph') (AltGr layouts).

title: ActionService.dispatch() never rejects — .catch()/.finally()-only handling and fire-and-forget void dispatch silently swallow failures, and a caller-side fix is decorative if the action handler itself swallows its own error
summary: ActionService.dispatch() (src/services/ActionService.ts) always resolves ActionDispatchResult {ok:false,error} and never rejects; FilePane's .catch(), useDevPreviewNavigation's .finally(), and BrowserPane's void dispatch() + synchronous banner clear all silently swallowed failures (issue #11114). Root cause: idiomatic promise error-handling is dead code against a never-rejecting contract, app-wide per the PR's own scope note; worse, devPreviewActions.ts's promoteToPortal caught its own portal.create IPC error, rolled back, and returned normally, making dispatch report ok:true on a real failure -- any caller fix needed the handler to rethrow too. Fix idiom: await + branch on result.ok, attempt/generation refs (openAttemptRef, promoteAttemptRef, blockedNav.noticeId) to drop stale results, pane-local InlineStatusBanner (Tier 3, notification-system.md) not global toast, and timer callbacks that re-check ownership since clearTimeout can't cancel an already-queued callback.

title: checkForUpdatesAndNotify() silently double-notifies over our own in-app toast, invisible on unsigned dev builds because Electron 42 no-ops unsigned native notifications; one-shot UPDATE_* broadcasts also miss any renderer that mounts later, which per-project WebContentsView LRU eviction guarantees
summary: AutoUpdaterService.ts's checkForUpdatesAndNotify() duplicated the in-app toast useUpdateListener.tsx renders on update-downloaded; invisible in dev since Electron 42 no-ops unsigned notifications. One-shot UPDATE_* broadcasts miss renderers mounting after LRU eviction. Fix: checkForUpdates() plus getLatestUpdate() behind update:get-latest, pulled on mount with liveStateSeen guard.

title: registry.tsx types onClose as (force?: boolean) => void so Alt+Click can signal force — forwarding it bare into any child's onClick is invisible to tsc and swaps recoverable close for permanent delete
summary: registry.tsx types onClose (force?:boolean)=>void, backing handleClose's fork: removePanel (permanent) vs trashPanelGroup (recoverable). ReviewPane (#11138) forwarded it bare into ReviewHubContent's onClick={onClose} -- tsc-clean, yet the child's MouseEvent lands in force at runtime, swapping recoverable close for delete. Same hazard for any panel with its own close button.

title: The process-global 'current project' pointer is never a proxy for per-window identity — resolve from sender or union across windows, and null is an identity not a wildcard
summary: Multi-window IPC context resolution: electron/ipc/utils.ts typedHandleWithContext resolved ctx.projectId via the single-slot windowRef.ts ProjectViewManager global (last-created window wins) instead of webContentsRegistry's cross-window viewToProject map (getProjectForWebContents), so ~97 IPC handlers saw null projectId for any non-latest window, failing the terminal write guard open and help handlers closed. Same process-global-as-identity pattern (ProjectStore.getCurrentProjectId, a last-focused not last-window pointer) independently caused hibernation tearing down visible-but-unfocused windows (#11123), CopyTree leaking cross-window exclusion rules (#11125), project-switch layout corruption (#11127), notification state clobber (#11146), and stale File-menu gates (#11152). Fix pattern: resolve from sender identity or union active projects via collectActiveProjectIds, require exact null-inclusive equality in ownership gates, snapshot before any await. Precedent chain #5541/#6016/#8607.

title: A fail-open corruption probe (probeDb) is the wrong predicate for a destructive promotion — reuse it for backup-rename gating and a truncated candidate silently overwrites the only good backup
summary: DatabaseMaintenanceService reused fail-open probeDb() (safe for boot quarantine) to gate fs.renameSync backup promotion, letting a truncated sqlite.backup() copy silently overwrite the only good backup. Fix adds probeDbFile() tri-state (ok/corrupt/unknown) plus backupsSuspended, and fixes a deferredQuickCheckPending race via in-flight Promise tracking.

title: autoUpdater.quitAndInstall() on macOS skips before-quit entirely because Squirrel.Mac closes every window before app.quit() fires — before-quit-for-update can't gate it (no Event object), so the install call itself must be gated behind an extracted shutdown-chain runner
summary: shutdown.ts ran the graceful-shutdown chain (journaling, WAL checkpoint) only on before-quit. macOS quitAndInstall() lets Squirrel.Mac close windows before app.quit(), skipping it; before-quit-for-update has no Event to gate on. Fix: shutdownCoordinator.ts shares one cleaning/handoff chain between before-quit and AutoUpdaterService, backstopped by SHUTDOWN_DEADLINE_MS.

title: A bubbled keydown handler that calls preventDefault() on Enter cancels the focused button's native click activation — Enter on Cancel confirmed the dialog
summary: WebviewDialog.tsx keydown called preventDefault()+handleOk() on every bubbled Enter, cancelling the focused Cancel button's native click so the guest confirm/alert/prompt always confirmed (#11106); FleetArmingRibbon.tsx had it worse via capture-phase Enter dispatching fleet.kill/trash. Fix adds restoreFocusTo() + one-session focus capture in useWebviewDialog.ts.

title: Electron's askForMediaAccess is macOS-only, and a missing spawn() binary fails asynchronously - a synchronous try/catch around either one is a no-op
summary: voiceInput.ts requestMicPermission() returned false on Windows/Linux (askForMediaAccess is macOS-only); VoiceRecordingService.start() treated that as fatal mic_permission_denied, dead-ending Windows voice input. openMicSettings()'s Linux spawn(gnome-control-center) lacked child.on('error'); a missing binary's ENOENT crashed the app via globalErrorHandlers.ts's uncaughtException.

title: Hand-rolled pixel-to-column math must match FitAddon bug-for-bug — gutter, whole-pixel truncation, and dedup boundary all diverged, and the watchdog 'repaired' the drift 3s after paint
summary: TerminalResizeController hand-computes cols/rows instead of calling FitAddon.proposeDimensions() (DOM staleness), so its arithmetic must mirror FitAddon exactly. Three divergences: scrollbar gutter (15px) not reserved in calculateTerminalDimensions/xtermConfig.ts column math after 9cd995a9d set it without touching call sites; ResizeObserver fractional pixels divided raw vs FitAddon's parseInt whole-pixel truncation; resize() dedup `<1px` threshold swallowed sub-pixel deltas that cross a truncation boundary. TerminalReconciliationWatchdog (WATCHDOG_INTERVAL_MS=3000) treats FitAddon as ground truth and silently re-wraps the grid ~3s post-paint, corrupting cursor-relative inline TUIs (Assistant sidebar). Fix: TERMINAL_SCROLLBAR_WIDTH constant + getEffectiveScrollbarWidth() (mirrors FitAddon's scrollback/showScrollbar gating) + toFitPx() truncation + isRedundantResize() on truncated values. Companion #11098 extends with a strategy-aware resize coordinator.

title: Daintree's own memory-pressure mitigation was the incident: unbounded RAM-fraction thresholds plus a cooldown-free tier 1 cleared Chromium caches and forced GC in the visible renderer every 30s
summary: ProcessMemoryMonitor.ts/ResourceProfileService.ts derived memory-critical floors as an uncapped fraction of os.totalmem() (0.1/0.2), so 64GB Macs hit false critical pressure from ordinary file-cache use. Cooldown-free tier 1 cleared Chromium caches + forced GC in the visible renderer every 30s, misdiagnosed as a PTY stall. Fix: systemMemory.ts caps thresholds, adds a 5min tier-1 cooldown, resample rechecks system memory.

title: An optimistic cache write is worthless until every re-seed path is blocked: revalidate downgrades, backend TTL caches, broadcasts, and in-flight singleflight joins can all clobber it back
summary: forgeResourceCache.ts optimistic assign/unassign patch (patchIssueAssigneeCache) for the toolbar Issues dropdown kept getting clobbered: planWarmRevalidate in useGitHubResourceListSWR.ts downgrades revalidate to cached via count-fingerprint (assign doesn't move counts), stats broadcasts in useRepositoryStats.ts trust a fetchedAt stamped at push-build time not fetch time, ForgeStatsToolbarButton's cache-first hover prefetch joins a pre-assign in-flight singleflight request, and mutations.ts's assignIssueImpl/unassignIssueImpl invalidated nothing. Fix threads a stale boolean through all four consumers plus the paired unassign patch and new invalidateRepoIssueCachesForAssignment (GitHubCaches.ts). Lesson: enumerate every reader of a shared cache slot before trusting a single-site optimistic patch.

title: currentProject === null is overloaded for two different things, no workspace at all and a Scratch is active, so every feature gated on it silently broke inside a Scratch
summary: Scratch workspaces made `currentProject === null` ambiguous (main clears it on scratch switch), so every `if (!currentProject)` gate broke silently: assistant launch, empty-canvas routing, cwd fallback chains, terminal-kill via mutable PtyClient.activeProjectId, MRU cycle, branch-chip layout. Fix: resolveX(currentProject, currentScratch) project-first in workspaceCwd.ts/emptyCanvas.ts.

title: A palette's selection index must be derived from identity over the exact array it renders — a second, narrower filter (or an index instead of an id) strands the highlight off-screen and breaks aria-activedescendant
summary: useProjectSwitcherPalette.ts/ProjectSwitcherPalette.tsx (#11071): modal browse's displayResults filter diverged from the results array indexed by selectedIndex/aria-activedescendant/Enter, stranding the highlight off-screen (WAI-ARIA violation). Fix: hook-owned single results array, id-derived selectedIndex via findIndex, updater-resolved step(), plus nonActiveAgentCounts.

title: A one-shot repaint keyed on state that may not exist yet must become a durable, generation-stamped obligation — and a published id is not a paintability signal
summary: Assistant sidebar cold-open footer skipped its first paint: AppLayout's transitionend-triggered repaintAssistantAfterTransition read useHelpPanelStore terminalId and early-returned when null (session still provisioning), permanently dropping the sole geometry pass; a project switch-back masked it by supplying a working repaint elsewhere. Fixed in src/lib/sidebarToggle.ts via createAssistantRevealCoordinator: a durable pending/visible/generation obligation discharged on store subscription, gated on terminalInstanceService.waitForAttachSettled (terminalId publishes synchronously before the terminal attaches, so it is not readiness), driving the new shared src/services/terminal/revealUntilStable.ts double-confirm-paint loop. Distinguishes repaintForReveal vs revealTerminal semantics (isVisible WebGL gate #10671, missing-instance reporting) and guards drag-resize (isAssistantResizing) from being treated as a reveal.

title: Electron UtilityProcess.kill() can block main for ~2s on macOS, and installing a SIGTERM handler without exiting strands the child it should have killed
summary: workspace-host teardown (WorkspaceHostProcess.dispose backstop, electron/workspace-host.ts) froze Main for ~1s on 'Free memory' (#11069): child.kill() runs Chromium's base::EnsureProcessTerminated which blocks up to 2s on macOS, while the child's SIGTERM handler suppressed default terminate-on-SIGTERM without calling process.exit(), so it never died. Fix: idempotent shutdown() that actually exits via an unref'd deadline (ParentPort has no close()), plus a non-blocking raw process.kill(pid,'SIGKILL') backstop in the parent, cleared on cooperative exit. Same blocking child.kill() pattern remains in PtyHostLifecycle.ts, PluginDevWorkerHost.ts, AssistantHostProcess.ts as known follow-ups.

title: Never trust a persisted focus pointer as liveness — intersect it with what the dock actually renders before an enforcement effect trusts it
summary: useContentGridContext's maximized-tab-group focus enforcement (contentGridFocus.ts getMaximizedGroupFocusTarget) snapped focus back whenever focusedId sat outside the group, instantly closing dock popovers via setFocused clearing activeDockTerminalId (#11065). The obvious exemption — trust activeDockTerminalId as proof a popover is open — would be worse: DockPanelOffscreenContainer's keep-alive watchdog (#7278) deliberately keeps that pointer valid for panels no longer rendered (wrong worktree, trashed, moved to grid, help panel), so trusting it would permanently strand focus. Fix: new isDockPanelRendered predicate (dockPanelVisibility.ts) intersects the pointer with panelIds registration, dockable kind, docked location, untrashed, non-help, worktree scope; useContentGridContext derives openDockPopoverId via a Zustand selector (not useMemo, avoiding #8593 churn) returning a primitive id. Generalizes to: never treat a stored 'currently open X' pointer as liveness when other subsystems deliberately keep it alive past the referent's visibility.

title: framer-motion's layout="position" is a second, independent FLIP animator riding alongside dnd-kit — disabling dnd-kit's animateLayoutChanges does not disable it, and #6862 wired both uniformly across five sortable wrappers whose contexts want different reflow feel
summary: Dock chips FLIP-slid on drop (#11063) despite dnd-kit's animateLayoutChanges: () => false, because the wrapping m.div's framer-motion layout="position" is a second, independent FLIP animator the flag never touches. #6862 wired both onto all five sortable wrappers; #11066 fixes only the dock, leaving the trap live in GridPlaceholder/SortableWorktreeTerminal.

title: A module-level refcount guarding an abandonable MCP-dispatched RPC wedges forever once one side stops settling — replace it with per-dispatch TTL leases
summary: src/store/mcpSpawnFocusGuard.ts used a module-level depth counter (increment on dispatch start, decrement in finally) to drive focusPolicy preserve for indirect MCP-spawned panels. Main's rendererBridge.ts abandons a dispatch after MCP_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_MS (30s) without cancelling the renderer side, so a hung action handler's finally never fires, wedging the counter above zero for the life of that project's long-lived ProjectViewManager V8 context -- every later addPanel forces preserve, silently killing dock-popover auto-open in exactly one project until restart. Fixed via per-dispatch leases (Map keyed by nextLeaseId) with a 45s TTL (30s timeout + grace); expired leases stop suppressing and log the hung actionId once; late settles release only their own lease, avoiding underflow.

title: A grid-landing focus invariant ("never focus a panel the maximize state hides") has to be enforced at every path that sets focusedId, not just addPanel — and toggleMaximize's conditional unmaximize branch can silently re-maximize instead of exiting
summary: panelStore.addPanel/terminalFocusSlice.ts: panels created, restored, or moved while maximizedId was set landed focused but hidden behind the fullscreen cell (#11060). exitMaximize() now always clears maximize state; toggleMaximize's conditional unmaximize could silently re-maximize instead (live focusOrMaximizeByIndex bug). Applied to every focus-setting path with a panelsById liveness check.

title: A read-side filter (isDockPanel) enforced at render but not at write time strands state invisibly — guard every path that can commit location:"dock", and let the redirect double as the hydration rescue
summary: Daintree's content dock renders only panelKindIsDockable/isDockPanel kinds (shared/config/panelKindRegistry.ts, shared/types/panel.ts), but addPanel.ts, DndProvider.tsx drag-drop, DockLaunchMenuItems.tsx, and bulkMoveToDockByWorktree could all commit location:"dock" for any kind (#11054), stranding browser/plugin panels invisibly yet persisted, limit-counted, unreachable. Fix redirects dock->grid in addPanel before background/runtimeStatus derivation; since hydration replays through the same addPanel call, the write-guard also rescues already-stranded persisted panels with zero migration code. The redirect broke panelStore.ts's create-focus wrapper, which branched on requested options.location instead of committed panelsById[id].location — fixed by reading back committed state post-commit. Companion #11058 reused existing moveBefore/stable-wrapper DOM relocation (from file-panel precedent) to make browser panels dockable, incidentally preserving the Electron webview guest within one portal host, but grid<->dock still remounts across render hosts.

title: h-full inside a row that only sets min-height resolves to auto, not a clamp — drag-ghost overlays must match siblings' explicit h-[var(--token)], and shared 'compact mode' content isn't free just because a prop is passed
summary: ContentDock.tsx row sets only min-height, so DockPlaceholder.tsx's h-full drag-ghost resolved to auto, letting content set row height and grow the dock bar mid-drag (#11055). BrowserPlaceholder/DevPreviewPlaceholder skipped the compact content-hiding pattern Terminal/AgentPlaceholder used. Fix: explicit h-[var(--dock-item-height)] ghost, compact-gated body.

title: Agent restart resumed the wrong pane's conversation: resume-latest (`claude --continue`, `codex resume --last`) is nondeterministic across same-agent panes, and the fix requires deferring the resume/fresh choice until AFTER the kill
summary: restartTerminal (src/store/slices/panelRegistry/restart.ts) lacked the pane's own agentSessionId, so it fell to buildResumeLatestCommand (claude --continue / codex resume --last / gemini -r latest, from resumeLatestArgs in shared/config/agents/*.ts), which resolves to the CLI's most-recently-active session, not this pane's - with multiple same-agent panes (fleet broadcasting), restart could load another terminal's conversation. Fix: route restart's kill through gracefulKill (electron/ipc/handlers/terminal/lifecycle.ts) instead of bare kill to recover the captured live session id, deferring the resume/fresh command decision until after Promise.all([gracefulKill(id), buildRestartEnv(...)]) settles. Guards: discard capture on detectedAgentId mismatch, never degrade an unbuildable exact id to resume-latest, keep durableCommand transient-free, and allowResumeLatest:false (moveToNewWorktreeAndTransfer, #4773) discards the capture for fresh-launch intent.

title: completionSources schema turns per-agent discovery into pure declarative data an engine narrows structurally (zero engine change per new source) — extending it to Codex's undocumented Plugins/Apps required confirming the on-disk format against source AND a live install first, shipping zero code where none existed
summary: SlashCommandService.list()'s three hardcoded agentId branches became a declarative completionSources array on AgentConfig plus a generic CompletionDiscoveryEngine (electron/services/completions/). shared/types/completionSources.ts must stay pure data (no fs/regex/functions) because the renderer (HybridInputBar.tsx) reads the same array at runtime that Main's engine scans disk with. CompletionRegistryDiscovery reuses CompletionDirectoryDiscovery's shape so the engine needed zero new branch for Codex Plugins (#11051) — extension is free only when structurally narrow-able. Adding Plugins required confirming the on-disk format (config.toml + plugins/cache manifests) against codex-rs source AND a live v0.144.1 install; Apps got zero code because the format was confirmed to not exist locally. Companion #11056 fixed a global-vs-per-item autocomplete staleness bug (isResultsStale boolean → staleKeys Set).

title: Rate limiters keyed on mechanical action count punish legitimate batch fanout, and raising the burst just accrues token debt in the shared leaky bucket — admit a bounded batch as ONE slot instead
summary: Terminal spawn limiter (waitForBurstRateLimitSlot, electron/ipc/utils.ts) keeps nextAvailableMs across calls, so raising burst past 6 doesn't speed recipe fanout — repeat launches accrue debt. Fix: recipeStore.ts tags a fanout with spawnBatchId+spawnBatchSize; lifecycle.ts claimRecipeSpawnBatchAdmission claims ONE slot per batch, capped, 30s TTL. #11044 reused it for bulk worktrees.

title: The diff-review 'slow tokenize' wasn't in our highlighting or diff-match-patch — it was react-diff-view's own tree plumbing being quadratic, found only by profiling instead of assuming
summary: Diff review tokenize (runDiffTokenize, src/components/Worktree/diffTokenizer.ts) profiled at 414ms, but syntax highlighting (~7ms) and diff-match-patch (~22ms) were innocent; 92% lived in react-diff-view's own normalizeToLines (quadratic array-spread accumulator) and backToTree (per-node lodash deep-equal). Fixed via a linear reimplementation (diffTokenizePipeline.ts, tokenizeFast) that keeps the library's markEdits/pickRanges enhancers as the semantic seam, proven correct by a 10-case deep-equal parity suite (src/components/Worktree/__tests__/diffTokenizePipeline.test.ts). PERF-161 410ms->64ms (85% faster). Parallel finding in the same PR: actionPaletteSearch.ts's rankActionMatches hotspot was Intl.Collator.compare buried in the sort comparator's tiebreak, fixed with a cached positional rank array in a WeakMap guarded by an identity-snapshot staleness check.

title: A partial credential-store cutover leaves two live sources of truth — fix with a migration that persists into the new store AND deletes the old key, never a read-time fallback
summary: electron/services/migrations/024-backfill-github-forge-credential.ts: #10347's forge-neutral refactor moved the GitHub panel connection gate (forgeSettings.ts getCredentialStatus) to the provider-keyed forgeCredentials store, but GitHubAuth.getToken() and toolbar counts kept reading the legacy secureStorage userConfig.githubToken key, so panels showed 'not connected' while counts worked. Fix is a boot migration (schema v23→24) that backfills forgeCredentials and deletes the legacy key, not a read-time fallback, because PluginHostFactory.registerForgeProvider replays forgeCredentials into live provider impls via setCredentials() and utility-process hosts like workspace-host can't reach secureStorage. Also closes a second-order bug: forge:clear-credential never deleted the legacy key, so a cleared token would resurrect via initializeTokenStorage() on next boot. Migration guards the destination not the source and repairs corrupt sibling data instead of throwing to avoid tripping MigrationRunner's whole-chain restore-from-backup.

title: A diff cache/staleness key built from a coarse status enum misses continuous edits — derive freshness from a scalar summary of the live store, not the status field, and never silently refetch under the reader
summary: Daintree diff viewer (diffContentCache.ts, useDiffContent.ts, DiffPane.tsx) cached diffs by file status, which never changes under continuous agent edits, so open diffs went silently stale. selectDiffFreshnessKey adds a primitive status:mtimeMs:insertions:deletions key from the live worktree store, flipping a GitLab-style refresh banner instead of silent refetch.

title: Radix tooltips open on focus, dialogs move focus on open/close — the fix is one lifecycle hook plus a suppression window, not another per-component .finally(hide)
summary: AppDialog/AppPaletteDialog autofocus on open and restoreFocusTo the trigger on close; Radix Tooltip opens on focus too, so both transitions strand or spuriously reopen tooltips (FileChangeList row tooltip, the diff viewer's header tooltip — then FileViewerModal, since retired into a dialog-presented DiffPane panel) plus an identical ShortcutHint z-toast strand bug. Four components had grown separate isRestoringFocusRef/.finally(hide) patches before PR #11034 centralized fixing into tooltipDismissRegistry.ts (registerTooltipDismiss/dismissAllTooltips, 250ms TOOLTIP_FOCUS_SUPPRESS_MS cleared by pointerenter/pointermove) plus dialogOverlayDismissal.ts's clearDialogOverlays(), wired into AppDialog/AppPaletteDialog transitions, with dismissOnDialogTransition={false} opt-out for IssueBadge/PRBadge, and suppressShortcutHint:true set on the three palette-opening ActionDefinitions instead of more manual hide() calls.

title: Trailing-only debounces made the worktree sidebar feel slow when the real git work costs single-digit ms — a leading-edge flush claws back latency, and a cooldown gate that only sets a dirty flag strands events until the 90s safety net
summary: WorktreeMonitor/WorkspaceService/TopologyWatcher (workspace-host) used pure trailing debounces despite git-status costing 8.2ms; PR #11029 benchmarks (PERF-130-141) proved sidebar lag was timer wait, fixed via leading-edge flush plus armCooldownDrain() for a stranded cooldown-dirty-flag bug an old test masked.

title: O_NOFOLLOW closes the symlink-swap TOCTOU but not a type-swap to a FIFO — diffMedia's post-open fdStat + O_NONBLOCK closes a window the established files:read pattern (#6263) still leaves open
summary: electron/ipc/handlers/diffMedia.ts (readWorkingSide, PR #11028) claims 'same containment discipline as files:read' (#6263: realpath + O_NOFOLLOW open) but adds O_NONBLOCK plus a post-open fileHandle.stat() fd re-check that files.ts's handleRead still lacks. Mechanism: O_NOFOLLOW only rejects a symlink swapped into the final path component; a regular file swapped for a FIFO between the pre-open fs.stat() and fs.open() isn't a symlink, so O_NOFOLLOW is silent, and without O_NONBLOCK a blocking read-open of a FIFO hangs the open() call forever waiting for a writer. Consequence: electron/ipc/handlers/files.ts's handleRead (verified in current source) still has this exact hang window — no O_NONBLOCK, no fd-level stat before readFile(). Lesson: re-verify on the opened fd, not the pre-open path stat; treat 'same discipline as X' comments as claims to diff, not facts to inherit; backport diffMedia.ts's hardening into files.ts.

title: A background-drain hold keyed on a single lastActiveWheelId self-defeats the moment two terminals are wheel-active at once — each pane's gesture holds every other pane's redraws
summary: TerminalOutputIngestService's background-drain hold (24ms recheck, 250ms cap) exempted only the single terminal in TerminalBurstController's lastActiveWheelId scalar; wheel-scrolling several mouse-reporting TUIs at once made each pane evict the other's exemption, so concurrently-scrolled panes held each other's redraws (scroll-concurrent p99 161ms worst 244ms -> 64ms, flick settle 343ms -> 67ms after fix). Fixed by replacing the scalar with a Map (activeWheelAt) and splitting the query into hasActiveWheelGesture()/isWheelActive(id), mirrored in TerminalOutputIngestService as hasInteractionHold/isInteractionParticipant, shared with the pre-existing echo-pending hold. Caught only by PERF-127's scroll-concurrent Playwright benchmark (6 simultaneous TUIs), not scroll-fleet (1 TUI + 12 background terminals). General lesson: any 'lastActiveXId' single-slot tracker for a non-exclusive interaction is a latent concurrency bug.

title: overflow:clip is not a scroll container — switching AppLayout's row from overflow:hidden re-enabled flex min-height:auto and let intrinsic-height panel content blow out the whole grid
summary: AppLayout.tsx row + TwoPaneSplitLayout.tsx wrappers: PR #10694 swapped overflow:hidden for overflow:clip to stop focus scrollIntoView drift, but clip (unlike hidden) isn't a scroll container so flex min-height:auto never zeroes. File-viewer's intrinsic CodeMirror height inflated the row to 7446px in a 1662px window. Fix: explicit min-h-0 on overflow-clip items.

title: Keystroke-to-paint under output flood was a queueing problem, not a slow path — the fix holds/shrinks background freight instead of speeding anything up
summary: Terminal keystroke-to-paint under output flood was a queueing problem: interactivity-perf.spec.ts (PERF-120..122) proved pty-host echo stayed sub-ms. Fix shrinks background watermarks (shouldDeferDrain), flushes interactive PortBatcher chunks synchronously not setImmediate, adds a 150ms echo hold (getEchoPendingHoldId). p95 84->52ms, FPS 33->60. Same class as #10948, different layer.

title: Mechanical god-object splitting via getter-proxy host interfaces scales to 5000-line files with zero test changes, but white-box reflection tests into the exact fields you want to move are a hard veto, not a speed bump
summary: 13-PR god-object-split batch (#11010-#11022, 2026-07-08) uses getter-proxy Host interfaces, proven by tests-unchanged. #11019 reverted TerminalProcess.ts InThreadAnalysisHost: tests white-box cast into activityMonitor/getAgentOutputContentSnapshot, same wall #10920 hit earlier. #11022: dead-code-first + preserve-incident-ordering exceptions.

title: dnd-kit's MeasuringStrategy.Always turns a rect-based drop-position decision into a feedback loop, fixable only with hysteresis whose memory must be stored space-agnostically across two divergent index spaces
summary: dropResolution.ts resolveGridInsertionIndexFromRects flickered between grid-drop slots: MeasuringStrategy.Always reflows the DOM on placeholder insert, flipping the rect verdict each frame. Fixed via 8px hysteresis (GRID_INSERTION_HYSTERESIS_PX) memoized as {overId, after}, not an index, since group-space/terminal-space diverge on multi-panel tab groups.

title: Docked panel bodies are a separate React subtree from the dock chip that owns the drag handle — grid-level context providers never reach them without an explicit cross-portal bridge
summary: Dock: DockPanelOffscreenContainer portals DockedPanel bodies separately from SortableDockItem (both descendants of the container but disjoint branches), so DragHandleProvider set by SortableTerminal/SortableDockItem never reaches the portaled panel via useDragHandle/PanelHeader — fixed via dockPanelPortalContext.ts registerDragHandle id-keyed registry bridge gated on activeDockTerminalId, plus a useRef+useMemo getter-proxy to survive dnd-kit's per-frame listeners churn without re-rendering the container on every drag frame.

title: Stopping a self-relaunching agent terminal must close every revival path in one synchronous op — auto-relaunch, in-flight launch, and hibernate restore — or the stop undoes itself
summary: HelpSessionController.endSession() closes 3 revival paths: bumps _launchGen (abort in-flight launch), revokes via revokeHelpSession before removePanel PTY kill (#7522 race), sets _hasAutoLaunched (suppress auto-relaunch) — shared _teardownBoundSession also fixed launch({replaceExisting}) ordering; ProjectStatsService.isHelpTerminal() excludes assistant PTY from switcher counts.

title: A preventive comment in one file didn't stop the anti-pattern it warned about from shipping in another: React 19's ~300ms Suspense fallback throttle plus the 400ms animate-pulse-delayed gate stacked to ~700ms of static gray
summary: registry.tsx Suspense fallback= wired BrowserPaneSkeleton's animate-pulse-delayed (400ms), stacking with React 19's FALLBACK_THROTTLE_MS=300 for ~700ms static gray on first lazy panel open (#10984), despite PR #9040's preventive comment warning against exactly this. Fixed via animate-pulse-immediate plus kind-specific ReviewPaneSkeleton.

title: Tailwind @layer base theme overrides always lose to a plugin's own @layer utilities output — layer origin beats specificity, so the fix is to go unlayered, not more specific
summary: Markdown viewer (#10980) reused .prose-daintree inside src/index.css's shared @layer base block to remap @tailwindcss/typography's --tw-prose-* tokens; the plugin emits .prose into @layer utilities, which always beats @layer base regardless of selector specificity, so dark mode rendered light-theme colors. #10982 fixed it not by raising specificity but by deleting the block and moving identical remaps into an unlayered src/components/Markdown/MarkdownDocument.css imported directly by MarkdownDocument.tsx (unlayered beats every named layer), plus an E2E resolved-color assertion in e2e/full/panels/core-file-panel.spec.ts guarding against a future re-layer regression. Mechanism: CSS cascade layer origin overrides specificity/order unconditionally; check plugin layer membership before writing theme overrides.

title: CDP memory purge on Electron 42/Chromium 148: `Memory.forciblyPurgeJavaScriptMemory` SIGSEGVs a throttled hidden WebContentsView, and macOS GPU purgeable memory noise (~1GB swing) makes aggregate footprint useless for A/B — use `simulatePressureNotification`+`collectGarbage` and per-process-class metrics instead
summary: webContentsLifecycle.ts purgeMemoryWebContents (#10981): CDP Memory.forciblyPurgeJavaScriptMemory SIGSEGVs a throttled hidden WebContentsView on Electron 42/Chromium 148 -- use simulatePressureNotification(critical)+collectGarbage. macOS GPU purgeable memory swings memory-kitchen-sink.spec.ts appFootprintKb ~1GB between runs -- use per-ProcessClass footprintByClass/rssByClass.

title: macOS only routes Dock/Finder folder drops to apps that declare a public.folder CFBundleDocumentTypes entry, and Launch Services registers that entry only from a signed packaged build — the routing itself is undev-testable
summary: electron-builder.config.cjs mac.extendInfo.CFBundleDocumentTypes/fileAssociations gating: macOS Launch Services won't route Dock/Finder folder drops (Dock icon won't even highlight) unless the app declares the public.folder UTI, and only reads that declaration from a signed packaged bundle — npm run dev can never exercise the routing. Fix (#10979, building on #9293/#8035) gates the new public.folder Viewer/Alternate entry behind CSC_LINK alongside the existing .dntr fileAssociations (electron-builder merges both into one CFBundleDocumentTypes array), and environment.ts's open-file handler must fs.statSync().isDirectory() branch folders away from the .dntr plugin-install path before any consumer runs; openDirHandler.ts serializes opens through one promise chain to avoid project-focus races.

title: A monotonic 'last polled' timestamp inside a Zustand snapshot-equality check turned every no-op git poll into a whole-app re-render — fix: side-map the stamp, gate always-mounted hooks' selectors on visibility with stable empty sentinels
summary: createWorktreeStore.ts's snapshotsEqual() compared WorktreeSnapshot.lastGitStatusCheckedAt, a field the workspace host advances on every completed git poll including no-op ones, forcing a fresh worktrees Map identity per tick and re-rendering all whole-map subscribers (App included) — ~1,385 components at 50 worktrees for a poll that changed nothing. Fixed by moving the stamp into a side map (statusCheckedAt) read only by per-id freshness consumers, plus open-gating always-mounted palette/context hooks (useWorktrees({enabled}), usePanelPalette, useQuickSwitcher, useSendToAgentPalette, useResumeSessionsPalette, useContextInjection, useAccessibilityAnnouncements) behind visibility using module-level stable empty Map/array sentinels instead of inline literals. Includes a reusable render-fanout-probe benchmark (scripts/perf/render-fanout-probe.js, DAINTREE_RENDER_PROBE=1) that walks React's fiber tree via a DevTools hook to attribute per-component render counts.

title: Mirroring user content into an agent-writable directory needs per-segment lstat + Windows-aware traversal checks — and Daintree already had a different symlink-containment primitive it didn't reuse
summary: AssistantContentMirror.syncAssistantContent (electron/services/AssistantContentMirror.ts) mirrors ~/.daintree/assistant and <project>/.daintree/assistant into the help-session dir Codex/Copilot write back into. isUnderMirrorRoot rejects relpath segments with backslash/colon since Windows path.resolve treats backslash as a separator, letting '..\..' smuggle traversal past a POSIX-only '/'-segment check; verifyRealDirChain lstats every existing directory component before delete/copy to catch a symlink planted mid-sync. Tests: backslash-traversal rejection, symlinked .claude/skills escape. Daintree already had realpath+relative containment at three prior call sites (files.ts PR #6263, pathGuard.ts, pluginFsContainment.ts) unreused here — a fourth, differently-shaped technique now coexists.

title: Merging rolldown boot chunks to cut app:// requests exposed a latent module-eval-order bug — a singleton's constructor read an import before that module had run; strictExecutionOrder is the fix, not touching the singleton
summary: PR #10970 merged Rolldown boot chunks (vite.config.ts boot codeSplitting group, 80 to 21 entry-eager) to cut app:// requests, but reordering module eval broke KeybindingService: its eager singleton (KeybindingService.ts:723) read DEFAULT_KEYBINDINGS before that module ran. Fixed via strictExecutionOrder:true, not the singleton.

title: webContents.isDestroyed() is not a valid guard for postMessage — a reloading frame can dispose before its WebContents does, and the fix must NOT close the still-wired port
summary: electron/window/portDistribution.ts distributePortsToView threw a WebFrameMain-disposed error from webContents.postMessage despite isDestroyed() guards, aborting PtyClient setPortRefreshCallback recovery in perWindowInit.ts. Fix: try/catch per postMessage -- leave window ports wired, release worker ports -- plus per-window catch in the loop.

title: Windowing raw terminal output to the last N lines before ANSI-stripping desyncs from the visible text whenever an OSC payload embeds a literal newline
summary: AgentPatternDetector.detect(), the 30ms ActivityMonitor pattern scan, windows raw output via lastLinesOffset() before stripAnsi(). OSC payloads can embed newlines, so the window lands inside one, dropping the working-indicator line and missing an agent-state transition. Fixed via desync detection + widen-and-rewindow fallback.

title: Sibling WebContentsViews only give you separate GPU-context/atlas budgets if you force a separate renderer process — same-origin views silently consolidate with no error
summary: electron/window/SurfaceViewManager.ts (paint-fabric Phase 1V, #10966/#10954-10967 arc): hosting aux terminal-render surfaces as sibling WebContentsViews only isolates the 16-WebGL-context cap and glyph atlas if each view gets a unique non-persist session partition (surfaceViewPartition, nonce'd per creation) — same-origin views on a shared session get silently consolidated by Chromium into one renderer process, with zero error, quietly re-merging the budgets the split was meant to separate. Also documents Electron 42 sibling-only attach (never nested, electron#47990), no per-pixel input pass-through across stacked views (electron#49039, geometry must be disjoint), and tiered crash recovery (reload once, then crash-loop -> retireSurface after 3 crashes/60s).

title: Electron 42 never fires visibilitychange/resume on a detached setVisible(false) WebContentsView reattach — any renderer wake logic gated on those events silently stalls to its hard timeout
summary: ProjectViewManager caches per-project WebContentsViews; warm switches detach+setVisible(false) then reattach behind an anti-flash bridge, gated by a warm paint gate (notifyWarmViewPainted, 500ms/1500ms soft/hard timeout) that releases once WorktreeStoreContext's scheduleWake terminal-wake fan-out confirms repaint. In Electron 42 that detach/reattach never fires visibilitychange or resume (visibilityState stays 'visible'), so scheduleWake never triggered and every warm switch stalled to the 1500ms hard timeout (measured 1502-1506ms, 14 hard-timeouts in e2e). Fix: main sends an explicit APP_VIEW_WARM_ACTIVATED IPC event at reattach, renderer's onViewWarmActivated routes into scheduleWake as a primary trigger with visibility/resume kept as fallback (66-200ms after). Also documents the WorkspaceHostPool windowLoadSeq / windowSwitchEpochs 'last-requested-wins' guards needed when the concurrent worktree-load change this PR made introduced stale-write races on windowToProject.

title: Tailwind v4 translate/scale utilities emit standalone `translate`/`scale` CSS properties, not `transform` — an arbitrary `transition-[opacity,transform]` list silently drops the motion and only the fade plays
summary: Nine Daintree overlay surfaces (AppDialog, AppPaletteDialog, ActionPalette chip, fixed-dropdown, ScrollPill, notification pill, ReEntrySummary, GeneralTab chevron, GettingStartedChecklist) used arbitrary transition-[opacity,transform] lists alongside translate-y-*/scale-* utilities. Since Tailwind v4 splits transform into standalone translate/scale/rotate properties, translate-*/scale-* utilities never write to `transform`, so it matched nothing and the rise/zoom motion snapped instantly while opacity still faded — zero errors, zero lint signal, months of silent regression. Fix: name translate/scale explicitly in arbitrary lists; the named transition-transform utility is safe (v4 expands it to cover all four props); motion-reduce neutralizers need translate-none/scale-none, not just transform-none. Documented in docs/themes/interaction-state-recipes.md.

title: xterm's SerializeAddon only encodes state that differs from a DEFAULT terminal — repainting a mirror from raw snapshots leaks stale VT modes across ticks, and RIS can't be the reset because it also clears synchronized-output mode 2026
summary: src/services/terminal/workerParse/mirrorApply.ts + parseAuthority.ts (paint-fabric Phase 4 worker-parse, PR #10962/#10967): a headless-xterm ParseAuthority's SerializeAddon snapshot only encodes non-default state, so applying it raw onto a mirror terminal leaks stale alt-screen/bracketed-paste/mouse-tracking modes across repaint ticks; RIS (ESC c) can't be the fix because it also resets DEC synchronized-output mode 2026, breaking the atomic repaint bracket and flashing a blank frame. Fix is a narrow DECSTR-plus-explicit-mode-disable reset sent as one write() inside the 2026 bracket (MIRROR_RESET in mirrorApply.ts); also notes the ack-boundary-must-move-with-the-bytes rule from #10967 that avoids repeating the disabled SharedArrayBuffer ingest path's drop bug.

title: Hidden project views let xterm's ingest queue grow unbounded (Chromium throttles the parse-pump timer); reveal-time resize then flushSync's the whole backlog in one synchronous task, wedging the renderer for a minute
summary: TerminalResizeController + TerminalOutputIngestService: hidden WebContentsView throttles xterm's setTimeout parse pump while MessagePort output keeps queuing unbounded; on reveal, applyResize/commitResize force-flushes past the 128KB watermark then xterm's CoreTerminal.resize() runs WriteBuffer.flushSync() synchronously over the whole backlog, freezing the renderer 45-60s while pty-host/main stay healthy (misleading signal) and MCP calls through the active view stall in lockstep. Fixed via RESIZE_FLUSH_SYNC_BUDGET_BYTES (1MB, resizeFlushBudget.ts): over budget, skip flush, do NOT resetForTerminal, resume incremental drain instead. #10983 added PERF-112 regression guard reconstructing the incident.

title: workspace-host had two fail-silent watchers: a stat pre-check that only sees 4 .git metadata files never notices unstaged edits, and a topology watcher that no-ops on a missing dir was never re-armed
summary: workspace-host/WorktreeMonitor's 300s poll fallback statted only index/HEAD/refs/packed-refs before skipping git status, so unstaged agent edits in background worktrees (git-only watcher, no recursive fs watch) never triggered a real check; fixed via FULL_STATUS_MAX_AGE_MS=120000 staleness ceiling in StatPrecheck.ts. Separately WorkspaceService.startTopologyWatcher() no-op'd when .git/worktrees/ was absent (zero-worktree state) with no re-arm, so the first external git worktree add fell back to a 90s safety reconcile; fixed via a non-persistent fs.watch sentinel (armMetadataSentinel) plus ensureAlive() self-heal, now both in TopologyWatcher.ts. PR also wired agent activity into the focus-only elevation tier (isElevated = isCurrent || agentActive).

title: process.memoryUsage() only sees the calling isolate: moving headless mirror buffers into worker_threads (#10920) silently blinded the pty-host ResourceGovernor to their memory, recreating the heap-vs-external blindness #9905 already fixed one layer down
summary: ResourceGovernor.ts trim/pause gate reads isolate-scoped process.memoryUsage(); #10920's AnalysisWorkerPool worker_threads for mirror analysis were invisible to it — utilization read 1.9% vs true 26.3% (8 terminals), no trim/pause. #10953: workers self-report memory-sample folded into combinedMb/maxWorkerHeapMb; trims ranked by real bufferLines. Same blindness as #9905, one isolate up.

title: Terminal ids are reused across kill/respawn, so existence checks can't detect staleness — cross-process async completions need a monotonic generation ledger with two different validation regimes
summary: electron/pty-host, main (PtyClient.ts, PtyManager.ts), and renderer (addPanel.ts) share terminalId across kill/respawn/host-crash-respawn/shard-migration incarnations; async completions (spawn-result, exit, buffered resize, journal write, hydration snapshot) keyed only by id could land on the wrong incarnation. Fix: shared/utils/agentLifecycleLedger.ts's AgentTerminalLifecycleLedger, one instance per process, tracks a monotonic launchGeneration minted by main and adopted downstream. Live-state ops (resize/restore/attach) validate via withCurrent (current generation only); terminal-final ops (close/journal) validate via withGenerationMark (exactly-once per generation, past generations tolerated) — a reserve-before-write pattern (recordJournal/rescindJournal) needing explicit rollback on failure. Consolidates prior one-off fixes (#10811, #10905, #10927, #10940) into one mechanism.

title: waitingReason sat fully classified and typed on the backend for 3.5 months, invisible in the UI the whole time — Daintree's terminal snapshot/reconnect/hydration chain hand-enumerates fields at every hop with no spread-through, so an unlisted field is dropped silently and no type error ever fires
summary: electron/ipc/handlers/terminal/snapshots.ts builds 5 separate hand-listed snapshot object literals (no shared serializer); shared/types/ipc/terminal.ts's BackendTerminalInfo/TerminalReconnectResult omitted waitingReason so TS never flagged the drop; src/utils/stateHydration/statePatcher.ts (3 restore fns) and src/store/slices/panelRegistry/addPanel.ts (2 reconnect-merge branches) each needed the same agentState==='waiting' gate. AgentStateService/PtyClient had classified waitingReason since fb917ed10 (2026-03-20) but it never reached the UI until PR #10949 threaded it through every hop 3.5 months later. Lesson: a field typed away at a non-spreading IPC/hydration boundary produces zero build error, only a UI gap that looks like a missing feature.

title: State-aware pty-host buffer reclaim that exempts foreground terminals self-defeats on the fixed 512MB heap budget: the exempted buffers ARE the pressure, so it escalates straight to the global PTY pause
summary: #10948's state-aware retention tiers made the pty-host `ResourceGovernor` pre-pause reclaim exempt foreground terminals (`.filter(s => s.tier !== "foreground")`), but on the default (non-fabric) path the pty-host runs on a fixed 512MB V8 heap budget (`resolveHeapBudgetMb()`, not scaled to system RAM unless `DAINTREE_PTY_FABRIC` is enabled, which instead scales each shard's budget with RAM), so the visible active agent terminals filling that budget were exactly the buffers it refused to reclaim; it freed almost nothing, utilization climbed to the pause threshold, and it escalated to the global PTY pause that suspends terminal output for up to 10s. Trims the headless analysis mirror, not the renderer scrollback. Reverted whole rather than patched because the flaw is the PR's core premise. Symptom: intermittent multi-agent stalls under memory pressure, reproduced even on a 64GB machine.

title: Debounced async autocomplete needs two independent staleness guards, not one: a requestId race guard stops out-of-order writes, but only a query+cwd stamp stops Enter/Tab from accepting results that are correctly-ordered yet stale
summary: useFileAutocomplete.ts (@file provider, HybridInputBar.tsx/useEditorKeymap.ts): requestIdRef stops out-of-order responses but not debounce-lag staleness. Fix stamps results with {cwd,query} so cross-worktree same-text queries stay stale too; Enter falls through, Tab no-ops, AutocompleteMenu.tsx dims via isRowStale. Later widened to per-item staleItemKeys (#11043).

title: Assistant CLI banners duplicated because the shared 80x24 spawn default was masked everywhere except the one panel that mounts before spawnStatus is ready, and reveal reconcile re-wrapped scrollback the CLI was still painting
summary: addPanel.ts hardcodes PTY spawn at 80x24; only the eagerAttach Assistant overlay mounts XtermAdapter before spawnStatus=ready, racing terminalClient.spawn() against the unregistered pty-host terminal. reconcileGeometryFresh re-wraps still-streaming CLI scrollback, duplicating the startup banner. Fixed via live-grid spawn dims plus a shared quiescence gate.

title: A rename migration without dedup, plus a merge path that re-inserts legacy ids, compounds duplicate array entries forever across dev-profile builds
