summary: toolbarPreferencesStore.ts: v10 renameForgeStats migration (added by #10347's forge-neutral rename) renames github-stats to forge-stats via plain .map() with no dedup, unlike v3 renameAgentSetup's Array.from(new Set(...)) precedent. mergeButtonList re-inserts ids missing from the persisted list, so a stale dev build hydrating the shared daintree-dev profile reinserts the legacy id, which the next develop build renames into another forge-stats copy. Toolbar.tsx renders one pill per array entry with no dedup, so N duplicate ids became N stacked forge-stats pill groups in dev mode only (production's per-release profile never triggers the old-schema writer). Fix layers sanitizeButtonList dedup in merge(), a one-time v11 migration, and render-boundary dedup in effectiveLeftButtons/effectiveRightButtons. Likely the true cause of #10806's previously-diagnosed orphaned-WebContentsView theory.

title: Deferred PTY output must settle its backpressure ledger exactly once, on replay — acking it at defer time too double-debits the pending-ack FIFO and every future pause degrades to the 10s safety timeout
summary: TerminalWriteController double-acked deferred restore output (defer time + replay), stealing pending-ack FIFO entries from later chunks and permanently inflating the pty-host queued-byte ledger, so every subsequent backpressure pause rode out the full 10s IPC_MAX_PAUSE_MS timeout instead of resuming on ack. Fixed via {data,chunkCount} replay-once entries plus three sibling bugs: aggregate-watermark resume sweep only firing on acks (not timeout/teardown drains) in portQueue.ts/ipcQueue.ts, and disconnectWindow iterating getPausedTerminalIds() after resumeAll() had already cleared the map. Surfaced by a new real-component integration stress test.

title: Electron 41's destroyed-view webContents getter returns undefined (electron#50249) — unguarded reads and teardown outside switchChain strand ProjectViewManager entries and resurrect dead views as cache hits
summary: ProjectViewManager (electron/window/, ProjectViewLifecycleController.ts, ProjectViewSwitchController.ts): Electron 41 destroyed-view .webContents getter returns undefined (electron#50249) unguarded, stranding cleanupEntry mid-teardown; destroyView races outside switchChain, resurrecting dead views as cache hits; a throwing fan-out consumer skips all ResourceProfileService pushes.

title: Panel state resolved at spawn time (launch env, titleMode) is silently dropped by the snapshot->statePatcher->backend gauntlet unless wired at every layer, and the base-layer guard against this is a code comment, not a compile check
summary: Two panel-persistence bugs (#10927 launch env / issue #10922 Z.AI provider lost on restart; #10929 titleMode / issue #10738 preset-branded titles reverting) share one mechanism: a new field on PtyPanelData/PanelSnapshot must cross panelToSnapshot or serializer.ts, statePatcher.ts's SavedTerminalData and every buildArgsFor* (buildArgsForBackendTerminal, buildArgsForReconnectedFallback, buildArgsForRespawn, buildArgsForNonPtyRecreation), the spawn options type, and the pty-host's terminalInfo.ts mapTerminalInfo/snapshot handlers — missing any one hop silently drops the field. titleMode was dropped at four points including a self-canceling ternary (options.title ? "default" : "default") in TerminalProcess.ts. registry.fieldcoverage.test.ts's PTY_FIELD_CLASSIFICATION now compile-checks per-kind fields via satisfies Record<keyof T, boolean>, but panelPersistence.ts's BASE_PANEL_FIELDS only catches deletions, not additions — an open, self-documented gap. Also: persisting resolved env (not a preset id) required re-checking excludeFromPersistence/removeOnExit to avoid a secret leak.

title: Interactive git recovery buttons on an agent-shared surface self-defeat: a second process collides with the agent's live op, or gates on status frozen for the same op — passive indicator only
summary: WorktreeCard/WorktreeHeader.tsx dropped BlockingOpRow Continue/Abort buttons (added for issue #10715): agents run rebase/merge in their own PTY, so card-fired abortRepositoryOperation/continueRepositoryOperation IPC races the agent, or gates on data GitStatusPass freezes mid-op (index.lock safety). Kept the passive gitStateIndicator badge; ConflictPanel.tsx untouched.

title: Electron 37+ crashes on worker_thread spawn/terminate cycling, so pools must be persistent — which forces generation-stamped state everywhere and leaves process.memoryUsage() blind to worker heap
summary: PR #10920 moved pty-host analysis, SQLite maintenance, and copytree work into persistent worker_thread pools (AnalysisWorkerPool, DbWorkerClient) since Electron 37+ crashes on spawn/terminate cycling. Respawns need generation stamps (spawnedAt, feedEpoch). #10953: process.memoryUsage() is isolate-scoped, blinding ResourceGovernor until self-sampling.

title: xterm's WriteBuffer only yields BETWEEN write() entries, never within one: coalesced 256KB writes and per-instance headless mirrors both create atomic multi-ms parse tasks that queue-priority fixes (#10884/#10886) can't preempt
summary: Multi-agent scroll lockup was CPU saturation, not backpressure (pill never showed). xterm's WriteBuffer 12ms parse budget yields only between write() calls: 256KB coalesced writes and headless mirrors created atomic parse tasks #10884/#10886 could not preempt. Fix: 32KB write slicing, HeadlessMirrorScheduler cap, eventLoopMonitor p99 tile.

title: Passive agent-detection heuristics fail open by default: a stale probe read, an agent's own composer glyph, and an unguarded scrollback rewrite each independently flapped Codex identity and destroyed its scrollback
summary: IdentityWatcher/ProcessDetector agent detection flapped Codex 0.142.5 detected<->plain and destroyed xterm scrollback via four fail-open defects: null foreground-probe read mapped to shellIdle:true unconditionally (fixed with latched sawForegroundSnapshot fail-closed-once-proven flag), DECORATED_SHELL_PROMPT_PATTERN glyphs matched Codex's own composer echo (fixed with state-gated DECORATED_SHELL_PROMPT_PATTERN_NO_AGENT_GLYPHS), typed/aliased agents lacked isLaunchAnchored so tree-absence off-streaks demoted them (fixed via setLaunchAnchored on process_tree evidence), and restoreScrollback lacked reduceScrollback's focus/selection/cooldown guards so xterm's Buffer.resize trimStart destroyed history on every flap. Sibling PR #10928 fixed the same asymmetric-gate pattern: ActivityMonitor's content-delta heuristic missed isRecentUserInput at one of 9 promotion sites, letting mouse-report-driven TUI redraws flip idle to working.

title: An rAF-batched Zustand store that replaces its whole map reference every flush turns any always-mounted whole-map subscriber into an O(worktrees)/O(panels) recompute at up to 60Hz
summary: panelStatusBuffer.ts rAF-batches terminal status writes into one setState/frame but replaces panelsById's whole map reference each flush; SidebarContent, ContentDock, DndProvider subscribed to that reference, causing O(worktrees)/O(panels) recomputes at 60Hz while any agent streams (#10908). Fixed via narrow useShallow selectors, id-signatures, getState() snapshots.

title: Layering a backoff/override on an existing rate-request API breaks its same-value no-op guard: diff against the last requested value, not the live applied one, or you silently drop re-requests made while the override is active — the identical bug already hit hibernation tiering in #8998
summary: ActivityMonitor.setPollingInterval's no-op guard diffed against POLLING_INTERVAL_MS (live cadence), which idle-backoff also mutates — naive port drops tier re-requests mid-backoff. Fix splits requestedPollingIntervalMs so guard/wake path diff against what was asked. Same shape broke TerminalHibernationManager in #8998, also covers SessionSnapshotter epoch/throttle ordering.

title: ProjectStore.getAllProjects() took a write-locking IMMEDIATE transaction on every call just to self-heal status — gate the transaction on whether anything actually changed, and know SQLite can reverse-scan an ASC index to serve a DESC ORDER BY
summary: electron/services/ProjectStore.ts getAllProjects(), hit by periodic services plus menu/startup/IPC, opened a write-locking IMMEDIATE transaction every call to self-heal status drift, even when nothing was dirty. Fixed via check-then-transact. Migration 0006 ASC index gets reverse-scanned for a DESC ORDER BY; agentSessionHistory cache returns arrays by reference.

title: A per-process write queue cannot fix a cross-process file race: agentSessionHistory.ts's module-scope writeQueue serialized writes within main and within pty-host separately, so the two processes still clobbered each other's resume records
summary: agentSessionHistory.ts writeQueue (#10856) is module-scope, serializing writes only within one process; main and pty-host each hold an independent copy, so concurrent close writes to agent-session-history.json clobber each other at quit. #10905: main becomes sole writer via PtyHostEvent bridge; also fixes #10865 bogus No-worktree grouping via inferWorktreeIdFromCwd.

title: Plugin manifest schema fields validate without proof they're consumed — a .shape-sweep + satisfies-typed field→consumer contract test is the only thing that catches an orphan field, and it already found two
summary: electron/schemas/plugin.ts contributes.* zod schemas validate shape, not usage (#10888). manifestContributionConsumers.test.ts pairs a satisfies-typed field-consumer map with a runtime .shape sweep; it found ViewContributionSchema name/description had zero consumers and PR #10901 deleted them from schema, SDK templates, sample plugin, and tests.

title: Electron's utilityProcess.fork silently ignores Node's --permission/--allow-* execArgv flags — process.permission stays undefined and nothing is blocked, because Electron's utility-process bootstrap never runs Node's --permission CLI parsing
summary: utilityProcess.fork never runs Node's --permission CLI parsing, so pluginPermissionFlags.ts execArgv mapping (--permission/--allow-fs-*/--allow-child-process) in PluginService.activateViaWorker is silently inert on Electron 42.4.0 -- process.permission undefined, calls unblocked. Real boundary stays pluginFsContainment.ts; affects every utilityProcess.fork host, not just plugins.

title: activatePlugin's completion handlers guarded staleness with `plugins.has(id)` (presence) instead of identity — indistinguishable from a fresh reload under the same key, only reachable once user-plugin activation crossed a process boundary
summary: PluginService.activatePlugin cached results by plugin id in a Map (activationPromises) and Set (activatedPlugins); handlers checked presence (plugins.has(id)) not identity, so a stale gen-1 activation could mark a reloaded generation already-activated, skipping its real worker-fork. Fixed via identity compare; inert under #9304, reachable once #10526 added cross-process latency.

title: tsup's dts bundler mangles z.ZodType<T> into invalid syntax unless zod is external, so the plugin-sdk API-surface guard snapshots tsup's own dist output instead of standing up a parallel api-extractor pipeline that would retrigger the bug
summary: packages/plugin-sdk/tsup.config.ts keeps zod in tsup's `external` array because rollup-plugin-dts (tsup's dts bundler) inlines zod's CJS runtime and mangles public `z.ZodType<T>` exports (PluginChannelSchema in shared/types/plugin.ts) into invalid `undefined<T>` syntax with no build error. The same bundler injects a deprecated baseUrl tripping TS5101, worked around via `ignoreDeprecations: "6.0"` scoped to dts.compilerOptions only (mirrored independently in packages/daintree-plugin/tsup.config.ts). #10897's scripts/ci/check-api-surface.mjs snapshots tsup's actual shipped dist/index.d.ts and dist/react.d.ts bytes into packages/plugin-sdk/api-report/, wired as check:api-surface in npm run check, rather than adopting @microsoft/api-extractor — which lacks native dual-entry-point support and would reintroduce the same rollup-plugin-dts quirks via a second declaration pipeline.

title: Zustand-to-IPC persist subscribers must not let one variable serve as both the in-flight lock and the pending payload — actionMruStore.ts did, and a usage write landing mid-save silently vanished, invisible until Cmd+K's new HUD made writes fire on every keystroke
summary: Cmd+K leader-key-to-persistent-HUD rewrite raised ActionService.dispatch/actionMruStore.ts call frequency, exposing: Zod safeParse(undefined) failing on all-optional argsSchema (terminal.kill), and actionMruStore.ts reusing one variable (pendingPersist) as both in-flight lock and payload, silently dropping IPC persist writes that land mid-save.

title: Terminal-grid flicker was three interacting causes: a scroll-mode boolean missing the column boundary's hysteresis, a self-referential padding edge on the observed element, and a contentRect-vs-clientWidth mismatch — a follow-up then safely relaxed the belt-and-suspenders layer once one fix proved sufficient
summary: Terminal grid (useContentGridContext.tsx, ContentGridDefault.tsx, terminalLayout.ts) flickered (#10871): isScrollMode lacked hysteresis, toggled padding its own ResizeObserver measured, and mismatched contentRect vs clientWidth. Fixed via gridRowsOverflowWithHysteresis + unified clientWidth; #10898 dropped the redundant gutter; #10912 added a watchdog breaker.

title: MCP action `resultSchema`/`mcpOutputSchema` is manifest documentation only — nothing parses or strips the real `run()` return, so a schema narrower than the true data still leaks every field over MCP
summary: ActionService.ts resultSchema/mcpOutputSchema is manifest-only for MCP's advertised outputSchema; dispatch()/tierAuth.ts buildStructuredContent never validates run()'s return against it. #10864 agentSessionHistory.list leaked its snapshot field despite a narrower schema; #10870 hand-stripped it. Trap persists for any mcpOutputSchema action.

title: Reveal-repaint must have exactly one owner per terminal: a second, independently-timed reconcileGeometryFresh pass races xterm's non-reentrant reflow and corrupts committed scrollback
summary: Daintree Assistant duplicated/garbled main-buffer CLI output on view reveal because HelpPanel.tsx ran its own local reveal cascade (#10362-lineage 8-frame width poll + 1s/3s backstops) alongside the shared wakeActiveWorktreeTerminals.ts sweep that already owned it via collectActiveWorktreeTerminalTargets. Two independent calls to TerminalResizeController.reconcileGeometryFresh raced xterm 6.x's non-reentrant buffer reflow, corrupting isWrapped line-wrap metadata when a genuine column delta landed after a CLI committed output. Fix (resolves #10863): delete the local cascade, trust revealUntilStable's bounded retry as sole owner. Alt-buffer panes (isAltBuffer) are unaffected by design (#10632). Lesson: reveal/resize paths need exactly one owner per resource; extend the shared sweep's retry logic instead of bolting on a parallel cascade.

title: Electron's native role:close accelerator dispatches to whichever webContents has OS keyboard focus — a <webview> guest is a separate webContents that host-level setIgnoreMenuShortcuts guards never see
summary: Cmd+W closed the whole window instead of the panel when a webview guest (dev-preview/browser) held OS keyboard focus, because host-level guards in createWindow.ts/ProjectViewHandlers.ts never see guest keystrokes. Fixed in protocols.ts setupWebviewCSP() guest listener: intercept, forward WEBVIEW_CLOSE_SHORTCUT, dispatch terminal.close. No panel-kind gate.

title: A demotion-stripped recompute becomes a pure ratchet: pty-host's recomputeActivityTiers force-activated every terminal in every project on every project switch, so a long multi-project session monotonically pinned more idle terminals to the expensive 50ms poll, degrading the same event loop that forwards scroll
summary: electron/pty-host.ts's recomputeActivityTiers (three call sites: connection.ts set-active-project/project-switch, pty-host.ts disconnectWindow) looped ptyManager.getAll() and force-set every terminal in every project to the 50ms ActivityMonitor poll tier on each project switch/connect/disconnect. PR #10811's hibernation-removal experiment had stripped the old union-based demotion branch to fix alt-screen wake corruption, making the function strictly promote-only; since TerminalRendererPolicy.ts's own demotion only fires on write/visibility/focus/mount/reparent, idle backgrounded terminals never came back down, so a long multi-project session (issue #10857) monotonically ratcheted more terminals onto the 50ms cadence in the same single-threaded pty-host event loop that forwards scroll round trips. Fixed in #10861 by scoping the recompute to ptyManager.getTerminalsForProject(nextProjectId). Lesson: any promote-only reset loop is a ratchet under repeated triggers unless scoped to the event that changed.

title: Resource governance that downgrades under load throttles the exact interactive path causing the load: efficiency mode stretches the pty-host port-batch delay 16ms to 40ms and drops the WebGL flip threshold, both mid-scroll — fix with a time-boxed interactive override, not a slower signal
summary: ResourceProfileService downgrades performance/balanced/efficiency under sustained event-loop lag; efficiency stretches portBatcher's portBatchThroughputDelayMs from 16ms (PORT_BATCH_THROUGHPUT_DELAY_MS) to 40ms and drops TerminalWebGLManager's WebGL flip threshold (balanced 12 to efficiency 8 under the flat 16-context cap at merge time, later made RAM-tiered ratios by #11192), both firing exactly while scrolling a full-screen mouse-reporting TUI (grok, lazygit, btop) causes the load in the first place — a self-defeating feedback loop (#10858). Fixed across #10848/#10860/#10895 with a renderer-driven, time-boxed requestInteractiveOverride (MAX_INTERACTIVE_OVERRIDE_MS=5000) from TerminalBurstController.onActiveWheel/onUserScrollIntent clamping the profile to >=balanced, a single applyProfile choke point, plus removing a redundant requestAnimationFrame gate since Chromium already frame-aligns wheel dispatch (WHEEL_MIN_DISPATCH_GAP_MS=6). Also documents a deliberate override of xterm's MouseService._consumeWheelEvent that must not be deleted post-upgrade.

title: A module-level hydration lock is unlocked by whichever mounted instance runs its effect first — the pre-hydration skeleton AppLayout resolves its state restore before the real one mounts, so releasing on value alone (not instance identity) defeats the lock
summary: layoutTransitionLock.ts hydrationLocked (isSidebarMeasurementLocked) gates ResizeObserver remeasure in useContentGridContext/TwoPaneSplitLayout/TerminalReconciliationWatchdog, fixing AppLayout's first-load grid snap (#10827). Gotcha: App.tsx's skeleton AppLayout resolves restoreState first, so unlock gates on isHydrated, not value, else it unlocks early.

title: waitUntilIdle's subscribe-then-read pattern (right for missed-event races) traps on stale state left by a respawned agentId: it settles as already-idle and drops its listener before the crash's exit event arrives
summary: electron/services/mcp-server/waitUntilIdle.ts handleWaitUntilIdle subscribes to agent:state-changed before reading AgentAvailabilityStore.getState(agentId) to avoid missed-event races; correct in isolation but agent:spawned never reset agentStates on respawn, so a reused agentId inherited a prior session's stale 'waiting', settled as already-idle, unsubscribed, then missed the real exited event. Also: failed-to-start spawns (ptyManager.spawn throws ENOENT) produce no PTY exit at all, so electron/pty-host/handlers/lifecycle.ts now synthesizes agent-spawned+agent-state(exited) wire events gated on launchAgentId. Fix touched addPanel.ts and restart.ts (isAgent classification, #5764 demoted-shell gate). Consequence: MCP terminal.awaitAll misreported crashed agents as finished, reading nonexistent output.

title: Assistant cold-resume: the atomic takePendingHibernation guard existed but ran after the side-effecting provisionHelpSession call, so both racing windows displaced each other before either could lose gracefully
summary: HelpSessionController._executeLaunch's resumeOnly path called provisionHelpSession (which triggers HelpSessionService.displacePriorSessions, revoking the project's existing assistant backend) before checking the atomic takePendingHibernation claim. Two windows cold-restoring the same project simultaneously both provisioned before either learned it lost the race, so each displaced the other's just-resumed backend, leaving both with no live assistant and the hibernation token consumed. Fix (#10820, following #10818/#10819) hoists the take before any provisioning, aborts on null-take/agentId-mismatch/superseded-gen, and gates resume on the take result rather than the possibly-stale useHelpPanelStore.hibernateSessions entry. General lesson: in claim-then-act protocols the atomic claim must be the first side effect, not merely present before the terminal state.

title: MCP action handlers must throw, not return null, on failure: ActionService.dispatch already converts any thrown error into isError:true — a swallowed null just looks like success to a model client and drives retry loops
summary: agent.launch (agentActions.ts) returned fake success with null terminalId — useAgentLauncher's worktree lookup only console.warn'd, never threw; MCP serialized isError:false, driving 34-call retry loops. Fix: resolveLaunchWorktree throws listing valid IDs; ActionService.dispatch's try/catch already converts throws to isError:true via buildToolError.

title: Per-terminal hibernation (PR #4213) was torn out whole: suspend-then-resync of a live TUI is inherently lossy, and it was saving 0.1-1MB against a 100-500MB-per-project renderer lever
summary: electron/services/HibernationService.ts, ProjectViewManager.destroyView(): #10811 deleted per-terminal suspend/resync (TerminalWakeManager, TerminalHibernationManager) — resyncing a live alt-screen TUI from a snapshot is inherently lossy (#10800/#10805 corruption). #10796: hibernation freed ~1MB vs ~493MB via renderer eviction. #10832: disable guard broke Close Them.

title: LRU view eviction re-fires app:boot in a fresh V8 context: any main-process 'pending' singleton not explicitly cleared on resolve replays on switch-back
summary: ProjectViewManager LRU-evicts idle project WebContentsViews and cold-recreates them via createView; the fresh V8 context has no cached bootPromise (src/lib/bootPromise.ts) so app:boot fires again exactly like a real cold launch. CrashRecoveryService's pendingCrash singleton was set once in initialize() and never cleared on dialog resolve, so getPendingCrash() kept returning it, re-presenting the crash-recovery dialog hours later on switch-back with no new crash — whose decline path resets to a clean layout and would kill live hour-old terminals. Fixed via idempotent clearPendingCrash() called on both crash-recovery:resolve success paths (not on restore-failure, to keep retry alive) and on recovery:reset-and-reload before the reload's own app:boot fires. General rule: any main-process singleton feeding app:boot a once-only payload must clear itself on resolve or LRU eviction replays it.

title: Any code path that mutates activeProjectId outside the serialized switchChain can cancel a paint gate mid-flight, skip deactivateEntry, and leave two WebContentsViews composited at once
summary: ProjectViewManager bridge keeps outgoing+incoming WebContentsViews attached until paint confirms, guarded by activeProjectId. HibernationService.destroyView mutates activeProjectId outside switchChain, skipping deactivateEntry; the orphan stays attached, Chromium composites two renderers (duplicated forge toolbar, #10806). Fix: pruneOrphanedChildren sweep.

title: isAltBuffer, not focus-changed or sync-block-open, is the correct gate for a terminal 'heal it' primitive — wake's reset+replay and reconcileGeometryFresh's reflow both corrupted live alt-screen TUIs by gating on the wrong transient flag instead of the persistent buffer mode
summary: OpenCode/alt-screen TUIs garbled on click or reveal because two unrelated repair primitives — wake-on-focus's reset()+serialized-replay (terminalFocusSlice.ts: setFocused/activateTerminal/openDockTerminal) and TerminalResizeController.reconcileGeometryFresh (added #10488, watchdog-swept by #10637) — each guarded a transient flag (focusActuallyChanged, inSynchronizedBlock) instead of the persistent managed.isAltBuffer. Fix (PR #10805): reconcileGeometryFresh short-circuits on isAltBuffer; new TerminalRevealController.wakeForFocus no-ops for live foreground alt-screen panes. git bisect vs v0.19.0 found the reflow trigger after an earlier #10800 refocus-gate fix failed.

title: A hardcoded env-var isolation list in a test silently drifts from the agent registry it's isolating against — and CI's key-free environment can never catch the gap
summary: CliAvailabilityService.test.ts hardcoded a literal list of auth env vars (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, etc.) to clear before asserting an 'unauthenticated' CLI state. The list drifted from shared/config/agentRegistry.ts's authCheck.envVar as agents were added under shared/config/agents/, so a real key on an authenticated dev machine leaked into checkAuth's env probe and flipped the result to 'ready', failing locally while CI (no keys ever set) stayed green — inverted signal. Fix: derive envKeysToClear from getAgentIds().flatMap(id => getAgentConfig(id)?.authCheck?.envVar), mirroring checkAuth's own string|string[] normalization, so the isolation list can't diverge from the registry it protects against.

title: dnd-kit's KeyboardSensor calls preventDefault() on Space/Enter to start a keyboard drag pickup, which silently swallows a native <button>'s click activation — forwarding a drag handle's full listener set onto an interactive element breaks it, not just a theoretical risk
summary: Docked panel chips (DockedTerminalItem, DockedTabGroup, #10797) needed dnd-kit useDragHandle() wiring. Spreading DraggableSyntheticListeners onto the native button, as PanelHeader.tsx does onto a non-interactive div, lets KeyboardSensor onKeyDown preventDefault Space/Enter, killing onClick and the keyboard path to the preview popover. Fix filters out onKeyDown.

title: xterm WebGL atlas-resync recovery path synchronously re-fires the same atlas events it listens for, closing a self-sustaining 60fps reset loop — fixed with a synchronous re-entrancy guard, not rAF coalescing
summary: scheduleAtlasResync/runAtlasResync (TerminalWebGLManager) calls resetLocalWebGLRenderer -> handleResize -> _refreshCharAtlas, synchronously re-firing the same atlas events it listens for -- each resync reschedules itself via rAF, pinning a CPU core on alt-buffer TUIs. Fixed with a synchronous suppressAtlasResync flag; rAF coalescing alone cannot stop it.

title: Two independent sites (pty-host TerminalAgentDetection + renderer identityReducer) rewrite any panel title still tagged titleMode 'default' the moment agent detection fires — a launch-time computed title survives only if it's explicitly pinned custom, and 'the icon color is fine but the name reverted' is the diagnostic signature
summary: useAgentLauncher.ts pins titleMode:"custom" for caller names but not preset titles; computeDefaultTitle (terminalTitle.ts/TerminalAgentDetection.ts) and identityReducer.ts both rewrite any titleMode:"default" panel on agent detection, flattening 'Claude [Z.ai]' to 'Claude' while agentPresetColor survives untouched. Fix folds hasPresetTitle into the pin check.

title: Windows node-pty reports pid 0 during the ConPTY connect window and never fires a follow-up event — every '!== undefined' PID gate must become 'positive integer', and the gate itself must retry, not just reject
summary: electron/pty-host/handlers/lifecycle.ts, TerminalProcess.ts, PtyEventRouter.ts, TerminalRegistry.ts, terminalActivityPatterns.ts: Windows node-pty/ConPTY reports pid 0 during the async connect() window with no follow-up event carrying the real pid. Every producer/consumer gate used 'pid !== undefined', which pid:0 satisfies, starting ProcessDetector on an invalid pid and spamming 'Invalid PTY PID' warnings on every refresh tick across 8+ call sites. Fix generalizes an isValidPid (Number.isInteger && >0) helper everywhere, but a bare tightened gate would silently and permanently disable process-tree detection for affected terminals since nothing re-reads the pid later — so lifecycle.ts also adds a bounded setImmediate poll (schedulePidRetry, PID_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS=20) via PtyManager.startProcessDetectorForTerminal to recover the real pid once ConPTY resolves. Lesson: sentinel-value validity checks on OS handles need both a stricter gate AND a retry path when the underlying value can transition from invalid to valid asynchronously with no completion event.

title: simple-git's .env() replaces the spawn env wholesale, not merges — and simple-git 3.36.0 rejects any EDITOR-family key in that env unless allowUnsafeEditor is set, so the fix meant one rebuilt env object, not two .env() calls
summary: electron/utils/hardenedGit.ts + electron/ipc/handlers/git-write.ts: simple-git 3.36.0's @simple-git/argv-parser env scanner rejects EDITOR/GIT_EDITOR/GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR keys unless unsafe.allowUnsafeEditor is set, breaking all --continue git operations (rebase/merge/cherry-pick/revert) with 'Use of EDITOR is not permitted'. Compounded by simple-git .env() being last-write-wins not merge — a second .env() call on an already-hardened instance silently dropped all hardening (#7058 pattern), and raw process.env spreading leaked the user's shell EDITOR. Fixed via single buildContinueEnv() consolidating hardened env + editor suppression, exact-pinned simple-git to 3.36.0, and dropped --no-edit from merge --continue (git 2.54.0 rejects it with exit 129, unlike rebase/cherry-pick/revert). Verified all symbols still present in current codebase and cross-checked against gh pr view 10789.

title: audit_rings.created_at is re-stamped to now() on every writeAll() snapshot rewrite, so it can never encode record age — and a persisted settings value nobody reads is a silent lie
summary: AuditRingStore (electron/services/persistence/auditRingStore.ts) backs 6 SQLite audit_rings logs; writeAll() re-stamps created_at=now() every flush — flush time, not record age. pruneByAge (auditLog.ts/turnOutcomeLog.ts) filters embedded .timestamp instead; 4 other logs still trim by count only; helpAssistant.auditRetention had zero consumers (#10776).

title: A session-only overlay must be enforced at every read/write boundary of the shared map, not just the reported call site — the first cut of the verbose-logging fix reopened the same leak through the per-module override palette
summary: electron/ipc/handlers/logs.ts: verbose-logging toggle wrote "*":"debug" into the persisted electron-store logLevelOverrides map that electron/main.ts re-hydrates on boot (#10774). First fix commit made handleLogsSetVerbose stop persisting, but handleGetLevelOverrides still exposed the wildcard to LogLevelPalette, whose save handler (handleSetLevelOverrides) persisted it verbatim — reopening the exact bug through a second handler, fixed 10 minutes later by a verboseSessionActive flag plus savedWildcardBeforeVerbose bookkeeping across get/set/clear. Mechanism: a shared mutable map used as both live state and persistence payload needs every reader and writer taught about a session overlay, not just the call site named in the bug report.

title: HiDPI zebra banding in xterm's DOM renderer is a fractional-cell-height Chromium snap seam, not a Daintree bug — xterm 6.x dropped addon-canvas so the only fixes are pinning alt-buffer panes to WebGL and Bresenham-snapping DOM row heights to integers
summary: TerminalWebGLManager/TerminalListenerInstaller (#10768/#10771): full-width horizontal zebra banding in alt-buffer TUI panes (OpenCode, vim) on fractional-DPR displays traces to xterm DomRenderer._updateDimensions computing css.cell.height = css.canvas.height / rows, a fractional CSS value Chromium pixel-snaps inconsistently row-to-row. addon-canvas is removed in xterm 6.x, leaving only WebGL (no seam) and DOM (seam). Fix: altBufferPinnedIds set unified with focus pinnedId behind isPinned() across 8 DOM-mode exemption sites keeps alt-buffer panes on WebGL through fleet DOM flips; onRender-driven Bresenham row-height snap (snapDomRowHeightsToIntegerPixels) handles genuine DOM fallback panes, summing exactly to canvas height. Teaches: diagnosing HiDPI terminal corruption, onRender vs onResize choice, exact-sum pixel redistribution, and new-pin-category lifecycle/exemption-site completeness.

title: Logging is never free at scale: per-line appendFileSync plus synchronous worktree-update fan-out stalled the main event loop for 1-1.75s under multi-agent load, and a scrub-then-clamp ordering bug in the same redaction path could leak a truncated secret to disk
summary: electron/utils/logger.ts appendFileSync per non-error line (150-300/s, 0.2-20ms each incl. rotation statSync) plus WorkspaceHostEventRouter.ts's uncoalesced sys:worktree:update bus (10-50/s, synchronously driving PullRequestService+MCP listeners) stalled Electron's main event loop 1000-1755ms under multi-agent load, surfacing as keystroke echo lag across multiple terminals simultaneously (issue #10769). Fixed via batched async appendFile (pendingLogLines/runAsyncFlush, 256KB safety valve, sync ERROR bypass) and a 50ms per-worktree debounce (#10770); redactSensitiveData/emitError deduped and bounded at MAX_REDACT_DEPTH=5/STRING_CHARS=2000/ARRAY_ITEMS=20 to protect the 500-entry LogBuffer ring, with a scrub-before-clamp ordering fix preventing truncation from leaking an unredacted secret prefix (#10780); renderer logger (src/utils/logger.ts) gained a client-side resolveEffectiveLevel floor plus 16ms LOGS_WRITE_BATCH coalescing to stop ~99 call sites paying wasted IPC round trips (#10784).

title: Per-project WebContentsViews make one reactivation fire TWO polling triggers (visibilitychange + onProjectSwitch) — a rate-limit-triggered red error survived one fix because its tests modeled a single shared renderer instead of Daintree's per-view reality
summary: usePollingLifecycle (src/hooks/usePollingLifecycle.ts) fires onVisibilityVisible and onProjectSwitch independently on one project switch-back, doubling FORGE_GET_REPO_STATS IPC calls; rapid switching bursts the main-process checkRateLimit(10/10s) throttle, throws RATE_LIMITED, and paints a persistent forge-status-error toolbar line. Prior fix #10762's switchBackStatsCache only hid the loading skeleton, never the network call, and its tests modeled a single shared renderer instead of ProjectViewManager's one-WebContentsView-per-project reality, so it passed CI but not production. #10767 fixes it by threading a PollingLifecycleFetchReason (initial/reactivate/scheduled/manual) through the fetch context with REASON_RANK strongest-wins coalescing, and skipping the network on fresh reactivations in useRepositoryStats.

title: MCP CallTool rate limiter was self-defeating for the in-app assistant: hard-rejecting a model client with no backoff path breaks it worse than the runaway loop it guarded against, and removing it left docs/architecture/mcp-server.md silently wrong
summary: electron/services/mcp-server/ CallTool pipeline: PR #8517 added a per-(sessionId,toolId) token-bucket rate limiter (RATE_LIMIT_TIERS/RATE_LIMIT_TOOL_MAP/consumeToken/SessionStore.consumeRateLimitToken) guarding against runaway agent loops (#8468), which hard-rejected concurrent terminal.getOutput reads from the in-app assistant with MCP_RATE_LIMITED; the model client never honored retryAfter, surfacing an unrecoverable TERMINAL_OUTPUT error instead. PR #10766 removed enforcement wholesale (-602/+45 lines, verified via gh pr diff) while keeping the rate_limited audit vocabulary (McpAuditResult, MCP_RATE_LIMITED_CODE) read-only for historical record parsing, and leaving PLUGIN_MCP_RATE_LIMITED/IPC leaky-bucket/GitHub RateLimitBucket untouched (different trust boundaries). Verified docs/architecture/mcp-server.md still documents the removed rate-limit gate step and RATE_LIMIT_TIERS section as of 2026-07-08 (git log confirmed), two weeks post-merge — the doc is now stale and misleading on gate order.

title: A nullable path-equality ref is a self-disarming async guard: useRepositoryStats reset lastKnownCountsRef.projectPath to null on the exact event it needed to guard, so a stale cross-project fetch always sailed through — the fix is a monotonic generation counter, the same idiom already used for HybridInputBar's focus-steal guard
summary: useRepositoryStats.ts's cross-project fetch guard compared a projectPath ref that onProjectSwitch reset to null every switch, disarming its own !== null check exactly when needed — a stale in-flight fetch then landed on the new project, sticking a red forge-status-error line (#10761). Fixed via monotonic fetchGenerationRef, capture-then-recheck every await.

title: Fixed-size warm pools (workspace-host pool capped at 3, view cache capped at 4) ignore the real working set — a normal 5-project rotation evicts and cold-respawns on nearly every switch, stalling the main event loop for seconds
summary: Project-switch perf arc (#10737/#10746/#10748/#10751/#10757/#10760): WorkspaceHostPool's flat MAX_WARM_ENTRIES=3 and computeDefaultCachedViews' view-cache cap of 4 ignored real RAM and working set, so a normal 5-project rotation evicted+cold-respawned a utility-process host or renderer on nearly every switch (1-1.75s stalls, 326 spawns/session, A/B harness showed 7044ms freeze -> 0). Fixed by RAM-scaling both to shared 2/3/4/5 tiers. Related: ResourceProfileService's efficiency profile destructively clamped setCachedViewLimit(1) via a hardcoded getUserCachedViewLimit fallback regardless of RAM (#10748 split freeze-CPU from destroy-RAM, gated destruction on evictStaleViews' lowMemoryFreeThresholdMb only); WorkspaceHostPool.releaseOldProject never paused background hosts on switch-away, only on close (#10746 background/foreground send with multi-window guard).

title: Vitest threads-pool migration was tried and reverted in this same PR — @parcel/watcher's native addon can't load into a second worker_thread on Linux CI, so the sharding (not the pool) is the actual speedup
summary: vitest.config.ts / .github/workflows/ci.yml: PR #10758's own description claims a forks->threads pool switch for CI unit-test speedup, but the merged config keeps pool:forks — threads was tried and reverted (commits 8b684952d then eb62621da, both pre-merge, 37 minutes apart) because @parcel/watcher's native addon throws 'Module did not self-register' when loaded into a second worker_thread on Linux. Real speedup came from 4-way vitest --shard matrix in ci.yml, not the pool. process.cwd() stub (vs process.chdir) and minWorkers removal kept regardless; follow-up PR #11093 later added maxWorkers:Math.min(availableParallelism(),8) after uncapped workers oversubscribed 4-core CI shards. Lesson: verify PR body/title against actual diff, don't retry threads pool here.

title: Cold project-switch reveal waited on React's first structural paint when a themed skeleton already painted 10x earlier, and once fixed, the reveal was re-hidden by a shared 400ms Doherty gate never scoped to it
summary: ProjectViewManager (now split into ProjectViewSwitchController/ProjectViewPaintGateController/ProjectViewFactory) gated cold-switch reveal on APP_VIEW_PAINTED (1.5-4s) instead of the already-firing, earlier-sufficient APP_SKELETON_PARSED signal createWindow.ts already used. #10751 added the skeleton-painted gate channel with signalViewPainted fallback; #10760 found the shared 400ms Doherty animation-delay in skeletonCss.ts still hid the now-fast ~150ms reveal, fixed via opt-in instantReveal overriding only animation-delay (not the animation shorthand, which would defeat prefers-reduced-motion). Also covers projectStore.ts's yieldToPaint() macrotask-vs-microtask pattern (setTimeout not queueMicrotask) with a projectTransitionRequestId staleness guard so a busy overlay can paint before a heavy synchronous buildOutgoingState() snapshot.

title: A backgrounded WebContentsView freezes rAF and every reactive flag it drives — the warm-reveal path must prove state from DOM ground truth, race rAF against a timeout, get an explicit pre-freeze cancellation signal, and stash (never drop) events during the switch lock
summary: ProjectViewManager freezes backgrounded WebContentsViews: rAF stalls, isVisible sticks stale. PR #10750 makes terminal reveal (TerminalWebGLPolicy, revealUntilStable, TerminalResizeController, wakeActiveWorktreeTerminals) prove DOM truth, race rAF vs timeout, cancel pre-freeze, and stash mid-switch resizes. Fixes mangled glyphs, hung sweeps.

title: A self-rearming coalesce timer that pushes its deadline on every chunk never fires under sustained output — needs a hard max-defer ceiling independent of the soft deadline; the whole background-coalescing idea was scrapped 3 days later anyway
summary: TerminalProcess.ts background coalescing (#10747) self-rearmed its drain deadline on every chunk, so sustained output never drained: activityMonitor.onData starved, lastActivityTimestamp stalled, 8s IDLE_DEBOUNCE_MS flipped working agents to waiting. #10749 added COALESCE_MAX_DEFER_MS; #10811 deleted the subsystem 3 days later, net-negative.

title: A renderer setTimeout watchdog freezes forever on a parked per-project WebContentsView — recovery must key off the main-process app:view-revealed signal, and the existing reveal effect was itself gated on the one field (terminalId) that's null during the exact failure it needed to catch
summary: HelpSessionController launch FSM (#10739) sticks forever on switch-back: a parked WebContentsView freezes setTimeout so _armLaunchWatchdog never fires, and _maybeAutoLaunch skips while hidden. Fix keys handleViewRevealed off app:view-revealed; terminalId-gated repaint effect cannot fire mid-stall, needing a new isOpen-gated one. Relates #10707, #10714.

title: Adding heap-snapshot-on-near-limit diagnostics can defeat a burst-based crash guard: the snapshot write itself spaces OOM crashes wide enough to dodge the window, turning a crash loop into a silent infinite Reconnecting retry
summary: electron/services/WorkspaceHostProcess.ts burst crash guard (CRASH_THRESHOLD=3 in CRASH_WINDOW_MS=30min) never tripped because each OOM crash's ~55MB V8 setHeapSnapshotNearHeapLimit dump added jitter spacing crashes 6-11min apart, aging the oldest timestamp out before a third landed; host looped silently in Reconnecting (#10727/#10729). Fix: independent inter-crash-interval detector (OOM_LOOP_INTERVAL_MS=20min, OOM_LOOP_THRESHOLD=2, consecutiveShortCrashIntervals) sized wider than the burst guard's effective reach so the two never overlap, resets on manualRestart not ready, plus heap cap 256->512MB. Sibling PR #10732 added pruneHeapSnapshots/pruneHeapSnapshotsAsync (MAX_HEAP_SNAPSHOTS=10) after 103 files/5.6GB accumulated unpruned. Pattern: crash-triggered diagnostics need their own retention policy, and burst guards need interval-based backstops when the failure mode itself perturbs timing.

title: TerminalRendererPolicy dedupes FOCUSED and BURST to the same backend value, so typing on a paused-backpressure terminal never reached the host — the fix needed an explicit wake() outside the tier system, whose mechanism was rewritten days later
summary: TerminalRendererPolicy.setBackendTier dedupes FOCUSED/BURST to backend active/50ms, so onUserInput's BURST promotion no-ops and a paused-backpressure terminal's Paused pill never clears on typing (#10669). Fix: wake(id) gated on flowStatus+backgroundedTerminals. wake()'s TerminalWakeManager/wakeExecutor.ts mechanism was deleted 5 days later by hibernation removal.

title: MCP tool exposure has two independently-curated allowlists (external MCP_TOOL_ALLOWLIST vs help-tier WORKBENCH/ACTION/SYSTEM_TIER_ADDONS) — adding a tool to one does not add it to the other, and no build guard catches the drift
summary: electron/services/mcp-server/shared.ts curates MCP_TOOL_ALLOWLIST_ENTRIES for the external/api-key MCP tier independently from shared/config/helpAssistantTierAllowlists.ts's WORKBENCH_TIER_TOOLS/ACTION_TIER_ADDONS/SYSTEM_TIER_ADDONS consumed by shouldExposeTool (tierAuth.ts) for the Daintree Assistant (HelpSessionService.ts, system tier via ASSISTANT_ONLY_AGENT_IDS). #10696 added terminal.arm/disarm/disarmAll to the external list only; #10712 had to add them to SYSTEM_TIER_ADDONS after the assistant's own drift check flagged them as documented-but-missing. No build-time guard diffs the two lists (verified still absent from scripts/); docs/architecture/mcp-server.md's 'keep in lockstep' note is comment-only and didn't prevent recurrence. Every new MCP tool needs a deliberate placement call in both curations, plus a separate judgment on which help tier (system = first-party assistant only, action = third-party floor).

title: MCP fullToolSurface trusted the self-declared danger/mcpVisibility fields as a security ceiling instead of the server-side allowlist — 335 of 426 actions leaked to external API-key callers
summary: electron/services/mcp-server/tierAuth.ts shouldExposeTool and isTierPermitted short-circuited to return true for tier==='external' && fullToolSurface, bypassing MCP_TOOL_ALLOWLIST in shared.ts entirely and trusting each action's self-declared danger/mcpVisibility as the security boundary. Since zero shipped actions use danger:'restricted' and only ~8 use mcpVisibility hidden/discoverable, 335 of 426 actions (system.openExternal, system.openPath, env.global.set, project.cloneRepo, terminal.kill, app.quit, forge writes) became reachable to any external API-key client with fullToolSurface on. Fix: explicit fail-closed MCP_FULL_TOOL_SURFACE_ALLOWLIST as a provable superset union of the curated allowlist, applied in lockstep to both gates. Same bug class as #8331 (plugin self-declared danger).

title: Migrating a persisted flag that gates a billing side-effect must default false for EVERYONE, including returning users — preserving old behavior across the migration preserves the bug
summary: helpPanelStore's autoLaunchEnabled flag (persist v4→v5) gates HelpSessionController._maybeAutoLaunch, which previously auto-started billed provider-CLI assistant sessions on panel open (#10699). Migration must NOT carve out returning users with a preferredAgentId to autoLaunchEnabled:true — the old behavior IS the reported bug, so preserving it for existing installs preserves silent billing. Rehydrate uses strict `=== true` so undefined/malformed values normalize to false for everyone; re-enable is a one-click 'Start assistant' CTA. Consent check in _maybeAutoLaunch is ordered before the document.hidden guard so a visibilityEpoch restore can't bypass it. Applies to any of the ~13 persist-wrapped Zustand stores adding a consent/gate flag during a version migration.

title: Grandchild-reaping teardown must run on the COMMON settle path, not just the failure paths — a killTree() wired only to the deadline/buffer-cap backstop never fires on the normal exit-grace case
summary: AgentVersionService.runVersionProbe (electron/services/AgentVersionService.ts) spawns agent CLIs for version checks; killTree() fired only on deadline/MAX_BUFFER backstops, never the exit-grace settle, leaking a detached process group per probe (#10697). Fix wires killTree() into the grace path plus Windows taskkill /T /F, unref, ESRCH-only catch, dedup guard, error sinks.

title: A CSS width transition on a box wrapping a live PTY fires ResizeObserver on nearly every frame, not just at settle — animate transform on that box instead, never width
summary: AppLayout.tsx's assistant pane show/hide animated a flex wrapper's width (0<->helpPanelWidth); the ResizeObserver behind XtermAdapter's PTY resize fired xterm.resize->pty.resize->SIGWINCH nearly every frame instead of once at settle, storm-resizing the hosted Ink CLI so its status line autowrapped into an orphaned scrollback row per toggle (#10693). Fix: wrapper is fixed-width, slides via compositor-only transform:translateX (never triggers ResizeObserver); a terminal-free spacer div animates width to drive the <main> push instead, with suppressSidebarResizes armed on its transitionstart and a filtered repaint on transitionend. TTL bumped +100->+150ms; non-transition paths (reduced motion, performance mode, drag-resize) settle synchronously. Follow-on #11070: one-shot repaint dropped cold-open races, fixed via createAssistantRevealCoordinator.

title: PTY-hosted checks have no observable exit code: node-pty only sees the agent CLI process, so terminal.getStatus's lastCheckResult must be parsed from stdout text and is precision-over-recall, never authoritative
summary: MCP terminal.getStatus.lastCheckResult (CheckResultDetector.ts, AgentStateService.ts) parses tsc/ESLint/Vitest/Jest text since node-pty can't see child-process exit codes; OSC 133 injection banned (Agent Config Boundary #4100). Precision-over-recall: absent means unrecognized, not pass. Pessimistic +/-3-line Vitest/Jest verdict avoids masked sibling failures.

title: RepoFetchCoordinator's Infinity-TTL auth suspension turned one transient 401/403 into a permanent stripe on every worktree card — confirm severity across time-separated retries, never on a single observation, and coalesce concurrent siblings into one count
summary: electron/workspace-host/RepoFetchCoordinator.ts set AUTH_FAILURE_TTL_MS=Infinity on the first auth-classified git fetch failure, permanently suspending the repo and fanning the UpstreamSyncBadge auth-failed stripe onto every sibling worktree via WorkspaceService; GitHub secondary rate limits (403) and routine GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 credential-helper messages were misclassified identically in shared/utils/gitOperationErrors.ts classifyGitError/PATTERNS. Fix: exponential backoff schedule (5/15/30/60min), AUTH_FAILURE_CONFIRM_RETRIES=3 gating the alarming UI, buildAuthFailureEntry coalescing concurrent sibling/force-retry observations within one backoff window (now>=prior.retryAt) so confirmation can't trigger instantly, and a distinct rate-limited GitOperationReason ordered before auth-failed.

title: Off-screen agent terminals silently spent the shared WebGL budget, dropping every visible terminal to DOM — and a same-day sibling bug showed setFocused() (not focus()) is the only path to the WebGL pin
summary: TerminalWebGLManager's fleet-wide count-based mode switch (evaluateMode/flipToDom in TerminalWebGLManager.ts) flipped ALL terminals to DOM renderer once wants exceeded the upper threshold (12 at the time, now RAM-tiered via #11192), but wantsWebGLAtTier (now in TerminalWebGLPolicy.ts) had no visibility gate, so invisible streaming background agents (BURST tier via onPtyWrite, never idle) counted toward the cap and starved visible terminals of WebGL, causing flicker/glyph-mangling. applyAgentPromotion in TerminalInstanceService.ts bypassed the policy function entirely (isOpened && isWebGLEligibleTier check). Fixed by gating on managed.isVisible with a webGLHideTimer dwell guard. Sibling PR #10674: HelpPanel (Daintree Assistant) called terminalInstanceService.focus() (DOM focus only) instead of setFocused() (the only path to webGLManager.pinFocus()), so the Assistant could never reclaim WebGL once in DOM mode. TerminalWebGLPolicy.ts now carries a class comment flagging 3 past incidents in this exact logic as high-risk.

title: Agent-state FSM: append-only streaming reads as changedChars:0 to the visible-content diff, so a byte-volume detector alone isn't a fix — you must also defer every demotion gate that reads the same flat diff
summary: ActivityMonitor.onData's simpleOutputState path (agent terminals) exits before OutputVolumeDetector/HighOutputDetector, and measureVisibleContentDelta's isSuffixOf check reports changedChars:0 for pure append output, so a streaming agent never recovered waiting->working. Adding simpleOutputVolumeDetector alone still failed: the temperature stateHint:idle gate and two transitionSimpleToIdle call sites read the same flat diff and demoted the agent right back. Fix required a second clock, lastSimpleOutputVolumeAt/hasRecentSimpleOutputVolume (IDLE_DEBOUNCE_MS=8000ms), guarding all three demotion sites. Generalizes: a new promotion signal must defer every consumer of the old signal it patches around, not just add detection.

title: A field captured correctly at the pty-host source still vanishes before MCP sees it — every explicit-shape hop on the pty-host-to-renderer chain must be re-taught the field by hand
summary: electron/services/pty/AgentStateService.ts, PtyEventsBridge.ts, AgentAvailabilityStore.ts, mcp-server/sessionServer.ts and waitUntilIdle.ts, shared/types/pty-host.ts: exposing exitCode/exitSignal over MCP (terminal.getStatus, agent.getState, daintree://agent state resource, waitUntilIdle, agent:state-changed) required threading the field through 5 explicit-shape hops between the pty-host utility process and main — TerminalProcess capture, AgentStateService event construction, the PtyHostEvent IPC type, PtyEventsBridge.bridgePtyEvent's reconstruction (where review caught the field silently stripped even after capture was fixed), and AgentAvailabilityStore's cache. No hop uses generic passthrough; a named object literal that omits an optional field compiles clean and just drops it silently. Also documents !== undefined vs truthiness for 0/null exit values and unconditional-capture vs preserve-on-exit gating.

title: Terminal switch-back redraw only stops recurring once recovery is a CLOSED loop: one-shot timed repairs get silently spent on a detached pane, and the watchdog must verify the alt-buffer agent TUIs it used to exclude
summary: src/services/terminal/TerminalReconciliationWatchdog.ts: a month of ~10 point-fixes for stale/garbled terminals on project switch-back all added open-loop one-shot repairs (rAF/1s/3s/10s backstops) while the only closed-loop mechanism, the reconciliation watchdog, deliberately excluded alt-buffer/DEC-2026 agent TUIs — exactly the terminals that broke. Fix converts the watchdog into a continuous convergence verifier comparing cols/rows against fitAddon.proposeDimensions() for every on-screen terminal, with resetRenderer reporting whether it actually ran so the obligation transfers instead of evaporating on a detached host.

title: Per-test `if (process.platform === 'win32') return` reports GREEN with zero assertions; on Ubuntu-only unit CI the Windows branch is never covered by any real-platform test — use describe.skipIf for visibility PLUS a mocked-platform suite for real coverage, proven load-bearing by an anti-vacuous mutation
summary: electron/services/pty/__tests__/ProcessTreeKiller.test.ts: every test opened with if(win32) return before any expect, so vitest reported full green while the Windows taskkill /T /F teardown path had zero real assertions anywhere, compounded by Daintree's Ubuntu-only push/PR CI making the win32 branch permanently unreachable by a real-platform test. Fix: describe.skipIf for visibility (SKIPPED not PASS) plus a separate suite mocking process.platform+spawnSync to actually exercise the branch on the Ubuntu runner, verified load-bearing by an anti-vacuous mutation (dropping /T must fail the test).

title: A fire-and-forget agent launch that never blurs its toolbar <button> strands DOM focus there; a focused button fires click on Enter (HTML spec), so Enter at the CLI trust prompt re-launches — and the one-shot RAF meant to hand focus off silently no-ops against React.lazy HybridInputBar's null ref
summary: src/components/Layout/AgentButton.tsx handleClick fired void dispatch(agent.launch) with no DOM focus handoff, keeping focus on the native <button>; TerminalPane's one-shot RAF focus handoff raced HybridInputBar's React.lazy cold-chunk load (inputBarRef.current?.focus() silently no-op'd on null), so focus never left the button — pressing Enter at Claude's trust prompt synthesized a native button click (HTML activation spec) and re-launched a second agent. Fixed via mount-time self-claimed focus in the lazy component plus e.currentTarget.blur() on every launch, defense in depth.

title: Non-async Promise-returning plugin host methods must `return Promise.reject()` on validation failure — a sync `throw` escapes the Promise and the plugin's `.catch()` never fires; and lazy manifest command handlers get no `host` because it's revoked after activate()
summary: electron/services/plugin/PluginHostFactory.ts: postToPanel/setPanelBadge/invalidateFileDecorations wrap a sync fire-and-forget transport and return Promise.resolve(), so a sync throw for validation errors escaped the Promise entirely — a plugin's documented host.foo().catch() never fired. Fix converts every non-async host method's throw to Promise.reject(), mirrored across both the main-side host and the dev-worker proxy; lazy manifest command handlers structurally can't receive host (revoked post-activate()) — host.registerAction() in activate() is the only way to give a command live host access.

title: A shared plugin push channel fans out to EVERY open instance of a panel kind — per-instance routing needs a {panelId,payload} envelope + a ref-counted preload multiplexer; and an activation error persisted but not RETURNED across IPC surfaces as a generic import timeout
summary: electron/preload.cts: plugin:{pluginId}:{channel} is keyed only by identity with one raw ipcRenderer.on per subscriber, so with two open instances of the same panel kind, postToPanel pushes reached BOTH — no per-instance addressing. Fix: PluginPanelEventEnvelope {panelId,payload} on every push site plus a single ref-counted preload multiplexer keyed by channel. Separately, activatePluginForView persisted an activation failure to loadError but returned void, so the renderer imported an unactivated module and blamed a generic import-timeout instead of the real cause.

title: A green plugin build ships broken artifacts three ways: esbuild compiles code no tsconfig checks, the copy step drops bin/mcp asset dirs (and native spawn can't read them inside asar anyway), and .ts command handlers pass manifest validation then throw at first dispatch under Node's erasable-only type-stripping
summary: scripts/build-main.mjs: three green-build lies — copyPluginExtraAssets previously dropped bin/mcp dirs (ENOENT at spawn) and node-pty's native OS spawn bypasses Electron's asar patch entirely (needs explicit asarUnpack); plugin main/ code sat in no tsconfig so esbuild silently swallowed type errors (new tsconfig.plugins.json, tsc --noEmit only, never -b); and .ts/.tsx command handlers passed manifest validation then threw SyntaxError at first import() under Node's erasable-only type-stripping (extensions restricted to .js/.mjs, fatal build scan added).

title: shared/config registries are per-process singletons — the pty-host holds its own empty copy main never populates, so declared plugin detection patterns stay inert until a set-plugin-agent-registry IPC message mirrors AND replays them on every host-ready (per shard) before spawn replay
summary: shared/config/pluginAgentRegistry.ts is module state, a SEPARATE singleton per process — main populated it but the pty-host (which runs the activity monitor and calls getEffectiveAgentConfig) held its own permanently-empty copy, so declared plugin agent detection patterns were structurally inert with no error. Fix: a set-plugin-agent-registry IPC mirror pushed on every plugin load/unload AND replayed on every pty-host-ready BEFORE spawn replay (crash/shard-fork safe), one-way (main authoritative, pty-host only applies).

title: Plugin settings.get defaulted scope to 'user' on read while set/onDidChange enforced the manifest-declared scope — and the dev-worker proxy pre-defaulted omitted scope to 'user' too, so a host-side resolver fix alone still read the wrong store
summary: electron/services/plugin/PluginHostFactory.ts settings.get hardcoded scope='user' on read while set/onDidChange enforced the manifest-declared scope via assertSettingDeclared, so a project-scoped setting silently read the empty user store; the dev-worker proxy ALSO pre-defaulted omitted scope before the IPC bridge, erasing the omission signal main needed to resolve it. Fix: one shared getDeclaredScope authority for both read and write, proxy/wire type keep scope optional end-to-end, explicit-vs-declared conflicts throw instead of silently reading wrong.

title: plugin:// views are raw browser ESM: bare imports resolve ONLY via the host React-only import map, so SDK hooks fail at RUNTIME (not build) unless bundled by @daintreehq/plugin-vite; raw views use the window.electron.plugin bridge, and mapping the SDK subpath is the wrong fix (double-React, #9493)
summary: A plugin:// panel view is un-transpiled raw browser ESM: the host import map serves only 5 React specifiers, so bare-importing @daintreehq/plugin-sdk/react hooks fails at RUNTIME with no build error — the hooks resolve only when bundled by plugin-vite, which inlines the SDK while externalizing React. Docs wrongly marked the hooks 'shipped' for raw views; the fix was documentation (use window.electron.plugin.on/.onPanel/.invoke directly), NOT adding the SDK to the import map, which would ship a second React instance (#9493 Invalid hook call).

title: A plugin capability model is only as strong as its least-gated dispatch route: generic host.dispatch was a side-door into ungated safe actions, and static per-action danger can't see args-conditional effects
summary: src/services/ActionService.ts: a zero-capability plugin could type-and-submit text into any agent terminal via host.dispatch('terminal.sendCommand',...) since danger:'safe' built-ins were reachable through the generic capability-blind dispatch route, making the agent:read capability moot; separately worktree.createWithRecipe's blast radius depends on an arg (recipeId) that static per-action danger can't see. Fix: denyPluginDispatch:boolean gates by dispatch SOURCE not danger tier (agent:input + host.sendToActiveAgent for the sanctioned path), an args-conditional source guard before IPC, and parse-time deny-list enforcement in the manifest schema.

title: node-pty resolves the command binary BEFORE it applies the spawn cwd — a plugin's ./-relative agent command must be made absolute at registration and shell-escaped so a spaced install dir (Application Support) doesn't split the spawn string
summary: shared/config/pluginAgentRegistry.ts: node-pty resolves a command binary against its OWN process cwd before applying the spawn cwd option, so a plugin-relative `./bin/agent.mjs` command ENOENTs regardless of terminal cwd. Fix resolves to absolute at plugin registration time (pure string join, not node:path, so it stays renderer-bundle-safe); the absolute path then needs a filesystem-probe branch past CliAvailabilityService's bare-PATH-name regex, and shell-escaping since macOS install paths (Application Support) contain spaces that silently split the spawn string.

title: Parallel Electron E2E on macOS local exhausts crashpad Mach ports (GPU/network-service crashes with EMPTY logs that mimic product bugs); Playwright teardown/fixtures never run on SIGINT/SIGTERM, so module-scope signal handlers in launch.ts are the only orphan reaper
summary: e2e/helpers/launch.ts: ~10 concurrent Electron cold-launches on macOS local exhaust Mach ports (crashpad FATAL kr==KERN_SUCCESS, GPU/network-service crashes) with an EMPTY log that reads as a plugin/product bug but is purely environmental — reproduces on macOS local only, not CI. Fix: workers:1 baked into the full-plugins playwright.config.ts project entry (not a CLI flag); orphan Electron helpers from a SIGINT/SIGTERM kill are reaped only by module-scope process.once signal handlers, since Playwright teardown never runs on signals.

title: A plugin can build 'green' yet never load: manifest-copy was auto-discovered but the esbuild main entry was hardcoded, so every per-plugin build step must be discovery-driven — and manifests must be Zod-validated at build (check:plugin-manifests), not first app load
summary: scripts/build-main.mjs: copySamplePluginManifests() auto-discovered sample plugin dirs but esbuild's entryPoints hardcoded two literal plugin paths, so a new sample plugin's plugin.json copied fine while main/index.js was never emitted — green build, non-loading plugin, no error anywhere. Fix: discoverSamplePluginMainEntries() mirrors built-in discovery; scripts/validate-plugin-manifests.ts runs the same runtime Zod schema (getPluginManifestSchema) over every manifest in npm run check, before any clean/emit.

title: A consent pin keyed by identity silently inherits approval when the artifact behind that identity mutates — fingerprint the danger inputs, revoke on any code change, and grant only after validation runs
summary: PluginMcpConsentStore/PluginInstaller.ts: TOFU consent pins keyed by (pluginId,serverId,toolName) auto-approved a server that flipped a tool benign-to-destructive (fingerprint covered description+schema, not danger-tier hints), and a same-id plugin upgrade inherited prior MCP pins/capability grants for new code. Fix: annotationHash over the three tier-influencing ToolAnnotations hints with a never-matching sentinel migration, _purgeConsentPins on every upgrade/reinstall, consent gated LAST after validation/containment so a doomed call can't bank a grant, and resolved-IP (not literal host) SSRF re-checks per redirect hop.

title: User plugins must run out-of-process: in-process import() can never evict V8's ESM module cache (uninstall/reload leaks the realm forever), and any host API with a required-synchronous contract (registerForgeProvider's parseRemote/URL builders) can never cross the async MessagePort
summary: electron/services/PluginService.ts + PluginDevWorkerHost.ts: there is no in-process API to evict V8's ES-module cache, so in-process plugin import() leaks the whole module realm on every uninstall/reload regardless of disposer correctness; fixed by routing ALL user plugins through a utilityProcess.fork worker (VS Code's extension-host model), killed on unload. registerForgeProvider's parseRemote stays a permanent proxy stub because the host consumes it synchronously — an async MessagePort can't carry that contract, so built-ins alone stay in-process.

title: A discriminated-union narrowing helper (getNarrowPanel) reused as a grid-membership filter silently drops plugin kinds — registered plugin panels never mount and isEmpty stays stuck true
summary: src/store/slices/panelRegistry/selectors.ts getNarrowPanel narrows to the built-in PanelInstance union (undefined for any plugin kind by design); reused to build gridTerminals, it silently dropped plugin panels from the render set, so isEmpty stayed true and ContentGridDefault showed the empty state with zero errors. Fix: getRenderablePanel/isPanelRenderEligible as a separate render-membership predicate admitting registered plugin kinds; getNarrowPanel stays for built-in-union-only callers (fleet, dock).

title: Plugin↔host build/packaging contracts fail only at plugin runtime, never at plugin build: keep React externals and the import map on one shared HOST_IMPORTMAP_SPECIFIERS + a resolveId build-fail guard, give stdio servers a node target, and normalize leading './' in the .dntr filter
summary: packages/plugin-vite/src/index.ts + PluginArchive.ts: four plugin build/packaging traps invisible at build time — react-dom/server externalizes but has no import-map entry (unresolved specifier at load); a stdio MCP server built through the browser config shims node:process to empty; dev import map has no vendor-react chunk; and leading './' bypassed the dev-file archive-exclusion filter, leaking author's package.json/home path. Fixed via one shared HOST_IMPORTMAP_SPECIFIERS constant + build guard, a node target config, a dev virtual-module react map, and path normalization before exclusion.

title: `export type *` in the plugin-sdk barrel type-erases EVERY value binding: a re-exported runtime const compiles fine for authors but emits `undefined`, so `plugin.on(pluginId, CHANNEL)` silently subscribes to nothing
summary: packages/plugin-sdk/src/index.ts's `export type * from ...` strips all value bindings at emit — PLUGIN_PROCESS_STREAM_CHANNEL type-checked for authors but resolved to undefined at runtime, so plugin.on(pluginId, CHANNEL) silently subscribed to nothing with zero compile error. Fix: explicit named value re-export at every export-type layer, plus `as const` to preserve the literal type through .d.ts emit; type tests (expectTypeOf) can't catch value erasure, only a runtime typeof assertion can.

title: A regression guard that can't assert anything is not coverage: PR #10508's own E2E spec for the switch-back garble bug was deleted mid-PR for having no real assertions, and WebGL-off E2E can't reach the bug's worst variant anyway
summary: PR #10508 (project-switch terminal-garble hardening, arc with #10488) added e2e/full/worktree/core-project-switch-redraw.spec.ts + fixture fake-claude-agent.cjs + bridge global __daintreeProposeTerminalDimensions on TerminalInstanceService, then deleted the spec and fixtures 90 minutes later in the same PR (commit message: 'no real assertions') -- a live instance of CLAUDE.md's own tautological-test rule at the E2E layer. Since e2e/ runs the DOM renderer with WebGL disabled, the deleted spec's WebGL-paint-staleness variant now has zero automated coverage. What survived as real regression protection: fake-timer behavioral unit tests on the reveal-backstop scheduling state machine (WorktreeStoreContext.scheduleWake.test.tsx, HelpPanel.revealBackstop.test.tsx) and a dev-only diagnostic, TerminalReconciliationWatchdog.diagnoseGeometryDivergence, that logs (never repairs) an xterm-grid-vs-container mismatch gated on import.meta.env?.DEV. __daintreeProposeTerminalDimensions itself outlived the deleted spec and was later reused by core-terminal-divider-resize.spec.ts.

title: The GitHub forge plugin has three parallel mapper families producing one Issue/PR contract, and each GraphQL node mapper is fed by several query builders projecting different field subsets — a field the mapper reads appears only for callers whose query fetched it, so fixing the mapper is necessary but not sufficient
summary: GitHub forge plugin's three parallel Issue/PR mapper families in plugins/builtin/github/main/mappers.ts (toForgeIssue/toForgePR, restToForgeIssue/restToForgePR, gitHubIssueToForgeIssue/gitHubPRToForgePR) diverged silently: the GraphQL node mappers dropped commentCount while the list-shape mappers carried it, and even after fixing the mapper, buildBatchBranchPRQuery in GitHubQueries.ts under-projected comments{totalCount} so findPRsByBranches still produced undefined counts. No type error surfaced since commentCount is optional and assembled via conditional spread. Fixed at both mapper and query layers; added present/zero/absent/malformed tests plus a query field-shape assertion to guard drift.

title: A cross-platform metric convention fixed in one service (#8646 workingSetSize-only) doesn't enforce itself — the sidebar memory badge still summed Windows-only privateBytes (0 on macOS/Linux) and rendered a failed read as a healthy '0 MB'
summary: electron/ipc/handlers/diagnostics.ts handleGetAppMetrics/ProjectResourceBadge: privateBytes is Windows-only in Electron.ProcessMetric (0, not undefined, elsewhere) so `privateBytes ?? workingSetSize` silently summed to 0 on macOS/Linux — the identical #8646 bug recurring in an un-grepped parallel call site. Fix reads workingSetSize unconditionally, adds an unavailable:true flag so a read failure never renders as a plausible '0 MB', and scales severity thresholds to total RAM.

title: Not every plugin-registered interface is equally boundary-proof: FileDecorationProvider proxies cleanly across the dev-worker MessagePort because provideDecorations is invoked async, while registerForgeProvider stays a permanent stub because parseRemote is consumed synchronously
summary: pluginDevWorkerHostProxy.ts/PluginDevWorkerMainBridge.ts: FileDecorationProvider.provideDecorations proxies over the dev-worker MessagePort (host awaits it), but ForgeProvider.parseRemote stays a permanent stub (host reads it synchronously - proxying returns a Promise, not a value). Plus reloadGeneration + identity-guarded disposer delete for worker-relayed registries.

title: A swallowed plugin-invoke rejection returns {ok:true} from run(), so ActionService fires action:dispatched and PluginActionAuditService writes a false 'success' audit row over the real failure — rethrow after the user-facing toast so the result contract stays truthful
summary: src/hooks/usePluginActions.ts caught a plugin invoke rejection, toasted it, then `return undefined` — ActionService.dispatch treats a resolved run() as success and fires action:dispatched, so PluginActionAuditService wrote a false success audit row over the real main-side error row. Fix: rethrow after the toast; useActionPalette suppresses its own generic toast only for pluginId-tagged EXECUTION_ERROR to avoid double-notify.

title: Two hardcoded copies of the high-risk plugin-capability set drifted despite a 'keep in lockstep' comment — one shared constant plus a drift-guard test that iterates the constant is the only enforcement
summary: shared/config/pluginCapabilities.ts: PluginService's action-danger set and PluginMcpTierAuth's MCP-cap set were separate hardcoded copies of the same high-risk-capability predicate, joined only by a 'keep in lockstep' comment; agent:register drifted, under-tiering an MCP capability. Fix: one exported CONFIRM_TRIGGERING_CAPABILITIES constant plus an it.each(...CONST) drift-guard test that iterates the real constant, not a pasted copy.

title: Repaint/unpause can't fix a stale terminal grid on project switch-back — the 5s resize lock silently swallows fit() and settled agents skip it, so only a lock-exempt atomic re-fit (reconcileGeometryFresh) ends the garble
summary: src/services/terminal/TerminalResizeController.ts: agent terminals returned from project switch-back with garbled line wrapping (stale column count), repeatedly 'fixed' with more repaint/unpause/atlas machinery (#10362 and others) that can never fix a wrong dimension. Root cause: the 5s post-switch resize lock makes fit() return null and fall back to PTY-only resize, and settled-strategy agents (Codex/Gemini/Cursor) skip fit() on wake entirely. Fix: reconcileGeometryFresh(id), a lock-exempt one-shot atomic xterm+PTY re-fit that measures the live box fresh via fitAddon.proposeDimensions(), backed by a timed backstop cadence.

title: Two 'efficiency' optimizations silently killed agent state detection: a cursor-anchored scan window misses TUI activity streamed ABOVE the input box, and a CDP-frozen renderer queues agent:state-changed in Mojo forever
summary: electron/services/pty/analysis/headlessViewport.ts + ProjectViewManager.ts: a cursor-anchored bottom-15-row activity scan missed TUI status lines rendered above the pinned input box (agent flips to false 'waiting'); separately CDP Page.setWebLifecycleState('frozen') suspends JS entirely so agent:state-changed queues in Mojo forever on cached background views (throttle, don't freeze, views with a live agent). regression_of #10426.

title: Plugins share one app://daintree JS realm, so plugin:invoke can't bind an invocation to a sender — the only honest ownership guarantee is rejecting unloaded pluginIds at the dispatchHandler chokepoint, not the IPC entry
summary: electron/services/PluginService.ts dispatchHandler: all plugins render in one shared app://daintree WebContents/JS realm, so plugin:invoke can't bind a call to a sender identity. Fix throws PluginInvokeOwnershipError for unloaded pluginIds at the single dispatchHandler chokepoint (covers dev-worker/agent callers too, not just IPC). Also: schema fields validated-but-unconsumed are a frozen-promise violation (cut or wire, never freeze); Symbol error-tagging across catch boundaries must degrade gracefully on frozen/primitive errors.

title: A module-scope 'subscribe once' latch that a useEffect cleanup resets isn't once-only — for an app-lifetime IPC broadcast listener the reset re-arms re-subscription and a remount fires every notification twice; make the latch one-way and set it only AFTER a successful subscribe
summary: Notification hooks (useIdleTerminalNotifications, useHibernationNotifications, useDiskSpaceWarnings, PostHydrationListeners) guarded IPC subscription with a module-scope latch that useEffect cleanup reset, so remounts re-subscribed a second ipcRenderer.on handler and fired every toast twice past notify()'s coalesce window. Fix: one-way latch set after subscribe; useErrors.ts still unfixed, latent.

title: Electron 42 sandboxed preload flag detection must OR both process.argv (additionalArguments) AND an exact process.env check — neither channel alone reaches a sandboxed WebContentsView preload reliably across OS/CI
summary: electron/preload.cts E2E-flag detection under sandbox:true. process.env is polyfilled but drops individual vars per-OS, so main threads argv switches via webPreferences.additionalArguments (resolveE2EPreloadArgs in skeletonCss.ts, wired in createWindow/ProjectViewFactory/SurfaceViewManager). But Electron 42 local WebContentsView preloads can also omit those argv switches — so #10454's argv-only fix regressed local Playwright; the robust form (runtimeFlags.ts) ORs argv||env with exact ==='1' match and a !isPackagedBuild (app.asar) gate.

title: A reactive layout predicate observed the transient mid-mutation state of a multi-step store action (addTabForPanel) and crashed: two single-panel groups — one explicit, one virtual — satisfied useTwoPaneSplitMode; fix hardened the predicate, not the mutation
summary: Panel grid crash (#10438): addTabForPanel in useContentGridContext.tsx is a multi-step Zustand mutation (createTabGroup explicit group → await addPanel → addPanelToGroup); between the writes React re-renders and getTabGroups() returns one explicit singleton (id=tabgroup-uuid) plus one virtual singleton (id===panelId), which the useTwoPaneSplitMode predicate mistook for two ungrouped panels and activated TwoPaneSplitLayout against an already-grouped panel, crashing the renderer. Fixed by adding allGroupsAreVirtual (g.id===g.panelIds[0]) to harden the derived predicate against the transient shape rather than making the mutation atomic; e2e previously disabled split via localStorage to dodge it.

title: A debounced hover-prefetch with a click/leave cancel defeats itself: the fast hover→click it exists to accelerate lands inside the debounce window, the click cancels the request, and the dropdown mounts cold — and forcing bypassCache per hover makes it a GraphQL quota leak
summary: ForgeStatsToolbarButton's hover-to-prefetch used a 150ms trailing-edge setTimeout with pointerleave/unmount clearTimeout and forced bypassCache:true — so the dominant hover→click flow cancelled the prefetch (dropdown mounted cold) and every hover spent a GraphQL query, ignoring the 60s main-process list cache.
