Fix: fire prefetchResourceList synchronously on pointerenter (mouse-only), cache-first (bypassCache:false), omit freshBypassAt (SWR FRESH_REVALIDATE_SKIP_MS marker, real-bypass only), bound cost via in-flight refs + PREFETCH_FRESHNESS_MS; cap GitHubStatsDropdown's lazy-chunk requestIdleCallback preload at {timeout:2000} so first click can't hit a Suspense skeleton. #11087 later added a stale-entry bypass for correctness.

title: Restore that regenerates a panel id (PTY reconnect timeout) silently orphans persisted structures keyed to the old id — hydrateTabGroups drops the dead member, collapses the group to ≤1, and PERSISTS the loss; remap saved→restored ids before hydration
summary: stateHydration: a PTY panel whose reconnect times out respawns with a fresh generated id (statePatcher.ts:619 requestedId undefined), but persisted tab groups still reference the old saved id. hydrateTabGroups (tabGroups.ts:644-680) filters the dead member, drops groups with finalPanelIds.length<=1, and saveTabGroups (tabGroups.ts:768-769) persists the shrunk result on the happy path (only the catch path uses skipPersist) — permanent silent membership loss. Fix threads a sparse savedIdToRestoredId map (identity mappings excluded) out of restorePanelsPhase and remaps panelIds/activeTabId in index.ts before hydrateTabGroups runs. Companion #10450: addPanelToGroup returned void + console.warn on reject, orphaning create-then-add-then-focus panels; now returns a boolean read from get() canonical-store membership (tabGroups.ts:214), callers trashPanel the orphan.

title: Stopping pointerdown does NOT block a mousedown-based dnd-kit sensor, and a handler rendered before a {...listeners} spread is silently clobbered — disarm foreign sensors with [data-no-dnd] and compose activators AFTER the spread
summary: TabButton tab-drag co-armed the parent panel-move drag (#10443): a pointerdown stopPropagation guard cannot stop the mousedown-based NoDndMouseSensor (separate event families), and was clobbered anyway by the sortableListeners spread rendered after it (React last-prop-wins). Fix: [data-no-dnd] on PanelTabList plus composed handlers after the spread.

title: The dock drives terminal refresh tiers by hand because the portal-relocated wrapper escapes the IntersectionObserver — so every imperative VISIBLE upgrade must pair a BACKGROUND downgrade of the panel it displaced, or the hidden tab keeps painting at active tier behind the popover
summary: DockedTabGroup/DockedTerminalItem drive refresh tiers imperatively; relocated wrapper (moveToDestination) escapes IntersectionObserver. Tab switch upgrades new panel to VISIBLE, never downgrades outgoing — stale VISIBLE holds PTY poll at 200ms, inflates WebGL want-count toward 12-context DOM-fallback. Fix: prevActivePanelIdRef pairs upgrade+downgrade.

title: A persisted agentLaunchFlags snapshot is a security-flag time capsule: a bypass flag injected at spawn replays forever on restore/resume, so any global that injects a CLI flag must strip-and-reconcile against the live setting at every relaunch chokepoint
summary: #10437's global skip-permissions toggle (onboarding #10453): the bypass token baked into a session's persisted agentLaunchFlags at spawn replays verbatim on every restart/restore/palette-resume, so disabling the global left old sessions still bypassing permission prompts. Fix = reconcileBypassFlags/resolveEffectiveBypass in shared/types/agentSettings.ts strip-and-reconcile the canonical token at every relaunch chokepoint (restart.ts, statePatcher.ts, agentResume.ts); idiom later cloned as reconcileInlineModeFlag for the alt-screen global (#10876).

title: Tailwind v4 opacity modifiers (`/50`) compile to `color-mix(in oklab, token N%, transparent)` and MULTIPLY into a token's baked-in alpha — on a low-alpha theme token (border-subtle ≈ rgba .09) the result underflows to invisible in Chromium
summary: Tailwind v4 compiles the `/N` opacity modifier to `color-mix(in oklab, token N%, transparent)`, a linear blend that multiplies into a token's existing alpha. `border-border-subtle/50` on atacama's `rgba(39,33,25,0.09)` (withAlpha fallback in shared/theme/themes.ts:196) yielded ~4.5% effective alpha, rendering the QuickRun.tsx input border invisible over near-white `--dock-input-bg` and failing the light-theme smoke E2E (core-light-theme-smoke.spec.ts, quickRunFieldBorderContrast < 1.02 floor). Silent — no type/lint/build error. Fix: never stack opacity modifiers on alpha-carrying tokens; use pre-baked tokens (since hardened further to border-border-default, QuickRun.tsx:397). Live secondary hazards: src/index.css panel-state-compiling rings color-mix border-subtle at 8-10% (same underflow, lines 1911-1915); e2e/helpers/theme.ts parseColor() opaque-black fallback (line 139) masks regressions.

title: Statement-level try/catch/finally, raw dynamic import(), and ++ counters silently bail React Compiler for the WHOLE enclosing component/hook — but forcing compilation is wrong for hooks that read untracked store state (getState()) or refs at render: those keep 'use no memo'
summary: React Compiler bailout traps from the full-codebase perf audit (#10426; siblings #10402/#10405/#10409/#10411). A statement-level try/catch/finally, a raw dynamic import(), or a ++/-- increment disables memoization for the ENTIRE enclosing component/hook, not the expression — churned useContentGridContext's 40-field ctx per grid render; fix is hoisting to module scope (addTabForPanel, const load=()=>import, module-let counters). Conversely, hooks on the #8593 narrow-subscribe/wide-panelStoreApi.getState() pattern or render-time ref.current reads (useColdNumberGap #8079) MUST keep 'use no memo' — compiling caches derivations against untracked state and freshly-spawned panels never render. Coverage tracked in scripts/baselines/compiler-bailout-baseline.json via check-compiler-budget.mjs (build-gated, not in npm run check/CI). Bundling twin #10405: Vite catch-all vendor group needs entriesAware to keep lazy-only deps deferred.

title: A detached WebContentsView gets no resize events and its setBounds()/ResizeObservers stay silent, so backgrounded terminals wrap at stale PTY width — forward settled bounds over IPC (queued Mojo delivery survives freezing, no wake) and scale each PTY from a session-anchored snapshot so repeated resizes never compound
summary: Detached WebContentsViews get no resize events or ResizeObserver firing, so backgrounded terminals wrap at stale PTY width. ProjectViewManager.notifyBackgroundResize forwards debounced bounds over project:background-resize IPC to frozen views; TerminalInstanceService scales PTYs from a session-anchored snapshot to absolute targets, avoiding compounding across resizes.

title: Two parallel writes (store + service) must share the attach-generation guard: a warm-swap's stale unmount cleanup poisoned the unguarded store write, and the watchdog looped forever because its repair re-applied the renderer tier without touching the divergent store source
summary: TerminalPane writes visibility to panelStore.updateVisibility and terminalInstanceService.setVisible in parallel; only setVisible had an attach-generation guard, so a warm-swap stale unmount cleanup poisoned panelStore.isVisible=false, pinning getTerminalRefreshTier at BACKGROUND (panelStore.ts:160) and looping TerminalReconciliationWatchdog every ~6s.

title: Cached project views have no replay path on warm reactivation (#9490): only REPLAYABLE broadcasts (log batches, re-pullable via LOGS_GET_ALL) may skip them via broadcastToVisibleRenderers — state broadcasts must stay on broadcastToRenderer; and per-window aligned-interval samplers thunder-herd the main thread
summary: Cached/LRU-deactivated project views have no replay path on warm reactivation (#9490): only replayable broadcasts (log batches via LOGS_GET_ALL) skip them via broadcastToVisibleRenderers/isCachedViewWebContents — state broadcasts stay on broadcastToRenderer or the V8 context desyncs. Also: jittered per-window getAppMetrics samplers, PortalManager throttle not freeze.

title: Regex captures over multi-MB `ps` stdout stay V8 SlicedStrings that pin the whole slab in a long-lived cache — only a `Buffer.from(str).toString()` round-trip forces the flat copy; String()/concat/template literals keep the parent alive
summary: V8 caches regex/slice/substring captures as SlicedStrings pinning the parent buffer: ProcessTreeCache.parseUnixLine caching a 10-char comm from multi-MB ps stdout retains the whole slab until Buffer.from(str).toString() forces a flat copy. Sibling fixes: FNV-1a digest, capped acknowledgedMutations, GitServiceCache eviction, byte-scan counting.

title: electron-store v11 (conf) has NO read cache — every store.get() re-reads and re-parses config.json from disk; the Proxy-level lazy snapshot fix only works because main is the sole writer, and it must structuredClone object returns + invalidate before every mutation AND on the restoreFromBackup file-swap
summary: electron-store v11 (conf) in electron/store.ts has NO read cache — every store.get() re-parses ~35KB config.json, every set() re-serializes it. #10408 adds a lazy Proxy snapshot (storeValueCache): structuredClone on object returns, invalidate before set/delete/clear/reset, plus invalidateStoreValueCache() for MigrationRunner.restoreFromBackup's file-swap — sound only because main is the sole writer. Also batches handleAppSetState (v11 throws on undefined) and migration 023 moves audit rings to the lazy audit-logs store.

title: Import deferrals rot silently: an eager handler barrel re-anchors the singleton its handlers value-import, a lone constant drags its whole dep onto boot, and only the eager-import baseline count catches it
summary: Boot-perf: eager barrel handlers.ts value-imports PluginService via plugin.ts/pluginMcp.ts; a bare MAX_DNTR_BYTES constant drags yauzl; MCP SDK types.js builds zod schemas at import — three edges re-anchoring deferred modules pre-paint. Fix: cached await-import accessors + zero-dep constants; baseline count (1227->935->817) is the sole CI-absent guard.

title: xterm 6.1 Terminal.dispose() tears down listeners/DOM but never frees the 15-50MB CircularList/BufferSet buffer graph — it stays GC-reachable while ANY reference survives (including addons' loadAddon-time _terminal back-refs); reclaim = snapshot-then-dispose-then-drop-every-reference
summary: xterm 6.1.0-beta.221 (repo pin has since moved to beta.290) Terminal.dispose() never nulls the 15-50MB CircularList/BufferSet buffer graph; it stays GC-reachable while any reference survives, including addons' loadAddon-time _terminal back-refs. Reclaim (PreservedSnapshotCapture/serializeTerminal, TerminalProcess.ts): SerializeAddon.serialize once into a cached preservedSnapshot, drain the parser queue via headlessMirrorScheduler.flush, disposeHeadless, serve the string from serializeTerminal/serializeTerminalAsync. #10407 hibernation placeholder-swap variant removed by #10811. Also: terminal.options is a live proxy dispose() half-nulls (linkHandler).

title: electron-builder strips the arch suffix from its default arch, so macOS x64 artifacts shipped as bare Daintree-X.Y.Z.dmg and masqueraded as THE Mac download — restore -x64 via explicit artifactName, and Rosetta detection must be Darwin-gated since Windows ARM sets the same flag
summary: electron-builder's getArchSuffix renders empty for the default macOS arch (x64), so x64 dmg/zip shipped unsuffixed and Apple Silicon users ran them under Rosetta. Fix in electron-builder.config.cjs: explicit artifactName with ${arch} on mac/dmg blocks (never mac.defaultArch, which renames release/mac/ and breaks release-macos.yml paths); zip keeps -mac suffix so generate-update-metadata.mjs macZipPriority ranks -x64-mac.zip above legacy bare -mac.zip; MacUpdater routes by arm64 substring. #10399 Darwin-gates isRunningUnderRosetta()/app.runningUnderARM64Translation since Windows ARM WOW64 sets it too.

title: macOS Dock clicks fire `activate` before `app.whenReady()` resolves — DROP the pre-ready event with a synchronous `app.isReady()` guard; DEFERring via `whenReady().then()` double-creates the initial window
summary: electron/lifecycle/appLifecycle.ts activate handler threw Cannot create BrowserWindow before app is ready when macOS Dock clicks fired pre-ready during slow startup (#10381). Fix: synchronous app.isReady() guard before window enumeration/creation, not whenReady().then() -- main.ts already unconditionally creates the initial window there, so deferring double-creates.

title: Coalescing per-chunk agent:output into 50ms batches is only correct because every batch is force-flushed synchronously BEFORE any agent state transition — the turn-outcome classifier reads a per-terminal output ring synchronously at the FSM transition, so a still-pending batch would make it classify the state before the output that explains it
summary: pty-host coalesces agent:output into 50ms batches via AgentOutputForwarder; flushAgentOutput() must run before every TerminalProcess agent-state transition (~8 sites) since TurnOutcomeService.recentOutput reads sync at each FSM transition or agent-stuck/reasoning-loop misclassifies. Also: SemanticBufferManager/ActivityMonitor cooling caps, ReviewHub cache-invalidation.

title: Two silent Tailwind-v4 traps in Daintree's @theme: bare `rounded` jumped 4px→10px (checkboxes read as radios), and stock palette classes (amber/emerald/red-NNN) render nothing because `--color-*: initial` wiped them
summary: Daintree's Tailwind v4 `@theme inline` (src/index.css) hides two silent traps from PR #10374: bare `rounded` resolves to `--radius`=10px (line 176, not v3's 4px) so a 14px checkbox reads as a radio; `--color-*: initial` (line 34) deletes the stock palette so `text-amber-500`/`emerald`/`red`/`blue` render nothing -- use `status-*` tokens instead.

title: An IPC invoke's outcome can't be inferred from progress-event timing — the reply races the webContents.send pushes at the renderer; carry an explicit outcome discriminant, never named ok/success (ForbidIpcEnvelopeKeys/#6020)
summary: GitInitDialog inferred git-init success from sawTerminalEventRef (did a project:init-git-progress push arrive?) rather than the initGitGuided invoke reply — which races the sendToRenderer/webContents.send pushes as an independent transport, so a successful init flashed a sticky failure banner (#10361). Fix adds a GitInitResult.outcome discriminant, named outcome not ok/success because ForbidIpcEnvelopeKeys/#6020 bans envelope keys the security wrapper swallows, plus a sawErrorEventRef guard so late complete/success events clear stale errors without masking real failures.

title: Adding a bail-out state read to an effect's dep array to silence exhaustive-deps inverts the effect — crashState in the DevPreview URL-clear effect made it self-fire and wipe crash banners before they rendered
summary: DevPreview crash/unresponsive banners self-cleared before rendering: lint fix 11f2d99fe (PR #8338) added crashState to the [currentUrl]-only navigation-clear effect's deps, so setting crashState re-fired it while currentUrl was still a live proxy URL and reset it to 'none'. react-hooks/exhaustive-deps can't tell a bail-out guard read from a trigger; fix removes the read via a lastClearedCrashUrlRef URL-transition gate (now in useDevPreviewCrashRecovery.ts, mirroring BrowserPane). Also adds eviction crash-clear + persistence tests.

title: Coalescing a page-lifecycle wake via Promise.resolve() runs the fan-out before the thawed renderer's first layout pass — xterm reads stale geometry and garbles line wrapping; the settle primitive is double-rAF, not a microtask
summary: scheduleWake in WorktreeStoreContext coalesced the resume+visibilitychange page-lifecycle wake via a Promise.resolve() microtask (#9704) that drained before the thawed renderer's first layout pass, so fullWakeForVisibilityRestore→applyDeferredResize→terminal.refresh() read stale geometry while xterm's IntersectionObserver/RenderService were still paused — garbling agent-terminal line wrapping until a click re-fit (issue #10362). Fix: double-requestAnimationFrame settle (warmReactivationGate idiom), visibilityState recheck in the inner rAF, and cancelAnimationFrame on effect cleanup + app:view-cached so evicted views can't fire a stale wake. Later hardening adds a separate scheduleRepaint gate + timed backstops because double-rAF settles layout but doesn't defeat #9679 anti-flash paint culling.

title: The GitHub plugin has parallel mappers over the same LIST_PRS_QUERY node (toForgePR vs parsePRNode→gitHubPRToForgePR); when the list mapper omits a field the query already fetches, a refresh silently downgrades the richer cached data
summary: GitHub forge plugin toForgePR (mappers.ts) never read node.commits.statusCheckRollup.state though LIST_PRS_QUERY fetches it; parsePRNode to gitHubPRToForgePR did, so PR-dropdown CI icons flashed from cache then vanished on refresh. Node is untyped Record<string,unknown>, so no type error; fix maps rollup via mapListCIStatus, conditional-spread. Regression of #10347.

title: xterm 6.x has no scrollback prepend/inject API — lazy-loading older history into a live terminal needs reset()+full re-replay (≡ just holding a bigger buffer), so the only lever for deeper agent scrollback is widening the renderer window
summary: Terminal scrollback: xterm 6.1.0-beta.290 exposes only write()/clear()/reset() and a read-only buffer namespace (no prepend/inject/insertLines), so lazy-loading older history from the main-process mirror into a live xterm on scroll-to-top is impossible without reset()+full re-replay — equivalent to a bigger buffer. #10352 floated lazy-load; #10356 correctly rejected it and raised AGENT_POLICY.multiplier 1.5→5 in src/utils/scrollbackConfig.ts (getScrollbackForType), later 5→10/maxLines 10000 via #11223. Renderer window (10000) and pty-host mirror DEFAULT_SCROLLBACK (5000) are separate; restored-after-eviction sessions recover only ~5000. Unfocused terminals trimmed to SCROLLBACK_BACKGROUND=500 keep the wider focused ceiling affordable (~1200 bytes/line).

title: The diff viewer hides four render traps: refractor v4+ returns a hast Root that silently kills react-diff-view tokenization (adapter must unwrap .children), the lib's edit-pill :root colors are GitHub-light hex unreadable on dark, Chromium detaches sticky-gutter borders under border-collapse, and the diff cache key must carry the ignore-whitespace flag
summary: Diff viewer (#10354+#10349): refractor v4+ returns a hast Root not an array, tokenize throws, catch nulls tokens -> silent plaintext diffs, zero error; fix = refractorAdapter unwraps .children + console.warn. Also: edit-pill colors GitHub-light on dark; Chromium detaches sticky-gutter borders under border-collapse; diffCacheKey must carry ignoreWhitespace.

title: Re-stamping lastUpdated when a cheap 'unchanged' probe re-serves a cached count makes stale data impersonate a fresh read — it wins recency arbitration AND suppresses the refresh that would heal it
summary: Toolbar forge count badge (GitHubStats.ts/GitHubPRs.ts/GitHubCaches.ts) oscillates to stale: /events unchanged-probe re-serves cached counts but re-stamps lastUpdated=now, so resolveForgeDisplayCount picks stale over a fresher dropdown read and suppresses the healing force-refresh. Fix: per-count issueCountRefreshedAt/prCountRefreshedAt advance only on a real read/304.

title: Cold-start regressions hide in silent boot-path seams: module-entry `dom-ready` waits for the whole bundle to evaluate, rolldown chunk groups capture a module's dependency closure by priority (React dragged 451KB of CodeMirror onto every boot), and a side-effect-only import is tree-shaken from prod unless it's in `sideEffects`
summary: Cold-start #10346, four silent boot-path traps that pass CI green: Electron `dom-ready` on a `<script type=module>` entry fires only after the whole module graph evaluates (fix: classic `public/skeleton-ready.js`->`APP_SKELETON_PARSED` reveal in createWindow.ts); rolldown `advancedChunks` groups capture a dep's full closure by priority, so `vendor-editor` (60) swept React in and dragged 451KB CodeMirror onto every boot (fix: pin `vendor-react` at priority 80, plus exclude `@lezer/lr`); a side-effect-only import `src/lib/bootIpcEager.ts` is tree-shaken from the prod bundle unless listed in package.json `sideEffects`; sync `config.json` bootstrap read scaled boot cost with MCP audit-ring volume (moved to lazy `auditLogsStore`, migration v22). Also: V8 compile hints honored only on chunk line 1 via generateBundle order:post.

title: A plugin disable toggle only flips persisted state — it removes nothing unless every host surface gates at the point of USE, not at wiring time: IPC handlers register unconditionally and renderer slots resolve at render
summary: daintree.github disable toggle (#10343) only wrote persisted state; github:* IPC handlers and renderer slots resolved unconditionally, so disabling removed nothing. Fix gates at USE: builtinRendererRegistry+useBuiltinView reads pluginRuntimeStore.disabledPluginIds (fail-open); IPC gates via resolveForCwd throwing (fail-closed). #10347 deleted github:* for forge:* channels.

title: Node ESM has no module-cache eviction - hot-reload a plugin by respawning a utilityProcess.fork worker per rebuild, not unimport+reimport; and Electron 42 only WARNS on a utility process's unhandledRejection, so a throwing activate() hangs the parent's waitForReady() unless the worker forces its own exit
summary: PluginService dev-plugin hot-reload (#10340/#9304): Node ESM has no import() cache-eviction API (Vite #14438), so unimport+reimport leaks module-scope state - fix is to run the plugin in a utilityProcess.fork worker (PluginDevWorkerHost) and kill+respawn per dist/index.js rebuild. Electron 37+/42 only WARNS on utility-process unhandledRejection/uncaughtException, so a throwing activate() or failed dynamic import hangs waitForReady() forever unless the bootstrap installs a process.exit(1) guard (installBootstrapErrorGuard, shared with pty-host/workspace-host). Live built-in enable/disable serializes per-id via an enableTransitions promise chain; reload clears the crash window so it isn't counted as a crash. Symbols since generalized: activateViaDevWorker/devWorkers -> activateViaWorker/pluginWorkers, plus mode:prod.

title: Three #10339 'responsiveness' ideas self-defeated: a document-level View Transition on grid-maximize left the next tab-close uncommitted, a constant view-transition-name collides in keep-mounted dialog handoffs, and synchronous optimistic row-reorder breaks the keyboard-focus contract
summary: PR #10339 responsiveness arc: withViewTransition (src/lib/viewTransition.ts) is safe for dock-restore/dialog swaps, but a document-level VT on GridPanel toggleMaximize left a later panel tab-close uncommitted (reverted f9045f693, repro'd in core-panel-tab-groups e2e); a constant view-transition-name collides when old+new dialogs coexist in keep-mounted handoffs; synchronous optimistic row-reorder breaks the #9215 Review-hub keyboard-focus contract. Safe subset = property-only optimism (projectStore rename/emoji, fleet.deleteNamedFleet) + captureBufferText tail-scan + scheduler.yield.

title: SharedArrayBuffer can't cross the Electron UtilityProcess postMessage boundary ('could not be cloned'), so the entire SAB zero-copy terminal path — including the renderer semantic-analysis Worker — is dead in production; getAnalysisBuffer() is hardcoded null and the FUTURE_SAB skeleton is intentional
summary: SharedArrayBuffer can't cross the Electron UtilityProcess postMessage boundary (Chromium 'could not be cloned'), so the pty-host SAB zero-copy path is dead in production; PtyClient.getAnalysisBuffer/getSharedBuffers/isSharedBufferEnabled hardcode null/empty/false. SemanticAnalysisService.doInitialize spawned a renderer Web Worker before awaiting the always-null analysis buffer, terminating it every boot; fix reorders the precondition check first. FUTURE_SAB skeleton (backpressure caps, SharedRingBuffer, pty-host Priority-2 branch) is intentional dead code, not deletable; agent detection lives in pty-host AgentStateService.

title: Demo/screenshot E2E on hosted macOS runners: getDisplayMedia can't source a 4K frame from a ~885-tall virtual display, parallel cold Electron launches fight over the crashpad Mach port, and a Playwright project sweeps every spec in its testDir into one gate
summary: Playwright project = testDir: `screenshots` swept demo-reel.spec.ts in, reddening Marketing Screenshots despite clean PNGs. macos-14 traps: ~885px display can't yield 2160px getDisplayMedia, parallel Electron cold-launches fight the crashpad Mach port, /tmp fixture races. Fix (#10334/#10337): dedicated `demo` project, workers:1, strict-dims gate, off publish.needs.

title: requiresArgs answers 'does the schema reject {}', not 'can run() work with no inputs' — the palette gated on it and dispatched all-optional/run()-gated actions with {}, breaking them or silently bypassing D1 confirms; fix is a palette-only PaletteBehavior field, never a tighter schema
summary: useActionPalette listed kind==='command' && !requiresArgs and dispatched picks with {}, but computeRequiresArgs (ActionService) is true only when the Zod argsSchema rejects BOTH undefined and {} — so all-optional/.refine()/run()-context-gated actions report requiresArgs:false, leak into the palette, and throw, no-op, or bypass component-wired danger:'confirm' D1 dialogs (source:'user' is ungated). Audit found 18. Fixed by a palette-only PaletteBehavior (hidden/redirect/requireContext) on ActionDefinition, projected in toManifestEntry to paletteHidden/paletteRedirectTo/paletteDisabled and consumed only by useActionPalette; dispatch()/get()/MCP ignore it.

title: Electron protocol.handle() freezes its handler closure at registration — make a resolver hot-swappable via a module-scoped indirection that reads a mutable variable live, never unhandle/re-handle (that opens an ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME gap)
summary: electron/setup/protocols.ts plugin:// scheme: protocol.handle freezes the resolver closure, so to defer the ~2900-line PluginService off the app.whenReady()→createWindow first-paint path, register early with a placeholder () => undefined resolver but wire the handler to a module-scoped resolvePluginDir indirection reading cachedGetPluginDir live; the deferred plugin-service task calls setPluginDirResolver to mutate cachedGetPluginDir, reaching every already-registered default- and per-session handler without unhandle/re-handle (which would ERR_UNKNOWN_URL_SCHEME). registerProtocolsForSession gates per-view handlers on cachedGetPluginDir; swap stays unconditional on init failure; restored plugin panels may 404 first asset, self-heal via PluginViewHost ErrorBoundary.

title: Daintree's deferred-init drain serially awaits each task's returned Promise — a task that returns a thenable gates the whole queue, and sync fs inside one task freezes the entire main loop, not just the queue
summary: Deferred-init drain (drainNext, electron/window/deferredInitQueue.ts) serially awaits any Promise a task's run() returns; an awaited GitHubAuth.validate() bounded by AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) stalled ~30 successors (monitors/MCP/plugins) on slow networks — fix floats it via void(async()=>{})() returning undefined, guarded by a versionAtStart epoch token + own .catch(). Separately, sync readdirSync/statSync/unlinkSync in prune-old-logs froze the whole main loop (setImmediate yields only between tasks); pruneOldLogsAsync uses fs/promises opendir+for-await to yield mid-scan, sync twin kept for DiskSpaceMonitor. github-auth callsite later moved into the github builtin forge plugin.

title: A dimension restored by async IPC after mount, with its CSS transition live from first paint, replays the restore as a spurious animation — gate the class on a hydrating flag cleared in the SAME post-await continuation (React 19 batches it, no flushSync); transitionend never fires while suppressed
summary: AppLayout sidebar width restores via async appClient.getState() ~50-100ms after mount while transition-[width] is live from first paint, so setSidebarWidth animates from default 350px on every project switch (#10321). Fix: an isSidebarWidthHydrating useState(true) flag gates the class, cleared in the same post-await batch so React 19 commits width+flag in one paint (no flushSync, unlike the #7627 drag-start path). transitionend never fires while suppressed, so the flag is OR'd into #9864's sidebarFullyHidden clip-margin flush guard; clear it in catch/null branches or suppression becomes permanent; #10827 reused the flag to release the grid-measurement lock (unlockSidebarHydration).

title: The cast replay harness pinned its own ActivityMonitor options (simpleOutputState:false + 6000ms) and validated a detection path production never runs — derive harness config from buildActivityMonitorOptions, don't re-declare it
summary: castReplayHarness.ts pinned simpleOutputState:false + 6000ms debounce instead of buildActivityMonitorOptions (production: true/8000ms), omitting getVisibleContentSnapshot and OSC 9;4 routing — all 8 .expected.json fixtures validated a branch no real agent exercises. Fix derives options from the builder, wires Osc94Parser/Unicode11Addon, adds a differential OSC test; supersedes #10306.

title: A fresh xterm's serialize() returns '' → null, the same sentinel a genuine snapshot drop produces, so inferring 'output lost' from a null wake snapshot drew a false data-loss marker on every agent startup; disambiguate the absence, or route real loss through a dedicated signal (OSC 57301)
summary: Terminal wake/restore sentinel ambiguity: a fresh xterm serialize() returns '' → coerced by PtyEventRouter to null, indistinguishable from a genuine host snapshot drop; #9894's null-state branch (noteDecline(id,true) + removed isAltBuffer guard) drew a false 'Output dropped (output)' marker on every agent start (droppedBytes===0 label is the tell). Fix added an everWoken lifetime flag on ManagedTerminal and routed real loss to the OSC 57301 signal (#8375). TerminalWakeManager/everWoken/noteDecline later deleted by hibernation removal (#10811); injectDataLossMarker/drawDataLossMarker in TerminalInstanceService.ts now driven only by the window-scoped data-loss pulse in lifecycle.ts.

title: Per-terminal xterm buffer memory is a free closed-form estimate (lines×cols×12) — rank heaviest-first for graduated pre-pause reclaim, but keep the ≥95% panic path uniform-global and never rank by the scrollback cap
summary: pty-host ResourceGovernor per-terminal memory attribution (resolves #9904): estimate xterm headless-buffer footprint as lines×cols×12 (3 uint32s/cell, BYTES_PER_CELL) via getTerminalBufferSizes; performPrePauseTrim ranks heaviest-first and trims only terminals over SCROLLBACK_MIN in the warning band while the ≥95% critical path stays uniform-global trimBuffers(). Rank by actual bufferLines (getActualBufferLines, added by a7ddd3027), not the scrollback cap. buffer-memory-gauge stays pure observability. Live baseline that #10948 was reverted back to (see 10948.md).

title: Mutating a fetched project-settings snapshot and saving it back is a lost-update race — fold every settings mutation through useProjectSettingsStore's atomic setState updater, mirroring the recipeStore frecency path
summary: fleetActions.ts recall/saveNamedFleet did read-modify-write on getSettings() IPC snapshots, dropping concurrent lastUsedAt/usageHistory stamps and fleetSavedScopes appends. Fix: atomic useProjectSettingsStore.setState updaters (findFleetScope, appendFleetScopeInMemory, stampFleetUsageInMemory) mirroring recipeStore.ts; never setSettings(wholeObject) after an await.

title: Renderer↔pty-host flow control is strict two-sided byte accounting: a renderer teardown that outlives its host terminal must batch-ack its held port FIFO or queuedBytes keeps a permanent deficit that degrades every later pause to the 10s safety timeout
summary: Renderer↔pty-host flow-control ledger: a renderer destroy outliving its host terminal (project close, LRU evict) must batch-ack via discardPortAcks or queuedBytes keeps a permanent deficit, degrading every backpressure pause to the 10s force-resume (#9910); kill/trash just delete the FIFO since the host dies too. Ties to xterm dispose gaps and the #10811 hibernation removal.

title: A persisted opt-in map keyed by a reusable path must be pruned at every removal path AND self-healed owner-scoped (the map is global); serializing tri-state eligibility as `bool || undefined` collapses 'ineligible' into 'unprobed'
summary: Persisted WSL-git opt-in map wslGitByWorktree (electron/store.ts), keyed by a reusable filesystem path, was write-only — recreating a worktree on a recycled path silently re-inherited WSL git routing with no banner; fix funnels all removals through one removeMonitor chokepoint + a project-scoped pruneStaleWslGitEntries self-heal (the map is a single global electron-store key, so a naive heal erases other projects' opt-ins). Sibling #10264: wslGitEligible serialized as bool||undefined collapsed 'ineligible' into 'unprobed', fixed with a WslGitEligibility three-state union + 60s distro poll + wslProbeSeq supersede guard.

title: Terminal-recovery UI was dead in production because its events shared the pty-host reliability-metric funnel and inherited a DAINTREE_TERMINAL_METRICS gate nothing sets — split load-bearing signal types from gated diagnostics at the funnel
summary: pty-host funnel emitReliabilityMetricWithTracking gated recovery events (pause-start/end/suspend/pause-duration-gauge) behind the DAINTREE_TERMINAL_METRICS flag it shared with diagnostic gauges; nothing sets that env var, so the Tier-3 stall banner (useForceResumeCycleWatchdog) and held-duration tooltip were dead in production. Fix splits the funnel via isLoadBearingReliabilityMetric (loadBearingMetrics.ts) — load-bearing types emit unconditionally, diagnostics stay gated. Also force-resume read pause-start from SAB-only getPauseStartTime, non-functional in Electron utilityProcess (#7030).

title: A Node memory governor keyed to V8 heap utilization (heapUsed/heap_size_limit) is blind to `external` memory where xterm typed-array buffers and queued PTY slabs actually live (~10:1 external:heap) — bind pressure to max((heap+external)/process-budget, heap/heap-cap)
summary: pty-host ResourceGovernor measured only heapUsed/heap_size_limit, blind to external memory where xterm typed arrays and queued PTY slabs live (~10:1 external:heap) — RSS climbed but warn/engage/critical never tripped. #10302 binds pressure to max((heapUsed+external)/768MB, heapUsed/512MB); external used raw, never +arrayBuffers (double-counts).

title: Agent-state detection = FSM + ActivityMonitor's private busy/idle over four detector layers; the simple-output mode fork (on for every agent) early-returned past all four, and external FSM promotion that skips the monitor strands the agent in 'working'
summary: ActivityMonitor's simple-output mode (default for every agent) early-returns past four detection layers, killing completed state, waitingReason, compiled patterns and the boot guard. #10300 rewires them; #10297 fixes external FSM promotion (TerminalProcess.noteAgentOutputActivity) stranding agents in working by requiring notifyExternalPromotion().

title: Module-scope Zustand cross-store subscriptions with a globalThis dedupe guard silently desync under HMR/vi.resetModules — the old sub keeps mutating orphaned store instances while fresh ones go unwired; register through rendererStoreOrchestrator with an initial reconciliation pass
summary: Fleet cross-store Zustand subs (arming-failure clear, target-override pruning, broadcast IPC) were wired at module scope behind a globalThis guard; HMR/vi.resetModules blocks re-wiring, so the orphaned sub mutates dead stores while live ones never fire (#9923/#9973/#9967). Fix: subscribeX() factories via rendererStoreOrchestrator + reconcile pass.

title: A read API that acknowledges 'seen' state as a side effect (getAuditStats → knownCombinations) is silently consumed by any background poller sharing it — thread a markSeen=false passive-read flag end-to-end so the poll surfaces the one-shot signal without eating it
summary: AuditService.getSignals/getAuditStats mutate knownCombinations (acknowledging first-seen-combination) as a read side effect, so the useMcpAnomalyStats poll feeding the toolbar assistant pip silently consumed that one-shot signal before Settings saw it. #10282 threads markSeen (default true, poll passes false) through McpServerService/IPC/generated.ts plus an emittedThisCall dedup.

title: React reuses a createPortal fiber only when the container NODE identity is stable (key is not enough) — park/reveal panels by portaling once into a permanent wrapper div and relocating that node with Chromium 148's atomic Node.moveBefore, never by swapping the portal target
summary: Dock panel park/reveal (DockPanelOffscreenContainer, DockedTabGroup, DockedTerminalItem): flipping createPortal's container between an offscreen slot and the popover div remounted the entire subtree twice per cycle because react-dom 19.2 updatePortal reuses a fiber only on identical containerInfo — a stable key isn't enough — killing TerminalPane state, CodeMirror, and forcing an imperative xterm reattach. Fix: portal forever into one permanent per-panel wrapper div (wrappersRef) and relocate that node via Chromium 148 Node.moveBefore (atomic, preserves WebGL/canvas/focus) with isConnected guard + appendChild fallback for HierarchyRequestError. Also: scalar activePanelId deps to avoid poll-driven focus-yank, and #11133 park-blur so aria-hidden offscreen panes don't eat keystrokes.

title: A rate gauge whose numerator is a snapshot-and-reset accumulator must divide by the FIXED poll window, never wall-clock-since-last-emission — idle gaps dilute the denominator and collapse bursts (10MB/2s after 60s idle read as ~165KB/s)
summary: pty-host ResourceGovernor's throughput-rate gauge (emitThroughputRateGauge/getThroughputSnapshot) divided a snapshot-and-reset byte accumulator by wall-clock-since-emission, not the fixed poll window; idle ticks emit null, so a stale timestamp made a 10MB/2s burst after 60s idle read ~165KB/s. #10279 fixed the divisor and pauseCount baseline advance, cleared in dispose().

title: Per-agent detection tunables are silently floored to the 8s #3606 jitter guard — sub-floor debounceMs/promptFastPathMinQuietMs are dead config, and empty pattern arrays fall through to the UNIVERSAL set (not opt-out) while dropping declared fallbacks
summary: Config audit (#10273/#9877): buildActivityMonitorOptions in terminalActivityPatterns.ts floors debounceMs/promptFastPathMinQuietMs to AGENT_WAITING_QUIET_MS=8000, so 17 per-agent 6000ms overrides were dead. Empty primaryPatterns makes buildPatternConfig return undefined, falling through to UNIVERSAL_PATTERN_CONFIG/BootDetector banners (not opt-out) and dropping fallbackPatterns.

title: A per-project poll lease can never deny under one-host-per-project pooling: WorkspaceHostPool makes holderId 1:1 with the lease key, so acquirePollLease's denial branch was unreachable — yet still cost an IPC round-trip + timeout every poll and spawned a phantom bug (#9978)
summary: Forge poll lease (forgePollLeaseService, #9077) elected one poller among sibling windows, but WorkspaceHostPool pools one host per project — holderId is 1:1 with the lease key, so acquirePollLease's denial branch was unreachable, yet cost an IPC round-trip + 5s timeout every poll and spawned phantom bug #9978. #10272 deleted it; singleflight remains.

title: ErrorBoundary resetKeys derived from a one-way boolean (Number(isStateLoaded)) collapse to [1] after hydration and never reset — one crash kills an always-mounted dialog host for the whole session, and every deferred-promise action then leaks its promise silently; key off a monotonic per-request signal
summary: src/App.tsx always-mounts ~10 lazy dialog hosts wrapped in ErrorBoundary variant="component" with resetKeys={[Number(isStateLoaded)]}; ErrorBoundary.componentDidUpdate resets only when resetKeys change, but the boolean collapses to [1] post-hydration so a crashed host stays dead all session, and since deferred-promise stores (gitPushConfirmStore.requestConfirmation, no timeout) only resolve through the dialog UI, every later git.push/pull-rebase/panel-limit/MCP-confirm silently leaks its parked Promise (no error/toast) while the off-screen h-screen overflow:hidden fallback makes manual recovery unreachable. Fix: monotonic requestSeq bumped atomically with the pending payload in one functional set (covers back-to-back supersede), excluded from partialize; FIFO stores key on current.requestId/intentId; extracted to useModalResetKeys hook.

title: Clamping the per-frame dt (Math.min(dt, 0.032)) in an rAF spring silently makes simulation speed a function of frame rate — the guard only bites under sustained slow frames, which is exactly the 4K-capture condition; use a fixed-timestep accumulator instead
summary: DemoCursor scroll glide and DemoOverlay spotlight cutout clamped rAF spring dt (Math.min(dt,0.032)), dropping wall-clock time once 4K capture drags rAF below ~31fps -- recorded glide plays in slow motion. Fix: src/lib/demoSpring.ts fixed-timestep accumulator (FIXED_DT=1/120, MAX_FRAME_DT=0.064 guard) is frame-rate-independent; cancellable runSpringLoop avoids orphaned rAF hangs.

title: An agent config with no bootCompletePatterns silently costs a 15s phantom boot every launch — BootDetector falls back to hardcoded Claude/Codex/Gemini banners that never match your CLI; and a spinner glyph earns primary confidence only if it's disjoint from every other agent's set and verified from upstream (#3941)
summary: Missing/empty bootCompletePatterns in shared/config/agents/*.ts makes buildBootCompletePatterns return undefined, so BootDetector falls back to hardcoded Claude/Codex/Gemini BOOT_COMPLETE_PATTERNS that never match other CLIs — every launch waits the full 15s POLLING_MAX_BOOT_MS as a phantom boot with wrong [AgentStartup] telemetry. Also: a working-state spinner glyph is primaryPatterns-grade (0.95) only if disjoint from every agent (the braille class is shared by goose/crush/kiro/mistral/qwen/kimi → fallback 0.75; kimi's moon set → primary); never copy glyph sets between agents (#3941, OpenCode got Gemini's braille instead of Bubble Tea). Patterns are scoped to an already-identified agent (ProcessDetector).

title: A governor restore-branch checked hasToken("backpressure") — a PauseToken reserved for the dead FUTURE_SAB path — so it never fired for live ipc-queue/port-queue holds, leaving a stale 'Paused (memory)' pill stuck behind the status dedup map
summary: pty-host ResourceGovernor.disengageThrottle restored paused-backpressure via coordinator.hasToken("backpressure") — a PauseToken taken only on the dead FUTURE_SAB path, never by the live ipc-queue/port-queue holds — so the branch never fired; because BackpressureManager.emitTerminalStatus dedupes on last status, the engage-time paused-resource-governor stayed latched and the 'Paused (memory)' pill stuck ~10s. Fix: PtyPauseCoordinator.hasAnyBackpressureToken() enumerating the live token family (startsWith port-queue). regression_of #7934.

title: Renderer and pty-host converge on a terminal's activity tier ONLY through explicit broadcast state — deriving it from the poll interval, or letting the renderer's same-tier dedup drop a host correction, strands a pane at the wrong stream rate
summary: Terminal activity-tier convergence: renderer TerminalRendererPolicy dedups on lastBackendTier, pty-host stores TerminalProcess._activityTier. #10266 fixed setActivityMonitorTier deriving tier from pollingIntervalMs<=50, misclassifying visible-unfocused ('active',200ms) panes as background; #10284 fixed same-tier host corrections being dedup-dropped unless rebroadcast via tier-changed/onTierChanged/initializeBackendTier (recurred #9778/#8998); #10285 a fail-open decline (return true clearing needsWake). Wake/suspend machinery later deleted by #10811; tier now only gates headless agent-state poll cadence.

title: A setImmediate-drained deferred-init queue keeps draining during before-quit and re-inits services teardown just nulled — fix is a halt latch set before the first await, reached only after quit commits, and NOT cleared by resetDeferredQueue (macOS fires last-window-close first)
summary: Electron shutdown race: `deferredInitQueue.ts`'s `setImmediate` drain (`doDrain`/`drainNext`) has no quit awareness, so during `before-quit` a pending deferred task re-inits a service the teardown chain just nulled, orphaning the plugin-cli-server socket/`cli.sock` (init guards like `if (singleton) return` pass because they read the just-nulled ref). Fix: a process-lifetime `halted` latch via `haltDeferredQueue()`, guarded at all five queue entry points, set synchronously at the top of `runShutdownChain` before the first `await`, reached only after quit commits (cancelled quit must not halt), and deliberately NOT cleared by `resetDeferredQueue()` because macOS fires `last-window-close` before `before-quit`.

title: getDisplayMedia honors width/height only as advisory hints for DISPLAY capture — the track stays at the surface's native backing-store size until you applyConstraints({exact}) after acquisition and verify via getSettings
summary: getDisplayMedia (DemoCaptureBridge.tsx) treats width/height as advisory-only for display capture — Chromium 148 delivers native backing-store size regardless, so the 1440p preset (SCALE=2) silently recorded 3840x2160 at a 1440p 32Mbps budget. Fix: post-acquisition applyConstraints({exact}) + getSettings() verify, fail-hard on mismatch; e2e parses WebM dims via ffmpeg-static.

title: Webview JS-dialog state is document-scoped, not webContents-scoped: dismiss on did-navigate + render-process-gone + destroyed, and cache the parent window because hostWebContents is unreachable by the time destroyed fires
summary: Webview browser-panel JS dialogs (alert/confirm/prompt) intercepted in electron/setup/protocols.ts js-dialog handler are document-scoped: Chromium drops native dialog state on cross-document did-navigate, render-process-gone, and destroyed, but cleanup keyed only on destroyed left stale renderer overlays over the new page and leaked WebviewDialogService.pendingDialogs callbacks. Fix wires all three events to cancelPendingForGuest (resolve false) + WEBVIEW_DIALOG_DISMISS IPC draining useWebviewDialog's queue. Crux: on destroyed, hostWebContents is unreachable so getWindowForWebContents returns null; a resolveParentWindow() helper caches cachedParentWindow during the guest's lifetime. did-navigate (cross-doc) vs did-navigate-in-page (same-doc) distinction is load-bearing.

title: A channel left in BOTH the hand-written and generated IPC maps compiles clean (TS lets a child interface redeclare a structurally-compatible parent property) and evades all three guards — count ratchets, union drift tests, and one-sided codegen checks are each blind to overlap
summary: A codegen'd IPC channel (project:clone-repo/-cancel) left in BOTH maps.ts (IpcInvokeMap) and generated.ts (GeneratedIpcInvokeMap it extends) compiles clean — TS lets a child interface redeclare a structurally-compatible parent property — and all three guards miss it: the count ratchet (ipc-handwritten-ratchet.mjs), channelDrift.test.ts's UNIONed key sets, and codegen --check's generated-only scope. Fix: an intersection overlap guard via independent extractKeysFromBlock calls plus a negative-control test.

title: A dual-purpose metric funnel makes metricType a command discriminant: reusing the existing null-source `suspend` type to REPORT a data-loss drop was read as a force-resume COMMAND and erased live pause tracking — distinct events need distinct metricTypes
summary: pty-host `emitReliabilityMetricWithTracking` is dual-purpose: forwards a wire metric AND mutates the `pausedTerminals` map; metricType+source===null is a force-resume discriminant. The IPC cap-drop site reused `suspend`/null to report data loss, wiping the pause entry, silencing the tooltip + `heldDurationMs`. Fix: dedicated `ipc-cap-drop` metricType.

title: Canvas measureText under-reports system-ui width vs LayoutNG in Chromium 148 (~15% on macOS), so any measure-then-clamp text pipeline must bias the estimate upward and count wrapped lines with Intl.Segmenter, never char-count
summary: Demo caption title-safe clamp (resolveAnnotationPlacement/estimateCaptionBox/estimateWrappedLines in src/components/Demo/DemoOverlay.tsx): canvas measureText resolves system-ui to different SF Pro optical variants than LayoutNG in Chromium 148, under-reporting width ~15% on macOS, so a measure-then-render pipeline builds too-narrow boxes that escape the 5% SMPTE margin. Fix biases measurements MEASURE_FUDGE=1.15 (over-estimate only), counts real wrapped lines via Intl.Segmenter word granularity (CJK/ZWJ-emoji/break-word), uses independent per-edge clamps, pre-wrap+overflow-wrap to match estimator, and normalizeSize to stop NaN from untyped IPC payloads.

title: DOM idle heuristics (getAnimations + MutationObserver + double-rAF) are structurally blind to WebGL canvas repaints and <video> playback — for xterm activity subscribe onWriteParsed, never onRender (cursor blink fires onRender forever)
summary: Demo engine DemoCursor.tsx waitForIdle (demo:exec-wait-for-idle) declared the page idle while xterm streamed or a <video> played: document.getAnimations() returns only WAAPI/CSS and MutationObserver only DOM mutations, both blind to @xterm/addon-webgl canvas repaints and video frame advances. #10254 adds two channels — per-terminal onWriteParsed (onRender rejected: cursor blink fires it continuously so idle never settles) and capture-phase video playing/pause/ended/waiting listeners — plus a cancellable double-rAF (rafCancelled) closing the rAF-gap race and an idempotent cleanup(). isHibernated guard later removed by hibernation teardown 7d417ab2a.

title: Gating a dialog with `{isOpen && <Comp/>}` unmounts it in the same commit isOpen flips false, so useAnimatedPresence's exit phase never runs — the keep-alive latch must live in the HOST, not the child
summary: React exit-animation trap: {isOpen && <Comp/>} in src/App.tsx unmounts the lazy dialog/palette same-commit as isOpen flips false, so useAnimatedPresence's exit branch never fires. Fix: useKeepMounted(isOpen) latch in the HOST (child's hasOpenedRef is inert). GitInitDialog needs its own path latch; WorktreeOverviewModal/ProjectSwitcherPalette excluded.

title: In the packages/* npm workspace a `types` field pointing at src/ with files:['dist'] ships zero declarations, and a bare `*` sibling dep is NOT the workspace: protocol — both look correct locally because the workspace symlink hides the published shape
summary: packages/daintree-plugin + create-daintree-plugin npm-publish metadata (PR #10248, issue #9884): types/exports.types pointed at src/index.ts while files:['dist'] excludes src, so published consumers got zero declarations (dts:false was justified by the workspace symlink exposing src locally); fix = tsup dts:{resolve:true, compilerOptions:{ignoreDeprecations:'6.0'}} into dist + repointed type fields. Separately a bare '*' sibling range is not workspace: (never rewritten at publish, resolves to newest major at install), bounded to ^0.1.0; prepare:'tsup' keeps dist in sync. No publint/CI guard catches published-shape bugs — verify the type pointer lands inside files.

title: panelIdsByWorktreeId is a derived index over panelIds with a two-tier maintenance contract — order-changing mutations MUST call buildWorktreeIndex(), and reorderTabGroups was the site that skipped the rebuild its #7451 siblings already do
summary: panelRegistry Zustand slice: panelIdsByWorktreeId (worktreeIndex.ts) is a #7451 derived per-worktree bucket index over panelIds with a two-tier contract — targeted add/remove/transfer helpers for membership (preserve bucket array ref stability so useShallow selectors skip), full buildWorktreeIndex() only for order changes. reorderTabGroups (tabGroups.ts) returned bare {panelIds} and skipped the rebuild its ordering.ts siblings (reorderTerminals/moveTerminalToPosition/restoreTerminalOrder) do, so useWorktreeTerminals + AgentButton showed stale drag order until an unrelated mutation healed it; grid/split escaped because they derive order from getTabGroups. Fix #10246/issue #9939 adds buildWorktreeIndex to the return + worktreeIndexInvariant.test.ts.

title: The artifact extractor is the SOLE gate before a user-facing 'Apply patch' → git apply, so a one-token opener (any '---') must never promote a block — require trigger + corroborating +++ + a real @@ hunk
summary: extractPatches in shared/utils/artifactParser.ts opened a patch on any '---' line, so Markdown HRs and YAML front-matter became fake 'Apply patch' artifacts that failed against git apply (#9998). Fix: three-tier classifier — trigger (--- + non-space or 'diff '), corroborate (+++ within 4 lines), commit (real @@ hunk). findOpenPatchStart (#10224) stays loose; this stays strict.

title: notify's EVENT_POLICY manifest is the source of truth for ROUTING but not for severity-escalation re-toast — shouldReToast is deliberately kind-agnostic, so the reserved per-kind reToastOnSeverityEscalation flag was zero-reader dead config whose values contradicted shipped behavior; delete such a field, don't wire it up
summary: EVENT_POLICY in src/lib/notify.ts is the typed source-of-truth for notification ROUTING but not for severity-escalation re-toast: shouldReToast (notificationSeverity.ts) is deliberately kind-agnostic and never reads the manifest, called unconditionally on both dispatch paths. The reserved per-kind reToastOnSeverityEscalation flag had zero readers and values (host/recovery=true, eight kinds=false) contradicting shipped behavior; wiring it up would silently disable re-toast for eight kinds, so #10241 deleted it and JSDoc'd the global rule.

title: A module-level per-terminal Map in the renderer leaks for the whole renderer lifetime unless wired into teardown — and the panelIds subscriber MISSES the user-close path, which needs a separate trashedTerminals subscriber plus a mount-cleared tombstone for the queued-IPC race
summary: artifactStore Map in src/hooks/useArtifacts.ts leaked content strings for the renderer lifetime; only clearArtifacts pruned. Fix wires removeArtifactsForTerminal into rendererStoreOrchestrator via BOTH panelIds AND a trashedTerminals subscriber (trashPanel flips location to 'trash' without shrinking panelIds), plus a removedTerminals tombstone onDetected checks and the per-terminal mount useEffect clears so reused ids aren't blackholed; clearArtifacts must NOT tombstone.

title: Terminal restore methods never throw — they signal failure via a boolean AND a stashed classified error, so a caller that returns success without reading both replays a failed snapshot onto a reset-blanked buffer as if it worked
summary: Terminal scrollback restore (TerminalRestoreController.restoreFromSerialized / restoreFromSerializedIncremental, #8535) never throws: it swallows write-timeout/xterm-parse/poisoned-writeChain errors, stashes a classified TerminalScrollbackRestoreError on managed.lastScrollbackRestoreError, and returns false. #9896: TerminalWakeManager.wakeAndRestore returned true unconditionally, reading neither signal, so a failed replay onto a reset()-blanked buffer looked successful — needsWake cleared, onPostWake ran, held bytes flushed, no banner/retry. Fix mirrors the scrollbackRestoreScheduler hydration path (setScrollbackRestoreError, re-read via getInstance for stale managed). Fix site deleted by hibernation-removal #10811 but the dual-signal contract stays live for TerminalInstanceService/PaintFabricCompositor callers.

title: simple-git checkIgnore passes every path as its own argv entry and hits E2BIG on huge flat dirs; a swallowed catch made it fail OPEN and leak gitignored files — direct-spawn `check-ignore --stdin -z` and fail closed
summary: FileTreeService.getFileTree filtered gitignored entries via simple-git's checkIgnoreTask, which builds argv as [check-ignore, ...paths]; a flat dir with thousands of entries exceeds ARG_MAX and git fails E2BIG/ENOMEM. The empty catch(_e){} left ignoredPaths empty so the tree failed OPEN, leaking build output/secret-like files (issue #10003). Fix (electron/utils/gitCheckIgnore.ts checkIgnoredPaths): direct spawn of `git check-ignore --stdin -z` (NUL-separated paths over stdin, constant argv), fail-closed catch in FileTreeService.ts that adds every checked path to ignoredPaths, 30s throttled warn, stdin EPIPE tolerance, GIT_BLOCK_TIMEOUT_MS SIGTERM kill, and re-applied hardening via getHardenedGitConfig/buildHardenedGitEnv (electron/utils/hardenedGit.ts, extracted from createHardenedGit). Exit code 1 = none ignored, not an error; only >1 rejects.

title: A notification is only 'seen' if the window had focus — every toast dispatch path must gate on document.hasFocus(), and in Chromium 148 that read is stale inside blur/focus handlers so the event arrival itself is the signal
summary: src/lib/notify.ts + toaster.tsx: toasts fired into a blurred window auto-dismissed unseen yet were stamped seenAsToast:true, killing the unread badge and useReEntrySummary's !seenAsToast filter. Three independent toast paths (shouldToastThread, suppression-grace blur promote(), toaster dismiss timer) each need a document.hasFocus() gate; urgent bypasses quiet hours not focus. Chromium 148 hasFocus() is stale inside blur/focus handlers (use the event as the signal); jsdom defaults hasFocus() false so pin true in tests.

title: Distinguishing 'cleared' from 'never-set' across a defaults/merge boundary needs a non-undefined sentinel — because the back-fill layer keys off `=== undefined`, NOT because Electron IPC drops undefined keys (it preserves them)
summary: CopyTree Test Config dry-run (ContextTab.handleTestConfig -> mergeCopyTreeOptions in electron/ipc/handlers/copyTree.ts) previewed stale saved values for cleared form fields: the renderer omitted empty keys and the merge's `=== undefined` guard back-filled them (absent-vs-cleared collapse). Fix sends full form state with a `null` cleared sentinel via a scoped CopyTreeTestConfigOptionsSchema (.nullish()) + stripClearedFields() so downstream sees T|undefined. Correction: `null` is required by the `=== undefined` guard, not because Electron IPC drops undefined keys — modern Electron/V8 ValueSerializer + contextBridge preserve undefined-valued properties.

title: A sliding-window buffer feeding a paired-delimiter regex silently drops any artifact bigger than the window — anchor the trim to the nearest still-open structure, hard-cap it, and extract from the UNTRIMMED buffer before storing the trimmed one
summary: semantic.worker.ts trimmed analysisBuffer via slice(-5000); the code-block regex needs both fences at once, so blocks >5KB had their opener evicted before the closer arrived, dropping them forever (#9999). Fix: trimAnalysisBuffer anchors the cut to the nearest open fence/patch, capped at 1MB, and extracts from the untrimmed buffer before storing the trim.

title: MCP tools/list cache-fallback must snapshot getCachedManifest() BEFORE the await, not in the catch: a concurrent clearCache/teardown mid-fetch would otherwise null it or serve another window's tool surface — and pinned sessions still fail closed
summary: MCP ListTools handler (sessionServer.ts) hard-failed with JSON-RPC InternalError, wiping the agent's tool surface, when requestManifest() rejected on a transient renderer-bridge hiccup. #10222 falls back to getCachedManifest(), snapshotted BEFORE the await so a concurrent clearCache()/cachedManifest reassignment or pinned-session teardown can't null it or serve another window's tools; pinned sessions fail closed via === null (not !manifest) → McpError, and an empty zero-tool manifest stays valid. Later hardened by PR #10277 (issue #9887).

title: Playwright's JSON reporter sets spec.ok===true for flaky (and skipped) specs, so a --test-list retry filtered on .ok==false silently drops the flaky spec that tripped FAIL_ON_FLAKY_TESTS — a false green on the core/online release gate
summary: e2e.yml's run_attempt>1 retry scopes to --test-list failed-specs.txt; the old jq filter used .ok==false, but Playwright's JSON spec.ok=test.ok() is true for expected/flaky/skipped, so on core/online (failOnFlakyTests, playwright.config.ts:63) a mixed hard+flaky failure retried only the hard file and re-ran to a false green, never re-exercising the flaky spec. Fix: extract-failed-specs.mjs specFailed() includes a spec when any test status==='flaky' OR last-result not passed/skipped. Sibling extract-failures.mjs (stabilize triage) deliberately EXCLUDES flaky — same JSON report, opposite semantics per consumer; empty-list [ -s ] gate hides the pure-flaky case.

title: Collapse a normalized enum to its narrow legacy set only at the output boundary, never in the producer — the mid-pipeline declined→closed collapse made canonical linked.pr.state lossy, and an async re-emit must read the live map entry, not a captured object
summary: PullRequestService collapsed Bitbucket declined→closed in the producer (InternalLinkedPR.state typed narrow), making the canonical linked.pr.state projection lossy though the renderer and plugin SDK handle NormalizedPRState; #10220 (regression of #8350) widens the internal types (InternalLinkedPR.state, PRDetectionResult, sys:pr:detected, composeLinked) end-to-end and moves the collapse to legacy flat-field boundaries only (WorkspaceService.sendEvent, SnapshotBuilder). Also fixes a stale-closure: the fire-and-forget CI-enrichment re-emit read prState from the captured pr, not the live detectedPRs map entry, reverting re-detected state.

title: One MRU persistence pipeline ate data four ways: debounce fires with stale schedule-time args, a global list pruned per-view self-destructs on switch, a category pruned mid-hydration is gutted, and unfiltered focus recording pollutes a capped list
summary: Quick-switcher MRU pipeline (rendererStoreOrchestrator sub 1c, debouncedPersistMruList, useQuickSwitcher, ProjectState.mruList): four coordination bugs — stale schedule-time debounce clobbered fresher writes, a global list pruned per-view gutted other projects on switch, mid-hydration prune dropped unloaded categories, unfiltered focus recording ate the 50-cap.

title: An `as unknown as` cast erased the ForbidIpcEnvelopeKeys compile guard on the opValidated IPC path — validated handlers could return {ok|success}-shaped objects that nest silently inside security.ts's success wrapper; enforce the guard on every handler variant via SafeResult, never a suppression cast
summary: opValidated() IPC handlers bypassed the ForbidIpcEnvelopeKeys guard op() enforces via SafeResult<K>: define.ts's validated handler types used the bare result and `as unknown as` casts in utils.ts (typedHandleValidated/typedHandleWithContextValidated) erased the constraint, so validated handlers taking untrusted payloads could return {ok|success}-shaped objects nesting silently inside security.ts's {ok:true,data} wrap (#6020 silent-swallow). Fix: route every variant through SafeResult<K>, delete the casts, add anchored @ts-expect-error type tests.

title: In the pty-host multi-window fan-out, a single global `visualWritten` flag flips true the instant ANY window's PortBatcher accepts, suppressing the shared IPC fallback for a SATURATED sibling — silent per-window data loss; fallback/drop/loss must be computed per destination and signalled on that destination's own port, never broadcast
summary: pty-host `ptyManager.on("data")` fan-out in electron/pty-host.ts tracked delivery with a GLOBAL `visualWritten` flag that flips true the moment any window's per-window PortBatcher accepts, suppressing the shared IPC/SAB fallback for a saturated sibling window → silent per-window data loss (no fallback, no dropAccumulator counter, no terminal-status:data-loss marker) in multi-window mode (windowProjectMap null = fan-out target). #9891 fix: collect `saturated[]`, account drop unconditionally (UTF-8 byteCount) + post data-loss pulse on the starved window's OWN MessagePort (new terminal-status PtyHostToRendererMessage variant, dispatched by terminalClient.installPortDataHandler), never sendEvent broadcast (would falsely flag healthy windows). Original !ipcDataMirrorTerminals skip was wrong (data-mirror is Main-only, not re-dispatched into xterm), removed in 4211fbf86.

title: Browser-side dev-preview detection is confined to the passive CDP console stream: executeJavaScript hangs on CDP-frozen docked panels and native Chromium WS errors never hit the JS console, so dead-HMR detection can only match Vite's own failure log lines — and must be navigation-generation-gated
summary: Dev-preview dead-HMR detection (#10213, useDevPreviewConsoleCapture.ts). Detecting anything inside a guest webview is confined to the already-captured CDP console stream: executeJavaScript hangs on CDP-frozen docked panels (Page.setWebLifecycleState, the #8310 trap) and native Chromium socket errors (net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED) never reach the JS console, so detection can only match Vite's own VITE_HMR_FAILURE_PATTERN log lines while [vite] hmr update / UrlDetector 'Compiling' phase mislead. hmrDead set must be navigation-generation-gated (row.navigationGeneration >= currentGenerationRef) so a restarted server's stale-generation stragglers can't resurrect the DevPreviewHmrDeadBanner over a healthy reload.

title: CI gates must fail closed on unmet preconditions: PERF-004's -1 'not measured' sentinel became ~0ms wall-clock and always cleared its 8000ms budget, and the test-ratio windowCompleted precondition could never be met once any PR was filtered — both reported PASS forever
summary: Two self-checking CI gates reported PASS forever while gating nothing. PERF-004's -1 'not measured' sentinel (scripts/perf/scenarios/startup.ts) became ~0ms wall-clock in run.ts's negative-durationMs substitution, trivially clearing its 8000ms budget; fix throws fail-closed, rejects non-finite durationMs, packages a real binary under xvfb, and fixes electron-builder --dir path detection (isFile vs existsSync, injectable platform). The fix-with-test ratio gate (check-test-ratio.mjs/test-ratio-lib.mjs) self-disabled because windowCompleted needed 100 eligible PRs from a single 100-PR GraphQL fetch — any filtered release/version-bump PR short-circuited compareToBaseline to ok:true; fix paginates until 100 eligible collected (#10200). Canonical fail-open/self-disabling-gate lesson.

title: A greedy `.*` before an OPTIONAL suffix group never backtracks to feed it — it swallowed `:line:col` on every file link; anchor the greedy prefix to a terminator (the extension) and order specific alternations (`\wsl$`) before the bare-relative fallback
summary: Terminal FileLinksAddon path detection (now shared src/services/terminal/filePathDetection.ts: FILE_PATH_REGEX, resolveFilePathCandidate/resolveSelectedFilePath, also HybridInputBar/TerminalContextMenu). Old resolver /^(.*)(?::(\d+)(?::(\d+))?)?$/ let greedy .* swallow the whole :line:col into pathPart while the optional suffix group matched empty and the overall match succeeded, so it never backtracked — line/col always undefined and suffixed paths resolved to non-existent files; latent because bare paths worked. Fix anchors the prefix to the extension (\.[^\s:]+?, colon-free) and prepends a WSL UNC alternation (\\wsl$/wsl.localhost) ordered before the bare-relative fallback so it can't capture a broken mid-path fragment. #9919.

title: beforeunload never fires on WebContentsView detach (Electron 41/42, Chromium 148) — debounced-persistence flushes hung off it silently drop on project switch/close/quit; flush on visibilitychange, and pagehide is too late for async IPC
summary: Renderer persistence in the multi-WebContentsView (ProjectViewManager) model: beforeunload does NOT fire on view detach in Electron 41/42/Chromium 148, so flushPanelPersistence() and the debouncedPersistMruList (rendererStoreOrchestrator.ts, 150ms at PR time / 500ms panelPersistence.ts) writes were dropped on project switch, window close, and quit. Fix = visibilitychange listener flushing when document.hidden, plus flush-if-already-hidden at registration (races with fast switch). Nuance: pagehide (optimisticPanelClose.ts) only survives sync work; async IPC flushes must ride visibilitychange. App-wide invariant already in useFlushOnHide/SettingsDialog.

title: Synthetic MouseEvent-only dispatch silently no-ops on Daintree's pointer-first controls — programmatic actuation needs the full pointerdown→mousedown→pointerup→mouseup→click sequence carrying primary-mouse pointer metadata
summary: DemoCursor.tsx demo:exec-click/drag dispatched MouseEvent-only, silently no-oping on pointer-first controls: dnd-kit PointerSensor gates on pointerdown+isPrimary+button===0; Radix menus/Select read pointerType. Plain buttons masked it via native click. Fix leads each event with a PointerEvent (pointerId:1, pointerType:mouse, isPrimary:true). Arc PRs #10206, #10210.

title: CI failure-triage must reason over Playwright's resolved test.status and the strings the harness actually emits — not per-attempt results nor the platform's internal error text; plus the Windows /tmp upload trap and artifact-immutability 409
summary: E2E failure-report pipeline (scripts/ci/extract-failures.mjs, e2e.yml "Extract failure signatures", consumed by stabilize.yml). Gates on Playwright test.status==="unexpected" not per-attempt result.status; fixes Windows /tmp upload-artifact loss, v4+ immutability 409, and cross-OS path-normalize order. Companion #10207 classifier later removed (69069ac31) as unconsumed.

title: The internal `events` bus is a per-process module singleton — emitting `ui:notify` from a UtilityProcess (workspace-host, pty-host) is a silent no-op because its only subscriber, EventBuffer, runs in main; know which process consumes an event surface before emitting into it
summary: electron/services/events.ts TypedEventBus is per-process; PullRequestService (workspace-host) emitted ui:notify on breaker trip to zero subscribers — EventBuffer (perWindowInit.ts) starts only in main and merely records for the event inspector, never a toast. Real toasts come via src/lib/notify.ts; correct signal is sys:pr:detection-state to PRDetectionPausedIndicator.

title: GitHub's per-issue comments endpoint silently ignores sort/direction, so per_page:1 desc returns the OLDEST comment — a bot dedup guard against it can never match; paginate + .at(-1), also dedup against issue.body, and never let a missing scan read as zero-stale
summary: stale-quarantine.yml dedup never matched: per-issue comments endpoint ignores sort/direction (always oldest-first), so per_page:1 desc fetched the OLDEST comment; moving threshold dates and body-only reports also broke matching. Fix: paginate+.at(-1), normalize(), body check. #10202: line-scan parser to brace-matching findEnclosingObjectRange + fail-closed sentinel.

title: A forge IPC handler that resolves the provider from ambient state (global default → first-registered) validates a token against the WRONG backend the moment a second forge exists — provider-neutral surfaces must carry an explicit providerId and fail closed on unknown
summary: electron/ipc/handlers/forge.ts FORGE_VALIDATE_TOKEN had no providerId in its payload, so it resolved the forge from global forgeDefaultProviderId else providers[0] (first-registered) — latent-correct while GitHub was the only forge, fail-open once GitLab could register: a GitHub PAT validated against GitLab, reporting valid tokens invalid (#9985). Fix: payload {providerId, token}, normalizeProviderId + strict makeForgeProviderId canonical match, resolved {valid:false,error} for unknown/inactive (never fallback); provider-specific tabs pin BUILTIN_GITHUB_PROVIDER_ID; peer FORGE_SET_CREDENTIAL was the correct model. Action since moved to forgeActions.ts, tab into builtin github plugin.

title: A process-model migration left getPtyManager() importable but never populated — four main-process features read [] for months, and CI stayed green because every test mocked the dead singleton itself
summary: PTY management moved to the forked pty-host UtilityProcess (commit 5d802218b), but the main-process getPtyManager() singleton in electron/services/PtyManager.ts stayed importable and returns []. Four consumers (DiagnosticsCollector, IdleTerminalNotificationService, HibernationService, ProjectViewManager.hasActiveAgent) silently no-op'd for months: empty support bundles, dead idle notifications (#5064), hibernation never firing (#8534), active-agent views wrongly LRU-evicted (#5234). CI stayed green because unit tests mocked getPtyManager() itself — a tautology. #10190 routes all four to ptyClient.getAllTerminalsAsync(); patterns: sync eviction guard behind an event-fed agent-state cache (now ProjectViewAgentStateCache.ts, #11004), setPtyClient re-acquired on start(), seed after setupWindowServices.

title: Correlation IDs read from a mutable register must be snapshotted once at dispatch start and threaded to every consumer — three live reads of getCurrentTurnIdForSession disagreed whenever the FSM's active→passive clear landed mid-call
summary: MCP turn attribution race: httpLifecycle.ts's 3 closures each live-read turnOutcomeLog's getCurrentTurnIdForSession; FSM active→passive clears turnIdBySession mid-call, so McpActivityStrip and RecentCallsPopover disagreed on turn (#10067). Fix: sessionServer.ts CallTool snapshots capturedTurnId once pre-await, threads it to every consumer.

title: A font preload without crossorigin='anonymous' never matches the always-CORS @font-face fetch — and with font-display: optional the missed ~100ms window silently commits the whole session to fallback monospace
summary: Cold-boot font preload (src/lib/fontPreload.ts) lacked crossorigin, so it stayed no-cors while @font-face fetches are always CORS-mode -- never matched, woff2 downloaded twice, and font-display:optional's ~100ms block expired, locking cold boots into fallback monospace. Fix: crossOrigin=anonymous. Regression of #6794/#6781; covers URL-parity + Playwright listener-timing trap.

title: Electron <webview> src is not a controlled prop: onLoadCommit self-syncs the attribute, so a React re-bind after guest navigation is a same-value write Electron turns into a full reload — seed src once at mount, navigate only via loadURL
summary: BrowserPane/DevPreviewPane bound <webview src> to history.present. Electron's onLoadCommit self-syncs src via setValueIgnoreMutation, so React's re-bind is a same-value write the SrcAttribute observer reloads — doubling clicks, breaking SPA routing, masked by swallowed ERR_ABORTED(-3). Fix: seed src once at mount, navigate via loadURL only.

title: Electron's win.center() repositions but never resizes, and macOS auto-clamps larger-than-screen windows (enableLargerThanScreen is macOS-only, default false) — so an unclamped first-run default window spills off-screen only on Windows/Linux small displays, invisible on the dev platform and in big-work-area tests
summary: createWindowWithState (electron/windowState.ts) short-circuited to win.center() on coordinate-less bounds, skipping the size clamp, so the 1200x800 default spilled off small work areas (1366x768, RDP, VMs). macOS enableLargerThanScreen:false masked it; Windows/Linux didn't. Fix: unconditional clamp + safeWorkArea fallback; tests need mockReturnValue not Once.

title: In an Electron webview an HTTP 502 is a SUCCESSFUL load — did-fail-load stays silent and did-finish-load clears your error state; httpResponseCode exists only on did-frame-navigate, and the error must be latched in a same-tick ref so the trailing did-navigate/did-finish-load can't erase it
summary: Electron <webview>: HTTP 502 is a successful load — did-fail-load never fires, did-finish-load clears webviewLoadError, so raw 502 body renders forever. Fix (useDevPreviewLoadLifecycle.ts): did-frame-navigate (only event with httpResponseCode) latches pendingHttpErrorRef same-tick so trailing nav events can't erase it; scoped only to proxy's self-generated 502.

title: A coalesce key that omits a request dimension (opts.search) hands the second caller the first's payload on its OWN promise — renderer latest-wins guards pass it as fresh; and search results are ephemera that must never write the canonical list cache
summary: Forge issue-list path (electron/ipc/handlers/forgeData.ts listOptionsKey + GitHub provider dedupe/listIssuesInflight in readOps.ts). #10175 wired opts.search into listIssues; the IPC coalesce key omitted search, so two debounced IssuePickerDialog keystrokes aliased onto one in-flight promise and the second query got the first's items — and IssuePickerDialog's fetchIdRef latest-wins guard can't catch it since wrong data rides the newest request's own promise. Fix: add opts.search to the fixed-order tuple key; searchIssuesImpl uses a search:-prefixed dedupe key and never writes forgeIssueListCache so background polls don't serve typed-query ephemera as the canonical list. Two independent single-flight layers; listPRsImpl still ignores search.

title: .catch(() => null) inside a poll loader converts transient forge failures into authoritative 'no PR' — wiping valid rows via sys:pr:cleared AND disarming the breaker/backoff built to catch exactly those failures, because errors absorbed in the innermost layer never reach handleError
summary: PullRequestService's prByBranchLoader per-branch fallback collapsed rejections to null via .catch(() => null), indistinguishable from confirmed 'no PR', so bridge timeouts/mid-cycle 429s emitted spurious sys:pr:cleared wiping worktree-dashboard rows, while consecutiveErrors/3-error breaker/computeBackoff/sys:pr:detection-state/checkRateLimitGate sat unreachable as dead code downstream of the swallow. Fix (all in electron/services/PullRequestService.ts): BatchLoader per-key Error slots (electron/workspace-host/batchLoader.ts contract), resolvePRsForBranches returns {branch, pr, error} tuples, checkForPRs skips errored branches and routes failures to handleError once per cycle (not per branch) after re-checking checkRateLimitGate, consecutiveErrors resets only when prResults.length > 0, confirmed clears delete the detectedPRs entry. Regression of #8879 (forge-bridge IPC migration); resolves #9994.

title: A flow-control ledger must be acked in the exact unit it was charged: the pty-host charged UTF-8 bytes but the renderer acked UTF-16 `.length`, so every box-drawing char under-acked and ratcheted the queue into spurious 10s backpressure pauses
summary: Terminal IPC flow control: pty-host charged its ledger in UTF-8 bytes (Buffer.byteLength → ipcQueueManager.addBytes) but TerminalWriteController acked with string .length (UTF-16 units), so box-drawing/CJK/emoji output under-acked, drifting queuedBytes to the 67% watermark and tripping spurious 10s paused-backpressure stalls (IPC_MAX_PAUSE_MS self-heal masked the deterministic drift). Fix kept two ledgers each in its own unit (utf8ByteLength ack vs UTF-16 inFlightBytes), guarded Uint8Array port chunks from double-draining the IPC ledger, acked the hibernated drop path, and renamed charCount→byteCount.

title: Module singletons are per-process: the forge RPC bridge (#8870) left the workspace-host subscribed to a dead gitHubRateLimitService, killing fetch backoff invisibly (stuck multiplier 1 = healthy value) — cross-process pushed state needs cache-and-replay on every host ready
