summary: Forge RPC bridge #8870 moved GitHub HTTP into main, leaving workspace-host's per-process gitHubRateLimitService singleton silent: onStateChange relay fired zero times, WorkspaceService.applyFetchThrottle stuck at multiplier 1 (= healthy value, so invisible) until the rate-limit wall. Fix #10170: main pushes apply-fetch-throttle via relayFetchThrottle with WorkspaceHostProcess cache replayed on every ready plus WorkspaceHostPool seeding — the setLogLevelOverrides cache-and-replay pattern.

title: A resolver that returns the same null for 'registry not populated yet' and 'no provider will ever match' turns the 5s cold-start poll cap into a forever hot loop — discriminate the miss, pause timer-less on the permanent one, and enumerate every re-arm surface
summary: PullRequestService's 5s cold-start clamp never lifted for GitLab/Bitbucket/no-remote projects — invokeResolveProvider returned identical null for transient and permanent misses, ~17k git subprocess spawns/day/project. Fixed via discriminated ForgeResolveProviderResult gated on isPluginScanComplete, pausing timer-less on no-match with enumerated re-arm surfaces.

title: Eviction protection keyed to a pointer set at the END of a multi-step flow (activeTabId in showTab) protects nothing during the flow — mid-restore portal tabs need an explicit intent flag on the FIRST IPC call, cleared on every terminal path
summary: PortalManager.evictIfNeeded() skipped only activeTabId, set at showTab()'s END, so the create-to-show restore flow was evictable by concurrent background createTab past PORTAL_MAX_LIVE_TABS=3, stranding tabs on the restore skeleton (#9971). Fix: isRestore flag on PortalCreatePayload marks restoringTabIds before createTab, cleared on five terminal paths.

title: notify() eventKind is a routing directive, not a label: passive kinds fill priority:'low', transient:true skips the inbox, and the intersection fires nowhere — with the eventKind-mandating lint rule herding callers into the trap
summary: notify() EVENT_POLICY (src/lib/notify.ts): passive eventKinds (uiFeedback/settings/workingPulse) resolve omitted priority to 'low' (inbox-only) via resolveEventPolicyDefaults; transient:true skips the inbox, so the composition fires nowhere. Ten sites adopted passive kinds to satisfy the #9050 notify-event-kind lint, silently dropping copy confirmations, undo toasts, storage warnings; onClick-only actions also die outside toasts. Fix: explicit priority:'high', policy-aware DEV warn, composition lint; plus the esquery :has(> A > B) silent-no-match trap.

title: Warm project-switch freshness lives in two seams: PTY port rebrokering must not queue behind the worktree git await, and background-tier resizes write latestCols/Rows but never targetCols/Rows — so reattach has no saved grid and flashes 80×24
summary: Warm project-switch terminal staleness arc (#10159/#10160) in activateProjectView (electron/ipc/handlers/projectCrud/switch.ts) + TerminalRevealController/TerminalInstanceService/TerminalResizeController. Three mechanisms: PTY rebroker (ptyClient.onProjectSwitch + distributePortsToView) queued behind the awaited worktreeService.loadProject so the swapped view showed stale output; fullWakeForVisibilityRestore deferred the safe geometry sync (applyDeferredResize) together with the unsafe async wake under one isAttaching guard, so the 80×24 snap fired after the bridge view dropped; background-tier resize wrote latestCols/Rows but not targetCols/Rows, so detachForProjectSwitch must backfill targets (unset-only, non-zero). Later concurrency in #10965, resize caveat in #10863.

title: Every fleet dispatch must route through runManagedFleetBroadcast — a bespoke fan-out silently loses batching/Cancel/progress and races the one-run progress store; verbatim replay is empty-draft + perTargetOverrides, and eligibility filtering is caller-owned by design
summary: fleet.retryFailures forked a stripped broadcastFleetLiteralPaste (no batching/AbortSignal/progress/directing-state) and the preview's private detectUnresolved contradicted replaceRecipeVariables on unknown {{vars}} (#10143/#9954). Fix extracted runManagedFleetBroadcast single-flight wrapper (activeBroadcastController + fleetBroadcastProgressStore); verbatim replay = empty draft + perTargetOverrides; filterEligibleIds stays caller-owned, not inside executeFleetBroadcast.

title: DOM z-index can never cover a native WebContentsView, and the portal overlay effect only corrects on transitions — every renderer portal.show path must re-read overlayStack at show-time (after its awaits), leaning on the overlay-clear reconciler instead of a pending-show queue
summary: Portal WebContentsView surfaced above open DOM modals: four renderer paths (restoreActiveTabAfterClose, activatePortalTab, portal.duplicateTab, devPreview.promoteToPortal) called portal.show without checking overlayStack; PortalVisibilityController's hide effect is transition-edge only and PortalManager.showTab can't see renderer state. Fix: showPortalTabIfNoOverlay helper reading overlayStack after the bounds-retry awaits, recovery via the existing overlay-clear reconciler, no queue.

title: OSC 9;4 state=0 fires between every Claude tool call, so it can never be an authoritative idle signal — idle stays timestamp-decay-only, and the 200ms 'debounce' that seemed to guard it was fully inert
summary: ActivityMonitor/Osc94Parser: Claude OSC 9;4 state=0 fires between every tool call, not just completion, so authoritative idle would flicker working/idle and clobber workingHoldUntil. onOscProgressIdle is a documented no-op; idle stays 8s IDLE_DEBOUNCE_MS decay. The 200ms debounce timer was dead code (removed); stripIdleTerminalSequences feeds only the byte-gate, not renderer.

title: A boolean suppression predicate over the global-banner slot union kept answering 'suppress' when advisory slots joined the recovery-only union — classify slots via a compile-exhaustive Record and scope the settle tail to true no-cause
summary: useShouldSuppressLocalError returned true for any non-null GlobalBannerSlot, so advisory banners (forge-token, cloud-sync) swallowed actionable spawn/reconnect/restart errors in TerminalPane. Fix: exhaustive SLOT_IS_RECOVERY Record (TS2741-forced classification) + settle tail scoped to cause===null.

title: Chromium net error -6 is ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND, not a cancellation — only -3 (ERR_ABORTED) is ever safe to swallow in a did-fail-load handler, and Daintree's duplicated webview error taxonomies let a mislabeled guard get fixed in Browser but survive in its Dev Preview copy
summary: Dev Preview webview went blank on ERR_FILE_NOT_FOUND (#9966): handleDidFailLoad in useDevPreviewLoadLifecycle.ts early-returned on errorCode -6 as 'Ignore cancellations' -- only -3 (ERR_ABORTED) is the real cancellation. Guard copied from BrowserPane by #6107, fixed there by #7369 but left live in Dev Preview a month. #10131 removes it, hardens retry-timer cleanup.

title: A vitest shard denominator hardcoded apart from the matrix list silently skips whole partitions with every check green — and the #10130 SHARD_TOTAL fix was erased by a job rewrite 45 minutes later, so the trap is live in ci.yml again
summary: CI sharding trap in .github/workflows/ci.yml: vitest --shard=i/N denominator hardcoded apart from the matrix list [1,2,3,4] — shrink the list and partition 4/4 is never scheduled, ~25% of tests silently skip while ci-ok stays green. GHA facts: env context unavailable at strategy.matrix evaluation (inputs/needs are); strategy.job-total is the os×shard Cartesian product, not the shard count. Fix (job-level SHARD_TOTAL env) was deleted 45min later by 34d18a74e and PR #10758 reintroduced the literal /4 — trap is live on develop; e2e.yml matrix-setup outputs+fromJSON is the robust pattern.

title: Synthetic boot-time focus routed through the user-focus path corrupts every persisted recency signal a little more per boot — machine-initiated state changes need a dedicated non-recording action, and a hydration suppression flag doesn't cover fallbacks that run after its finally
summary: useAppHydration's boot-focus fallback called setFocused after suppressMruRecording lifted, so stampLastActive persisted Date.now() and recordMru pushed an arbitrary panel to MRU head each boot: self-compounding corruption. Fix: recency-ranked pickBootFocusPanelId, non-recording setBootFocus, statePatcher lastActiveAt propagation (was always 0).

title: An uncaught rejection anywhere in hydrateAppState never crashes — useAppHydration's outer catch marks the app loaded anyway, so a boot task that doesn't self-catch converts its failure into a silent empty workspace; every hydration task must degrade internally and keep last-known-good state
summary: hydrateAppState (bootstrapGuard.ts) ran keybindingService.loadOverrides() bare in a Promise.all; a rejecting getOverrides IPC aborted every restore phase, but useAppHydration's catch set isStateLoaded anyway -- silent empty workspace. Fix: self-catch matching initialize(), last-known-good overrides, no notify on degrade, formatErrorMessage.

title: Marker-only crash entries must derive crash time from pre-crash evidence, never Date.now() at relaunch — and the obvious fallbacks are trapped: backup mtime is rewritten by the Windows EPERM copy-fallback, and JSON.parse of an oversize numeral yields Infinity that passes > 0 validation
summary: CrashRecoveryService.buildCrashEntryFromMarker stamped Date.now() at relaunch for log-less crashes (OOM, kill, power loss), defeating the 30s suspect-window check (#8704 quarantine). Fix: resolveMarkerCrashTimestamp priority chain (killedAt > lastSuspendStart > backup capturedAt > lastHeartbeatMs), clamped to session bounds; traps: Windows mtime rewrite, JSON Infinity passing >0 checks.

title: app.exit() skips the before-quit cleanup chain, so every deliberate self-relaunch/hard-stop site must write the clean-exit marker trio itself — or the next boot books the intentional restart as a crash and accrues a crash-loop strike toward safe mode
summary: GpuCrashMonitorService relaunched via app.relaunch()+app.exit(0), skipping before-quit so shutdown.ts never wrote its clean-exit markers — next boot misread the restart as native-crash (stale dialog, crash-loop strike). Fix: writeCleanGpuMitigationMarkers at all four exit sites, shutdown.ts order, invocationCallOrder-tested. Same class as AutoUpdater #9638.

title: A shared pure resolver only prevents drift among its own callers — resolveForCwd hardcoded forgeProviderOverride:null so every forge operation ignored the override the settings UI displayed, and cwd→project lookup must resolve the main worktree path, not exact-match the cwd
summary: resolveForCwd (electron/ipc/handlers/forgeResolution.ts), the shared cwd→provider resolution behind every forge IPC operation, hardcoded forgeProviderOverride:null while forgeSettings.ts display and workspace-host PR detection honored the real per-project override — settings claimed one provider, operations used another or threw. Fix resolves the owning project via listWorktrees→isMainWorktree main-worktree path (ProjectStore keys on it; cwd is often a linked-worktree subdir), degrading non-fatally through getRepositoryRoot→raw cwd.

title: A webview's session partition is write-once at attach — Electron silently ignores later changes, so per-scope partitions need a synchronously-seeded id at first render, a key={partition} remount escape hatch, and a sweep of every singleton-session assumption
summary: BrowserPane hardcoded partition="persist:browser", leaking cookies/localStorage/IndexedDB across projects on shared localhost origins. Fix (buildBrowserPartition, persist:browser-<projectId>) hits Electron's write-once partition: needs sync __DAINTREE_INITIAL_PROJECT__ seed at first render, key={partition} remount, lazy session-created lockdown replacing eager fromPartition, partition-pattern matching replacing session object-identity, and both will-attach-webview allowlist copies (createWindow.ts + ProjectViewHandlers.ts, post-#11004 extraction from ProjectViewManager.ts) updated.

title: runRecipeWithResults resolves with every spawn failure inside the payload — void-awaiting callers reported success on zero spawns, and the failure toast must omit worktreeId or origin-surface suppression swallows it on the active worktree
summary: recipeStore.runRecipeWithResults throws only on missing recipe id; spawn failures resolve into results.failed silently. Dock menu, recipe.run, workflow actions voided the payload — recipeLaunched=true, MCP told success on zero spawns. Fix: notifyRecipeSpawnFailures omits worktreeId (dodges isOriginSurfaceVisible), notify-then-throw for MCP.

title: Plugin contribution ids are unique only per-plugin — any surface keying on the bare id collides across plugins, and a hardcoded well-known bare id ('github') lets a third-party contribution hijack the built-in card; route on canonical {pluginId}.{contributionId} and normalize legacy forms only at read boundaries
summary: Forge settings subtab routing/selection/React keys in CodeForgeSettingsTab used bare contribution.id and a hardcoded GITHUB_ID='github', so two plugins sharing an id collided (second unreachable, duplicate keys) and a third-party 'github' contribution hijacked the built-in GitHubSettingsTab; contribution ids are only SAFE_ID_PATTERN-validated per plugin, and the #8451 canonicalization sweep missed ~8 stringly-typed app.settings.openTab deep-link sites plus the FORGE_CLASSIFY_PUSH_ERROR IPC return; fix routes everything on makeForgeProviderId canonical ids with normalizeProviderId shimming legacy forms at read boundaries.

title: ipcMain.handle runs async handlers concurrently — same-tick read-merge-write invokes on the per-project state file silently revert each other's fields, and the renderer's persisted-snapshot cache makes the corruption sticky; serialize via ProjectStore.enqueueProjectStateUpdate
summary: Five terminalLayout.ts set* IPC handlers did unserialized read-merge-write on the per-project state file; ipcMain.handle handlers interleave at awaits, so paired 500ms-debounced setTerminals+setTabGroups invokes read the same stale snapshot and the last write reverted the other's field, with panelPersistence's persistedTerminalsByProject dedupe cache making the reverted file sticky across restarts. Fix: ProjectStateManager.enqueueProjectStateUpdate per-project promise-tail queue with .catch anti-poisoning, .then(cleanup,cleanup) not .finally, null-skips-save.

title: A shared flag registry fed by multiple React effects must refcount per publisher — flat last-writer-wins keys get permanently wiped (the victim's effect deps never change, so it can't self-heal), and publisher identity must be useState(() => Symbol()), never Strict Mode-unstable useId
summary: SettingsValidationRegistry's flat Set<SettingsTab> let one publisher's clearTab/unmount wipe another's live error under the same key (CodeForgeSettingsTab + nested GitHubSettingsTab, code-forge) permanently, since the victim's effect deps never change. Fix: useRef Map<SettingsTab,Set<symbol>> refcount; identity via useState(()=>Symbol()), never useId (react#27103).

title: An options object in an attach-effect dep array turns every appearance tweak into a full detach/reattach (and a silent focus steal) — and the in-place fix must forward deltas only, because updateOptions keys on key presence, not value change
summary: XtermAdapter's attach useLayoutEffect had memoized terminalOptions in deps, so theme-picker hovers (selectEffectiveTheme mints a new ITheme per previewSchemeId) tore down/reattached every mounted terminal, and detach()'s unconditional terminal.blur() stole focus. Fix (#10106, issue #9929): options via ref, separate diff effect forwarding only changed keys — terminalInstanceService.updateOptions refits/refreshes on key presence, and a mount-time full-options call breaks the saved-dims reattach skip; appliedOptionsRef handshake no-ops attach commits.

title: test
summary: test

title: IPC guards (checkRateLimit, absolute-cwd) are per-handler opt-in statements, not middleware — replacing a dispatch surface (github.* → forge.*) silently sheds every guard unless the migration diffs the old surface channel-by-channel
summary: When forge.* IPC handlers replaced github.* as primary dispatch, all 29 per-handler checkRateLimit guards and the path.isAbsolute cwd check were silently dropped — 14 uncapped entry points incl. forge:open-issues/open-prs reaching openExternalUrl (tab-flood risk). Guards are opt-in first statements, not middleware; a false header comment and a single-flight coalescer masked the gap. #10104 restored budgets, guard-before-swallow placement, and the exhaustive forge.rateLimit.test.ts wiring backstop.

title: Tokens derived at theme-build time are frozen against runtime input overrides, and --theme-* vars have no stylesheet fallback — so CVD maps must re-derive downstream tokens, and clearing an override must restore base values, never removeProperty
summary: themes.ts bakes --theme-diff-* from status-success/danger at build time; light-mode .diff-viewer CSS reads baked tokens so runtime CVD overrides (colorVisionOverrides.ts) never applied. Fix: withDiffSurfaces re-derives diff tokens from override hex; applyColorVisionMode restores base values on clear, not removeProperty (no stylesheet fallback).

title: panelStore pointer fields don't follow the panel — every path moving a panel out of visible scope must synchronously sweep focusedId/the maximize trio/activeDockTerminalId/pingedId in a store wrapper; reactive subscribers can't see a stale pointer, and async listeners undo fixes they don't re-derive
summary: panelStore pointer fields (focusedId, maximizedId trio, activeDockTerminalId, pingedId) go stale when registry moves change panel location unswept: three same-day fixes (#10102/#10099/#10093) fixed Cmd+W trashing a backgrounded panel, blank ContentGrid on maximize-then-move, dock-restore focus loss. Wrappers use pickFallbackFocusId/buildMaximizeClearPatch, snapshot pre-mutation.

title: @sentry/electron merges renderer scope into events BEFORE main's beforeSend fires, so sanitizeEvent must walk tags/user/contexts — and a repo-wide no-restricted-syntax ban must be replicated into every flat-config block or last-write-wins silently drops it
summary: Telemetry scrubbing: sanitizeEvent (TelemetryService.ts) skipped tags/user/contexts per a stale comment, but @sentry/electron merges renderer scope (ErrorBoundary tags, componentStack) into events pre-beforeSend. request.url's success branch left u.toString() unscrubbed. Fix = deep-walk fields, scrub URLs, replicate the lint ban across all six eslint.config.js blocks.

title: Level-state UI fed only by edge-triggered events goes permanently stale across process boundaries — a respawned pty-host has an empty status map and never emits a corrective event, and clearing the store without evicting RAF-buffered patches resurrects the stale value on the next flush
summary: Stuck 'Paused' pill (#9899): flowStatus on PTY panels is level state written only by edge-triggered pty-host terminal-status events; onExit (lifecycle.ts), restartTerminal (restart.ts), and onBackendReady (backendHealth.ts) all failed to clear it, and a respawned host's empty status map never re-emits. Fix pairs every clear with cancelTerminalFlowState buffer eviction (RAF patches resurrect cleared state; the < prevTs guard passes vacuously against undefined), re-derives runtimeStatus, and guards exited panels at the flush sink.

title: A gate can print reasons, warn, and exit 0 forever: the perf regression gate stacked six independent fail-open paths — a noise floor that exempted 100% of critical scenarios, undefined-baseline skips, a reason-without-flag branch, a stub comparison arm, silent merge-base failure, and mutation of a detached report copy
summary: Perf regression gate (scripts/perf/run.ts, lib/gate.ts) exited 0 on real regressions: 5ms noise floor exempted all criticalScenarios, missing-baseline/stub-compare/merge-base branches warned-and-passed, A/B failedBudget mutated a detached computeComparisons copy. Fixed via pure evaluateScenarioBudget(), fail-closed Number.isFinite, per-occurrence averageMetrics.

title: A credential save path can be fully green (validation passes, store populated, UI 'connected') while the live provider impl never sees the token — a persisted-store→live-object bridge needs delivery on save, clear, AND replay-on-bind
summary: FORGE_SET_CREDENTIAL persisted to the forgeCredentials store but never called impl.setCredentials, so non-GitHub forge providers ran unauthenticated while validateToken passed and the UI showed connected; builtin GitHub masked it via its own token path. Fix delivers at save, clear, and bind-time replay (buildStoredCredentials in PluginHostFactory registerForgeProvider), with deliberate throw-handling asymmetry and pickPrimaryValue shared between save and replay.

title: test
summary: test

title: Inbox dedup keys on supersedeKey alone — every writer for one logical event must route through notify() with the shared key, and a routinely-superseded row must NOT carry a correlationId or the archived-thread re-promotion path toasts it on the next cycle
summary: Notification system: history-store dedup matches ONLY supersedeKey/supersedes — never title or correlationId — so a raw addEntry beside a keyed notify() (GitHub token expiry, #9961) left duplicate durable rows. Coupled trap: sharing the key arms shouldReToast's fully-archived-thread re-promotion, so a correlationId on the superseded backstop re-toasts a priority-low row on the second expiry cycle. Pattern now generalized in useForgeTokenHealth/forgeTokenSupersedeKey.

title: Zod v4 ZodError.message is the JSON-serialized issues array — raw user values included — and handlers that report failure via returned { error } result objects bypass the throwing ValidationError sanitizer entirely
summary: IPC trust boundary: six handler sites in copyTree.ts/appAgent.ts embedded ZodError.message (Zod v4 = JSON issues array with raw user values) in renderer-bound errors; CopyTreeResult.error surfaced it as UI text. Result-object channels bypass the throwing ValidationError sanitizer; fix = static strings + exact-match tests.

title: A Doherty-gated loading flag cannot discriminate loading-from-empty — for 400ms the data is [] with the flag false, so the empty state paints a false claim every load; branch on a raw pending signal (plus an identity ref for the pre-effect frame) and render nothing
summary: ProjectRoutingPanel in ForgeIntegrationsTab.tsx branched its empty state on the Doherty-gated showRemotesLoading; during the 400ms gate window remotes was reset to [] with the flag still false, flashing a false 'no git remotes configured' on every mount/project switch (#9990). Fix: raw remotesPending = remotesLoading || identity-ref mismatch (remotesLoadedForRef vs activeProjectId, covering the pre-effect frame) with a scoped return-null guard (pending && !loading && remotes.length===0); zero-providers early return removed so remotes/RoutingBadges always render, absence copy gated on providersLoading.

title: A failed hydration read must degrade to empty-backend restore and prime the persistence diff baseline — rethrowing past restore lets the first post-boot save overwrite the user's saved session with []
summary: Cold-start hydration data-loss trap (#9928): a rejected terminal:getForProject was rethrown past panelPersistence.primeProject and restorePanelsPhase, so the panel store booted empty and the first saveNormalized wrote [] to disk, permanently wiping the saved session. Fix in hydrateAppState degrades the query to [] (mirroring the PtyClient timeout path) and primes the diff cache; invariant applies to every hydrate-then-persist Zustand store.

title: Create/wake drift recurred despite #6674's canonical installer — it only protects wiring inside its boundary, and an optional callback on an always-consume OSC handler makes the drift symptomless; only required deps fields hold
summary: TerminalHibernationManager.unhibernate() recreated TerminalParserHandler without the onDataLoss 3rd ctor arg getOrCreate() wires to drawDataLossMarker; the always-consuming OSC 57301 handler (onDataLoss?.(); return true) swallowed post-wake data-loss signals with zero symptom (#9907, introduced by #8375). Recurrence of #6674's create/wake drift outside the canonical installer's boundary; fix = required HibernationManagerDeps field so omission fails typecheck. Hibernation later deleted (#10811) but the optional-callback/always-consume shape and dual restore paths survive.

title: overflow-clip-margin is discrete — a width-to-zero collapse strands the clip edge and content bleeds at rest; the transitionend cleanup must synchronously flush under every transition-suppression mode, and perf mode is the sneaky one (it narrows transition-property, not disables transitions)
summary: AppLayout.tsx sidebar hide leaves a 6px strip (#9864): overflowClipMargin is discrete/non-animatable, so the clip edge stays 6px out when width transitions to 0. Fix gates sidebarFullyHidden via filtered onTransitionEnd, flushed synchronously under reduceAnimations, drag-resize, prefers-reduced-motion, and perf-mode narrowed transition-property.

title: PROJECT_ON_SWITCH lived only on the dead legacy single-renderer path — production multi-view activation silently never emitted it, so every subscribed consumer no-opped; switch signals must be targeted sends from activateProjectView AND menu.ts, never broadcasts
summary: Single-renderer→multi-WebContentsView migration left PROJECT_ON_SWITCH emitted only by legacy ProjectSwitchService; production activateProjectView (projectCrud/switch.ts) and menu.ts handleDirectoryOpen sent nothing, so projectClient cache invalidation and usePollingLifecycle fan-out silently never fired. Fix: targeted view.webContents.send (broadcast would falsely flag LRU-cached views). The lastSwitchId cold-launch guard built on it was reversed 2 days later (1c30610e4); the emissions survived.

title: UI stacked with an xterm pane must hold fixed height (growth re-fires fit/resize), overlays must wrap AppDialog not native <dialog> (Escape bypasses the LIFO escape stack and double-closes the host panel), and renderer state keyed to a main-process per-session counter must flush when the counter restarts
summary: Help-panel figure arc (#9860/#9863): FigureRail fixed h-[88px] since sibling growth re-fires xterm fit/resize; FigureLightbox wraps AppDialog — native <dialog> Escape bypasses the LIFO escapeStack, double-closing HelpPanel; clearTerminal drops figures/activeFigureNumber because figureCounters restart at 1, else stale figures mis-resolve ImageLinksAddon [image #N] links.

title: The scrollback-restore FSM encodes failure by resetting to "none" — its retry re-entry gate — never a "failed" state, so a settle predicate must mean "no longer in flux" with the error read out-of-band, or a cosmetic restore failure strands every waiter until timeout
summary: waitForFullySettled/waitForAllFullySettled (TerminalSettleWaiterRegistry, ex-TerminalInstanceService via #11022) gate on scrollbackRestoreState; 3 of 4 FSM exits (swallowed failure, IPC catch, bail-before-start) reset to "none" not "done" because "none" reopens the scheduler retry gate — a done-only predicate hangs 30s; isFullySettled accepts done|none, error via lastScrollbackRestoreError; notify hooks needed at all four scheduler exits plus attach-drain; "none" also = never-scheduled so a too-early wait false-settles; still no production consumer.

title: xterm 6.1's DOM renderer collapses emoji via negative inline letter-spacing (upstream #5893, fixed only in 7.0.0) — an author !important clamp scoped to negative values beats the inline style, but [style*=] selectors must cover BOTH cssText spacing forms
summary: xterm 6.1.0-beta DOM renderer (active above the WebGL pool's RAM-tiered upper threshold, bootstrap 18/15 in TerminalWebGLConfig.ts since #11192, was a static 12) writes negative inline letter-spacing on emoji spans because OffscreenCanvas.measureText mismeasures grapheme clusters (upstream xterm #5893). Fix: src/index.css scopes an author !important clamp to negative-only [style*=] selectors covering both 'letter-spacing: -' and 'letter-spacing:-' serializations (second form added in f4ef0e308 after nightly CI hit it); zero computes as '0px' or 'normal' depending on environment, needing a normalizer in the E2E test. Cannot downgrade below 6.1.0-beta.65 (reintroduces the #9546/#5818 dispose leak); remove only at @xterm/xterm >=7.0.0.

title: A visible terminal's render chain has ~5 independent suppression layers that can each freeze it alone, and the only organic repair (click-wake) destroys the evidence — recovery needs a DOM-geometry-ground-truth watchdog plus a capture-phase diagnostic that snapshots the chain BEFORE repair runs
summary: TerminalReconciliationWatchdog: 3s DOM-geometry sweep repairs the causal chain (visibility→tier→backend→ingest→render-pause→WebGL), 6s cooldown, ending 'frozen until clicked' terminals (#9777-#9781). Capture-phase pointerdown snapshots state before setFocused/wake erase it. Evolved via #10416/#10811/#10909/#11212.

title: Deferring a listener hook behind isStateLoaded mutates its subscription window — any one-shot main pushes at did-finish-load silently vanishes unless it joins _eventBusReplayable, so every staged hook needs the late-mount audit
summary: PostHydrationListeners (#9795) staged nine hooks out of AppInner's first effect flush behind isStateLoaded; useDiskSpaceWarnings' window:disk-space-status one-shot, pushed once at did-finish-load in windowServices.ts, would be silently dropped by the preload event bus on slow cold launch — fixed by adding it to _eventBusReplayable. Documents the four-category late-mount audit (re-attach latch, pull-on-mount, poll-backed, can't-fire-early), the pre-paint keep-set, and the staged-mount perf-mark rule; mount site now src/ModalHostLayer.tsx.

title: Every Electron major is a V8 ABI event: better-sqlite3 vs V8 14.8 needed an NMV-gated patch-package backport applied BEFORE any native rebuild (with failure isolation), and Electron 42's UNNotification migration silently emits 'failed' on unsigned macOS dev builds
summary: Electron 41→42 (Chromium 148, Node 24.15, V8 14.8) broke better-sqlite3@12.10.0's native compile via the v8::External::New signature change; fixed by backporting WiseLibs/better-sqlite3#1475 as a NODE_MODULE_VERSION>=146-gated patch-package patch in scripts/postinstall.cjs — patches first with --error-on-fail (default only fails under CI), skip the patched module's rebuild on patch failure so the compile error can't mask the cause; dlopen ABI probe dropped for unconditional source rebuild. Patch later removed (4f85a1236) when 12.11.1 shipped the fix. Also: Electron 42 UNNotification silently emits 'failed' on unsigned macOS dev builds — NotificationService failed-handler logs + cleanup.

title: Node's compile cache commits only on graceful exit — but Daintree ends every quit via app.exit() (no will-quit) and crashes exist, so without explicit flushCompileCache() the cache can stay permanently cold, and a FAILED enableCompileCache() is silent unless its status is captured at the call site
summary: Boot perf: Node's V8 compile cache persists only on graceful exit, but Daintree terminates every quit via app.exit() (skips will-quit) and crashy sessions never flush — so bootstrap.ts flushCompileCache() after the main.js import plus a sync flush atop runShutdownChain before any await; enableCompileCache() status captured via setCompileCacheEnableStatus into the APP_BOOT_START NDJSON mark (no later getter, no hit/miss API); perf harness strips inherited NODE_COMPILE_CACHE so cold baselines stay cold, counts versioned-subdir cache files, and clears append-only NDJSON on warm reuse.

title: A keyed warm cache whose warm key doesn't byte-match the acquire key misses 100% with zero error signal — the PTY pool warmed (projectRoot, env-empty) while restores acquire (worktree-cwd, envHash); warm the consumer's exact tuples and compute the hash in the lookup site's process
summary: PTY pool key mismatch: set-active-project warmed (projectRoot, env-empty), acquireByKey looks up (worktree-cwd, envHash) — silent 0% hit rate. #9790+#9849 thread panelCwds/projectEnv through IPC, pty-host computes envHash via computePoolEnvHash, warm after drainAndRefill epoch bump, capped below LRU eviction; POOL_HIT/POOL_MISS marks expose the miss.

title: xterm's OptionsService silently drops same-value option sets, so a font that loads after terminals opened never re-measures the grid — the only non-teardown invalidation is poking fontFamily to a CSS-identical distinct string, and the repair trigger must be re-derived when the Suspense gate it encoded is removed
summary: terminalFont.ts raced document.fonts.load() vs a 3s timeout and discarded the outcome in both branches; timed-out opens measured cells against the fallback stack and stayed mis-sized all session because xterm OptionsService dedupes same-value fontFamily sets so CharSizeService never re-measures and fit() reuses stale metrics. Fix: hold the real allSettled load, onTerminalFontArrivedLate → repairFontGrid() pokes fontFamily to a trailing-space distinct string, resets lastWidth/lastHeight, refits. #9844 removed the use(terminalFontReady) Suspense gate (≥1 blank render even when cached) and dropped the timedOut guard that encoded it.

title: Deduping outbound messages against last-known peer state desyncs permanently when the peer mutates that state silently — every host-side tier mutation must broadcast a reconciliation message, and it must ride the per-window data MessagePort to stay FIFO with the chunks it governs
summary: pty-host recomputeActivityTiers silently demoted terminals to background on window connect/disconnect/project-switch; renderer dedupe vs lastBackendTier never resent, so host suppressed bytes under a visible pane. Fix: tier-changed broadcasts over the per-window MessagePort; renderer re-arms via initializeBackendTier; undefined projectId = wildcard.

title: macOS 26 amfid SIGKILLs spawned helpers that claim a restricted entitlement — electron-builder's mac.binaries[] can't scope entitlements per binary, so helpers must be re-signed empty in afterSign and the outer .app seal repaired, because the inner cdhash change breaks it
summary: macOS packaging: on macOS 26 (Tahoe) amfid kills node-pty spawn-helper and daintree_pty_supervisor at exec because mac.binaries[] signs them with the full app plist (restricted com.apple.security.device.audio-input) and no per-binary entitlements option exists; fix = afterSign re-sign with empty entitlements.helpers.plist via resign-helpers-macos.cjs, then reseal the .app with --preserve-metadata=identifier,entitlements,flags (inner cdhash change breaks the seal); runs before the DAINTREE_SKIP_NOTARIZATION gate, CI-verified fail-closed in release-macos.yml.

title: Under heavy main-thread load Chromium's IntersectionObserver delivers stale isIntersecting=false for fully on-screen elements — confirm every hidden reading against fresh getBoundingClientRect overlap with the observation root before committing a demotion
summary: TerminalPane's IntersectionObserver wrote a load-induced stale isIntersecting=false to the store, capping a visible terminal at BACKGROUND tier, freezing output until click. isStaleHiddenReading (visibilityReadingGuard.ts) AABB-tests fresh rect vs root: hides double-checked, geometry not ratio, reads before writes, last batched entry only.

title: Chromium's HTTP disk cache never stores custom-scheme responses — net.fetch(file://) inside protocol.handle is a pure per-launch tax — but keep the validator/304 machinery, because the V8 bytecode cache is a separate mechanism that DOES need it
summary: createAppProtocolHandler (electron/setup/protocols.ts) served app:// via net.fetch(file://); Chromium HttpCache::Transaction is http/https-only, so custom schemes get zero caching — a network hop plus a buffered copy every launch. Fixed with fs.open+readFile, keeping If-Modified-Since/304 for the V8 bytecode cache (#8624), plus EISDIR and O_NOFOLLOW guards.

title: OpenAI prompt caching silently never engages below the 1,024-token prefix floor, and a prompt sent as `instructions` + string input isn't cache-eligible — verify via usage cachedTokens, never by reading the request shape
summary: VoiceCorrectionService's fixed-first prompt design got zero OpenAI cache hits for its whole life: CORE_CORRECTION_PROMPT was ~706 tokens (under the 1,024-token floor) and rode in `instructions` + string input, outside the cacheable message array. Fix: expand past the floor with useful content, developer/user input array, char-proxy floor test (>4800 chars), verify via usage cached_tokens; prompt_cache_retention deliberately omitted — unsupported models 400 and correct() silently degrades to raw text.

title: Voice session start streams PCM before the start IPC resolves, so async pre-start work must run concurrent and late-awaited behind the voiceStartNonce re-check — and Deepgram nova-3 400s the whole WS upgrade on the legacy `keywords` param, making layered keyterm caps load-bearing
summary: Voice keyterm wiring (#9753/#9757, voiceInput.ts): assembleKeyterms() tested but caller-less. handleStart concurrent-fires assembly, late-awaits behind voiceStartNonce + identity-guarded bail cleanup. Deepgram nova-3 400s legacy `keywords`; use capped `keyterm` params. gpt-realtime-whisper hard-rejects `prompt` (not a no-op), broke sessions until gated.

title: A readiness probe and the data path it gates must dial the SAME hostname: dev-preview's probe hit `localhost` (reaching Vite 8's [::1]-only macOS bind) while the proxy dialed literal `127.0.0.1` and 502'd — listen addresses want literals, upstream targets want hostnames so Happy Eyeballs picks the bound family
summary: DevPreviewProxyService shared one PROXY_HOST constant for its listen bind and its httpxy upstream target; Vite 8 on macOS binds [::1]-only, the readiness probe resolved localhost (Happy Eyeballs, passed → RUNNING) while proxy.web/ws dialed 127.0.0.1 → ECONNREFUSED → 502 on every request. Fix split PROXY_LISTEN_HOST (literal) from UPSTREAM_HOST (localhost); tests bind ipv6Only and assert IPv4 refused.

title: A count with two data sources needs recency arbitration on observation timestamps — 'source X always wins' freezes, and arbitrating on the cache-re-stamped lastUpdated oscillates because probe re-serves make stale counts look fresher than real reads
summary: Forge toolbar badge arc #9694→#9718→#9742→#10348: two sources (stats poll, dropdown list); fixed-priority arbitration freezes, re-stamped-lastUpdated arbitration oscillates. Fix: resolveForgeDisplayCount arbitrates on per-count issueCountRefreshedAt stamps; updateRepoStatsCount reconciles caches + ETag bump; adaptive nextPollIntervalMs.

title: The 'deliberately infinite' auth-fetch suspension was a classification defect in disguise — #9740's click-to-retry half-fix let the stuck stripe recur until #10675 split rate-limit/transient out of `auth-failed` and made the backoff finite with an hourly ceiling
summary: RepoFetchCoordinator suspended repo fetches forever after auth-classified failures (AUTH_FAILURE_TTL_MS=Infinity): classifyGitError bucketed broken tokens, 403 rate limits, and credential blips as one. #9740's click-to-retry half-fix let the stripe recur (#10670) until #10675 split rate-limited from auth-failed with finite hourly backoff.

title: Light themes go flat for measurable reasons — chroma decaying to zero up the ramp, depth riding ~0.02-L steps, selection darkening instead of lifting, cool ink on the wash ladders; the merged Bondi r7 file is the corrective template, and the PR's own body/comments describe rejected rounds
summary: Bondi light-theme redesign (#9727; template in #9732-#9739): hold OKLCH chroma on one hue up the ramp, lift content toward white (selection #FFFFFF, raised surface-input, opaque overlay-raised), re-ink overlayTint/scrims from field hue, borders/shadows carry depth past ~0.02-L steps; merged bondi.ts r7 contradicts the PR's blue-field narrative.

title: Fleet broadcast's confirm gate was deliberately deleted, not forgotten: the raw keystroke-mirror path has already dispatched the bytes before Enter, so a submit-time confirm on the structured path alone is unenforceable theater — arming the fleet is the consent boundary
summary: PR #9726 (#9722) deleted the #8725 fleet-broadcast confirm apparatus (fleetBroadcastConfirmStore, divergence ConfirmDialog, FLEET_DESTRUCTIVE_RE, 512B threshold): broadcastFleetRawInput mirrors keystrokes before Enter, ungatable, so consent moved to fleet arming, awareness to noteBroadcastCommit ribbon flash; safeguards doc D2->D1 safe(deliberate). Don't re-add the gate.

title: webContents.insertCSS stylesheets persist for the page lifetime — seeding first-paint theme vars at :root makes remove-by-absence optional tokens unremovable, so a live theme switch keeps the old theme's value until restart; scope injected startup CSS to #startup-skeleton, never :root
summary: Startup skeleton CSS (electron/window/skeletonCss.ts, buildSkeletonCss/insertSkeletonCss via wc.insertCSS cssOrigin:user) seeded theme vars at :root; insertCSS persists for the page lifetime, and applyAppThemeToRoot's remove-by-absence removeProperty can't neutralize it, so OPTIONAL extension tokens (--panel-grid-bg, extensionRegistry.ts) leaked the old theme's value after a light→dark switch until restart. Fix: scope to #startup-skeleton, a sibling of #root.

title: Chromium's oklab color-mix toward `transparent` mixes toward transparent-BLACK — muddy on light themes, invisible on dark; status washes are pre-baked rgba via withAlpha, and pre-baking severs live var() propagation so CVD/plugin paths must re-derive
summary: Chromium's oklab color-mix toward transparent black-shifts alpha washes — muddy on light, invisible on dark (GridNotificationBar banners). Fix pre-bakes status-*-surface as rgba via withAlpha in createDaintreeTokens; pre-baking severs var() propagation, so CVD and normalizeAppColorScheme must re-derive surfaces, guarding on tokenOverrides not normalizedTokens.

title: SVG strokeWidth is in viewBox units, not pixels — a 16-viewBox bespoke icon copying Lucide's strokeWidth=2 renders 1.5× heavier than 24-viewBox Lucide neighbors; normalize by 2 × viewBox/24 and rescale inner detail strokes by the same factor
summary: AgentStateCircles.tsx (16×16 viewBox, strokeWidth=2) rendered 1.5× heavier than adjacent Lucide CheckCircle2 (24 viewBox) in QuickStateFilterBar because SVG stroke-width scales as strokeWidth × renderSize/viewBoxSize. Fix: ring strokeWidth 1.333 (2 × 16/24) plus inner detail strokes scaled by the same 2/3; guarded by a cross-icon stroke-to-viewBox ratio-parity test in icons-a11y.test.tsx instead of literal assertions.

title: visibilitychange can be processed while the renderer is still CDP-frozen — Page Lifecycle `resume` is the authoritative thawed signal, and a wake fan-out that silently skips a mid-attach pane skips it forever unless it leaves a pending flag consumed at attach-settle
summary: Stale/blank terminals on project switch-back (#9702): frozen-WebContentsView thaw races. visibilitychange fired while the renderer was still CDP-frozen (unfreezeWebContents is fire-and-forget), fullWakeForVisibilityRestore skipped mid-attach panes with no retry, and an asymmetric resize-lock release left geometry stale. Fixes: resume listener coalesced via de-dupe, pendingVisibilityWake flag consumed by notifyAttachSettledWaiters, symmetric unlock. Code now in TerminalRevealController/TerminalSettleWaiterRegistry.

title: Widening PanelLocation drops the new member into the default bucket of every exclusion-list filter and `=== "dock" ? "dock" : "grid"` coercion — audit consumers of the OTHER members, and guard membership with a `satisfies Record<Union, boolean>` map so the next widening is a compile error
summary: PR #9668 added overlay to PanelLocation for the Daintree Assistant; exclusion-list filters and dock?dock:grid coercions across ~15 callsites defaulted it into the grid, duplicating the assistant. Fix: isGridPanelLocation()/GRID_MEMBER_BY_LOCATION satisfies Record<PanelLocation,boolean> in shared/types/panel.ts makes future widening a compile error.

title: Chromium composites a frozen view's stale pre-freeze GPU surface before any renderer JS runs — bridge warm reactivation BEHIND the outgoing view until a renderer-signaled clean frame; never repair one xterm pane via the module-global shared texture atlas
summary: Warm project-view reactivation: Chromium composites the frozen view's pre-freeze GPU surface before renderer JS runs (freeze != webglcontextlost; setBackgroundColor can't cover opaque surfaces), so ProjectViewSwitchController reattaches the cached view insertBehind and gates reveal on APP_VIEW_WARM_PAINTED with releaseChannel discrimination (#10965 added the deterministic wake trigger); xterm clearTextureAtlas() is module-global and blanks co-owner panes — per-pane fix is repairAtlasForReactivation (#9703).

title: Container opacity-50 on a live control multiplies through descendants' own alpha tokens (0.5 × text/70 ≈ 35% effective contrast, a WCAG failure) and spawns a stacking context — dim per-property via token alpha, and share both predicate and treatment across mirror variants or they drift
summary: Dock chips (DockedTerminalItem, DockedTabGroup) dimmed deprioritized idle/completed/exited terminals with container opacity-50, which multiplies with text-daintree-text/70 children to ~35% effective contrast on a still-clickable control and creates a stacking context; fixed with per-property token dim (text//40 + border//50), predicate unified as isDockAgentStateDeprioritized in useDockBlockedState.ts after the group variant drifted; #9691's hover pop-out button was reversed same-day in 90abb32a1.

title: Roving-tabindex rails with dynamic membership need explicit .focus() recovery gated on activeElement===body — reassigning tabIndex=0 after the focused item unmounts leaves keyboard focus dead on <body>, and every hand-copied roving rail keeps dropping pieces of the Toolbar.tsx checklist
summary: ContentDock.tsx roving tabindex: when a focused dock chip unmounted, the useLayoutEffect reassigned tabIndex but focus had already fallen to document.body, killing keyboard nav (#9681). Fix mirrors Toolbar.tsx: prevFocusedDockItemRef focus-capture ref, .focus() the promoted chip on eviction, gated on activeElement===body so Radix portals aren't hijacked; ref cleared before the guard. Same hand-copied rail later dropped the keydown containment guard too (#11156/#11160) — copy the full Toolbar checklist. Plus: chevrons tabIndex=-1/aria-hidden, scroll-px-4 vs scrim.

title: A debounce serving two jobs (visible filtering + localStorage persistence) makes typing lag by exactly the persist delay — split into an instant transient liveQuery and a debounced persisted query, seed liveQuery on hydrate, and commit the store value at fire time so an external clearAll can't be resurrected by a stale closure
summary: worktreeFilterStore's query was both persisted state and live filter, so WorktreeSidebarSearchBar's 200ms persist debounce delayed a sub-ms in-memory filter per keystroke; fix = transient liveQuery for instant UI + useDeferredValue for filter memos + 500ms debounced persisted write, with a fire-time getState() commit so clearAll can't resurrect stale text.

title: Virtualized-list visible-range counts have two plausibly-wrong sources — scroll-height fractions break on variable row heights, and virtuoso's rendered range is inflated by load-bearing overscan; the correct input is per-item geometry from itemsRendered vs live scrollTop, cached (it skips intra-overscan scrolls) and identity-tagged to the items array it measured
summary: Sidebar offscreen pills (useScrollIndicator.ts, SidebarContent.tsx) miscounted: scrollTop/scrollHeight fraction assumed uniform rows, and virtuoso's rendered range is inflated by 600px dnd-kit-load-bearing overscan. Fix: classify itemsRendered geometry vs live viewport (1px epsilon), cache identity-tagged to items array, count unmounted rows by index.

title: aria-live regions re-announce on every DOM mutation inside them — ticking timers, per-keystroke counts, and mixed persistent text all spam screen readers; Daintree's pattern is aria-hidden visible text + one-shot useAnnouncerStore fires on rising edges (Doherty-debounced for typing), and aria-disabled instead of native disabled so busy buttons keep focus
summary: Sidebar a11y arc (#9671/#9672/#9678): aria-live/role=status in SidebarContent.tsx re-announced a 1Hz reconnect tick and a per-keystroke count+sort-reason line; fix = aria-hidden text + useAnnouncerStore one-shot announce on rising edges (Doherty-debounced), plus aria-disabled (not native disabled) + re-entry guard so busy buttons keep keyboard focus.

title: A snapshot-and-revert gesture must capture every independent flag gating what it hides, and restore only the deltas it caused — focus mode reverted its gestureAssistantHidden mask but never snapshotted helpPanelStore.isOpen, so exit left the Assistant wherever the toolbar had drifted it
summary: Focus-mode gesture snapshot completeness: Assistant visibility is !focusStore.gestureAssistantHidden && helpPanelStore.isOpen; GestureSnapshot captured only its own mask, so exiting focus mode restored the sidebar but left the Assistant at drifted isOpen. Fix adds assistantWasOpen captured via getState() at entry, restore gated on hidAssistant so mid-mode toolbar actions survive; focusStore never imports helpPanelStore — AppLayout coordinates.

title: Spawn-batch state tear: addPanel commits panelIdsByWorktreeId eagerly but defers panelIds until flushSpawnBatch — any derivation reading panelIds alone sees a phantom-empty grid mid-batch; readers must union both indexes, because the eager index is a live mid-spawn lookup that cannot be deferred
summary: panelRegistry (usePanelStore) is deliberately torn during beginSpawnBatch/flushSpawnBatch: addPanel commits panelsById + panelIdsByWorktreeId eagerly, defers panelIds to flush. getTabGroups read panelIds alone so recipe-launched terminals derived into no virtual group and rendered blank until a worktree switch re-fired the tabGroups memo. Fix: collectUngroupedCandidateIds unions both indexes; deferring the index instead is wrong — applyWorktreeTerminalPolicy and gridPanelIds read it mid-spawn.

title: Agent restart/resume rebuilds the command purely from persisted agentLaunchFlags — a spawn site that bakes flags into the command string via generateAgentCommand but skips persisting them works perfectly on first launch, then silently drops --dangerously-skip-permissions, model, and recipe args on every restart
summary: recipeStore.ts and panelSpawning.ts built spawn commands via generateAgentCommand but never persisted agentLaunchFlags, so restart.ts silently dropped dangerous mode, model, and recipe args on resume/restart (#9650). Disk recipes strip session fields leaving flags undefined; settings fallbacks cannot recover per-panel args. Fix mirrors useAgentLauncher.

title: Electron 41+ nulls WebContentsView.webContents at destroy time — before once('destroyed') cleanup fires — so event-driven registry pruning alone can't prevent main-process crashes; every read needs presence-guard + prune-on-read
summary: Electron 41 (electron#50249) nulls WebContentsView.webContents at destroy time -- even inside its own destroyed handler -- while TS's non-optional type lets unguarded reads typecheck, then crash main when CDP Debugger emits mid-teardown. Fix: presence-guard + prune-on-read in webContentsRegistry.ts; recurred in ProjectViewManager (#10931). Regression of #4660 (v40->v41).

title: A fire-and-forget teardown that persists its resume token only after the async kill resolves loses it to a fast switch-back — write a synchronous sentinel first, ownership-guard the late overwrite, relax validators to accept the sentinel; the assistant terminal also sits outside every generic worktree-terminal fan-out
summary: HelpSessionService.revokeSession persisted the assistant resume ID only after gracefulKill resolved; a fast project switch-back hit takePendingHibernation first, got null, and fresh-launched (visible restart, #9639). Fix: synchronous empty-agentSessionId sentinel before the await, pendingCapturesByProject ownership guard, PendingHelpHibernationStore.isValid relaxed to accept the sentinel plus a capturedAt <= Date.now() upper bound. Sibling #9644: assistant excluded from the wakeActiveWorktreeTerminals fan-out froze on switch-back until fixed via collectActiveWorktreeTerminalTargets.

title: macOS quitAndInstall() never fires before-quit, so alternate exit paths silently break the clean-exit contract — hand-copying the markers fakes cleanliness without the persistence work; route the path through the single shutdown chain instead
summary: AutoUpdaterService's quitAndInstall() skips before-quit on macOS (Squirrel.Mac fires before-quit-for-update instead), so markCleanExit/markCleanLaunch never ran and cleanExit:false triggered a false crash-recovery prompt post-update (#9638). #9645's hand-copied markers were superseded by #11129, routing installs through requestGracefulShutdownForUpdate.

title: Framer Motion's global reduced-motion guards instant-complete only positional/transform keys — an opacity spring or tween sails through MotionConfig AND the CSS reduce-motion variant at full physics, and useReducedMotion never sees the in-app toggle
summary: FM12 reduced-motion trap (#9633 drag-overlay spring, DndProvider): MotionConfig instant-completes only positional/transform keys — opacity springs/tweens run at full physics; CSS reduce-motion variant can't reach FM inline styles; useReducedMotion sees only the OS pref not the in-app toggle (prefer useShouldSkipMotion); FM durations are seconds, repo tokens ms.

title: Any `filter` in a text-bearing animation — even a `blur(0)` endpoint or `will-change: filter` — routes glyphs through a composited filter pass that drops subpixel antialiasing, so ticking count chips read permanently soft; carry crossfades with opacity+transform only
summary: AnimatedLabel crossfade (label-swap-in/out keyframes, src/index.css) animated filter: blur() with will-change: filter; any filter — even blur(0) held by fill-mode: both — forces glyphs through a composited filter pass that drops subpixel AA, so always-on count chips (PanelHeader, FleetCountChip) read soft at rest. Fix #9632: opacity+transform only, plus a JSDOM-proof CSS-source contract test banning filter reintroduction.

title: app:set-state is a silent per-key allowlist — a field can have the AppState type, the electron-store schema slot, and the renderer hydration and still never persist; a persisted field needs four wiring points, TypeScript enforces only two, and only a restart round-trip proves the write
summary: handleAppSetState (electron/ipc/handlers/app/state.ts) is a per-key allowlist — unbranched/out-of-range keys drop silently, setState still resolves clean. dockedPopoverHeight had AppState type + dockStore hydration but no store.ts schema slot or handler branch, reset to 500px every launch for 4.5 months; only a two-session E2E round-trip caught it.

title: Bare renderer setInterval degrades to ~1 tick/min within ~10s of document.hidden — and every non-active project WebContentsView IS hidden; use the visibility-gated hooks with snap-tick on restore, never global un-throttling or performance-collapsed intervals
summary: Chromium throttles hidden-renderer setInterval to ~1/min after ~10s (quick intensive throttling since Chrome 108); every non-active project WebContentsView is document.hidden via ProjectViewLifecycleController's setVisible(false) plus a per-renderer CDP CPU throttle, so bare renderer ticks in SidebarContent, TerminalInfoDialog, and NotificationCenter (plus sibling PR #9585's audit-log viewers) went stale. Fix: useVisibilityAwareInterval / useGlobalMinuteTicker with snap-tick on visibilitychange restore — never setBackgroundThrottling(false) (window-wide since Electron 28, un-throttles cached siblings, #8599) and never route refresh cadence through animationUtils performance-mode helpers, which collapse it to a hot loop or zero.

title: A shallow spread on ActionService's schemaCache is aliasing, not isolation — one consumer's nested write poisons every later list()/get(); clone-on-read + DEV deepFreeze fix it, and the cited Zod reused:'inline' physical-sharing premise is false (toJSONSchema finalizes via JSON round-trip)
summary: ActionService.toManifestEntry served schemaCache entries via `{ ...cached }`, isolating only top-level keys — nested properties/items/$defs stayed aliased to the cache, so any consumer (e.g. an MCP adapter) mutating a schema in place poisoned every later list()/get() including MCP tool manifests. Fix: structuredClone on the read path, DEV-only deepFreeze with a cycle guard, structuredClone of raw plugin schemas before caching, pinned target:"draft-2020-12". Also disproves the PR's cited amplifier: Zod v4 toJSONSchema finalizes via JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(result)), so reused:"inline" never yields physically-shared nodes in the returned value — verified against zod 4.0.0/4.3.6/4.4.3.

title: Warn-then-promote quality gates rot the day their tracking issue closes — ship the hard assert now over an exhaustive two-list classification (CONFIRMED_WIRED / BYPASS_WIRED) with per-row documented bypasses, and enforce call-site existence via a check-pipeline script
summary: actionDefinitions.quality.test.ts had no-op quality gates: dangerRationale only console.warn'd, confirm-wiring was expect(true).toBe(true); TODOs orphaned when #8431/#8415 closed same-day. #9578 hard-asserted EXPECTED_CONFIRM_DANGER = CONFIRMED_WIRED union BYPASS_WIRED, added confirm-wiring.mjs (token co-location scan, not dataflow) to npm run check.

title: Electron OOM almost never reports as reason 'oom' — V8 heap exhaustion arrives as 'crashed' and the OS OOM-killer as 'killed', so OOM routing needs a memory probe; and 'memory-eviction' is not a crash (explicit reload required, never feed the crash-loop guard or the one-shot crash log)
summary: render-process-gone in ProjectViewHandlers.ts/createWindow.ts: V8 heap OOM surfaces as crashed, OOM-killer as killed -- literal oom match misses both, reloading into pressure. Fix: probable-OOM via readAvailableSystemMemoryMb vs profile lowMemoryFreeThresholdMb (null/768/1024). memory-eviction skips crash-loop guard/recordCrash, needs explicit reload.

title: Electron WebContentsView defaults to an opaque-white compositor background and the double-rAF paint gate proves commit, not GPU presentation — so setBackgroundColor(surface-canvas) must be re-asserted at EVERY view creation site; the same miss recurred across three separate factories
summary: Cold-start project switch flashed white (#9573): WebContentsView defaults opaque white (electron#37201); double-rAF proves compositor commit, not GPU presentation, leaving a present gap. Fix: resolveInitialCanvasBackgroundColor() (skeletonCss.ts) before loadURL/addChildView at every WebContentsView site — no central enforcement, miss recurred 3x.

title: Rendering a D2 preview does not gate confirm — ConfirmDialog's async-preview gate is hand-wired per dialog (null = not-loaded blocks, empty array confirms), and hasPreview must drop role=alertdialog because screen readers flatten scrollable content into one aria-describedby utterance
summary: GitPushConfirmDialog/GitPullRebaseConfirmDialog allowed confirm while the async commit preview was loading/errored (only ForcePushConfirmDialog gated); fix = hasPreview boolean on ConfirmDialog/AppDialog + manual confirmDisabled={commits === null || !!loadError} per dialog — no auto-managing preview slot exists despite the PR body; hasPreview switches destructive role from alertdialog to dialog because aria-describedby flattens scrollable content; gate load-bearing data (!meta) not ornamental sizes; check:confirm-wiring proves presence not gating.

title: MCP tool hints each map from their own semantic axis: destructiveHint derives from the danger classification, not !isQuery — and the identically-shaped idempotentHint line must NOT get the parallel fix, because safe ≠ idempotent
summary: buildAnnotations (electron/services/mcp-server/tierAuth.ts) set destructiveHint = !isQuery, so every danger:'safe' command (git.stageFile, terminal.new) serialized destructive and pushed MCP clients toward needless confirms; fix maps danger 'confirm'→true with mcpAnnotations ??-override. idempotentHint deliberately keeps the isQuery default — idempotence is orthogonal to danger and needs a per-action field (still unfixed).

title: Cold-launch OS-ingress events cross three independent timing gaps — OS→main pre-ready, main→renderer pre-subscriber, subscriber→hydration — and 'renderer has painted' is NOT 'renderer has subscribed'; each gap needs its own buffer with deliberate replay semantics
summary: daintree:// deep-link install/open (#9564): 3 cold-launch timing gaps, each needs a buffer. macOS open-url attaches at module load (deepLinkUrlQueue.ts, package.json sideEffects) or drops; paint precedes AppInner subscribing, so preload _eventBusReplayable buffers events; usePluginDeepLink gates on isStateLoaded; parseDaintreeUrl fails closed.

title: Two-phase detect-then-enrich events blank enriched fields downstream: phase-1 needs an explicit loading flag, the hold must be entity-scoped at ONE layer, phase-2 must re-emit even the empty case — and a loading flag with no guaranteed phase-2 holds stale state forever
summary: PullRequestService emits sys:pr:detected twice: sync phase-1 with no CI status, async phase-2 after batched getCIStatuses. WorkspaceService.onPRDetected full-replaced phase-1 undefined, blinking the PRBadge CI dot each refresh (#9551). Fix: isCiStatusLoading flag, same-PR-scoped hold, clear-on-null re-emit; bf5ac9ba9 omits the flag when enrichment is off.

title: xterm 6.0 Terminal.dispose() leaks GC roots inside the library — fixable only by upstream bump, and minor bumps silently reshape the options surface
summary: xterm.js 6.0 instance teardown (TerminalWebGLManager pool eviction, TerminalInstanceService's destroy(id) on panel close/project switch): Terminal.dispose() fails to release internal GC roots when the WebGL addon is attached, so renderer heap grows across close/eviction cycles despite correct app-side dispose ordering; the leak is upstream-only and invisible on DOM-renderer panes. Minor xterm bumps also silently reshape the options surface.

title: node-pty kill() leaks the master /dev/ptmx fd — every PTY teardown path must call destroy(), not just the pool
summary: node-pty's `TerminalProcess` PTY teardown (electron/services/pty/TerminalProcess.ts) leaks the master /dev/ptmx fd because `kill()` alone never releases it; all three live-process end-of-life paths (kill, onExit, dispose) must converge on `destroy()`, or fd churn exhausts macOS `ptmx_max` (~511) and blocks new terminal spawns.

title: Plugin subsystem integration traps: shared caches need ref-counting, dispatch needs the focused view, security pins must be purged on uninstall
summary: Plugin subsystem integration (`PluginService`/`WhenClauseService`/`plugin-mcp`) exhibits cross-plugin coupling traps invisible to per-PR review: process-global caches (compiled `when`-clause ASTs) need ref-counting before eviction, dispatch must target the focused view, and security pins must be purged on uninstall, else unloading one plugin breaks another or leaks registrations.

title: Atomic plugin install: extract to a SIBLING temp dir for same-filesystem rename, never re-throw in proper-lockfile onCompromised, restore runtime state on swap rollback
summary: PluginInstaller (`electron/services/plugin/PluginInstaller.ts`), the sole writer to `~/.daintree/plugins/`, must extract `.dntr` archives into a SIBLING temp dir rather than `os.tmpdir()` — otherwise the final `fs.rename` hits `EXDEV` across filesystem mounts and breaks atomicity; the swap also needs multi-instance lockfile guarding and runtime-state restoration on rollback.

title: Track the durable worktree restore target separately from the in-session active selection
summary: Worktree restore in the project-switch flow (`useWorktreeSelectionStore` snapshotted via `buildOutgoingState`, rehydrated by `stateHydration`) conflates the in-session active selection with the durable restore target, so transient worktrees from a batch PR-merge run get persisted and restored instead of the user's real root worktree.

title: React.lazy retry and AbortSignal teardown in the plugin view content layer: new lazy() ref per reset, ref-mirror the post-retry AbortController
summary: Plugin view retry/teardown lives in `src/components/Plugin/PluginViewContent.tsx` (wrapped by the chrome-only `PluginViewHost.tsx`): reusing the same React.lazy() ref after a load failure makes "Try again" silently reload the cached failed module, and not ref-mirroring the post-retry AbortController aborts a stale controller so the live plugin view's fetches/subscriptions leak past unload.

title: Sharing one React instance with externalized plugin bundles via host importmap
summary: Plugin view rendering (externalized React + host importmap): sharing the host's single React instance fails silently or at first render in three independent ways — a duplicate React copy slips into the plugin bundle, CSP strips the inline `<script type="importmap">`, or the HTML parser rejects the importmap tag — surfacing as `Invalid hook call`.

title: Custom Electron protocol containment needs realpath + O_NOFOLLOW-on-candidate, and privileged schemes must register before app.whenReady()
summary: Electron custom-scheme containment (`plugin://`/`daintree-file://` handlers in `electron/setup/protocols.ts`): lexical `path.relative` traversal checks pass while symlinked components escape the plugin root, so containment requires realpath plus O_NOFOLLOW on the candidate; privileged schemes also silently break unless registered via `registerSchemesAsPrivileged` before `app.whenReady()`.

title: Push-hydrated per-project WebContentsView goes stale after LRU eviction — needs init gate + targeted snapshot replay on view-ready
summary: Plugin contribution mirroring into per-project WebContentsViews relies on a mount-time IPC pull plus an EVENTS_PUSH listener; both fail intermittently when the pull races plugin startup activation (handlers return empty) or when LRU-evicted views cold-restore and remount before the next broadcast, leaving contributions silently empty until an unrelated mutation fires. Fix gates init and replays a targeted snapshot on view-ready.

title: Viewport-relative clamp belongs in a mount effect, not the zustand persist merge callback (innerWidth=0 pre-show)
summary: Portal dock width restore (zustand persist in src/store/portalStore.ts) clamps the persisted width against the viewport inside the persist merge callback, where window.innerWidth is still 0 pre-show, so safeMax collapses to PORTAL_MIN_WIDTH and every restore snaps to the floor; the viewport-relative clamp must run in a mount effect instead.

title: Native-module afterPack validation: N-API dlopen polarity is inverted from NAN, and existence checks pass on present-but-broken binaries
summary: afterPack native-module validation (scripts/afterPack.cjs) for vendored crash-safe PTY reapers: existence/X_OK checks pass on present-but-broken binaries (unresolved transitive deps, wrong arch), and N-API dlopen probe polarity is inverted from NAN while esbuild bundling instead of externalizing posix-pty-reaper breaks getSupervisorPath() resolution — so a dead reaper compiles, signs, and ships, failing only at first runtime use.

title: Stream interim transcription as a CodeMirror WidgetDecoration, not document text, to keep undo history clean
summary: HybridInputBar dictation streams interim speech-to-text deltas as CodeMirror document text via setDraftInput/doc.replace, so 30-50 volatile interim revisions per utterance pollute undo history (one Ctrl-Z reverts a mid-word interim, not the whole dictation) and cause visible churn; fix renders interim text as a WidgetDecoration instead. Related: sendFromEditor's final-transcript drop against the pre-stop doc (#9172).

title: Gate expensive GraphQL revalidation fan-out behind a cheap REST conditional-GET ETag probe; commit the ETag only when the caller is in sync, and keep polling CI on a 304
summary: PullRequestService steady-state PR poll fans out one ~3-point GraphQL re-fetch per tracked open PR, so at scale (25 PRs/30s) it overruns GitHub's 5000/hr GraphQL budget even on an idle repo; gate the fan-out behind a zero-cost REST conditional-GET ETag probe and only revalidate on a non-304.

title: VoiceOver drops aria-live updates from outside a focused aria-modal — close before announce, route via the announcer store
summary: ARIA-live announcer for destructive-confirm dialogs: closing an `aria-modal` element before announcing silently drops the `aria-live`/`document.ariaNotify` message on macOS VoiceOver, so blind users get no result feedback though the visible UI updates; announce before close.

title: Split PluginService load into scan-time vs activation-time; idempotent activatePlugin must never reject and must guard the unload race
summary: PluginService (electron/services/PluginService.ts) eagerly import()-ed and activate()-d every curated plugin's main module at startup, making cold-start cost scale linearly with the plugin set even for unused plugins; split loading into cheap scan-time contribution-point registration vs lazy activation, and make activatePlugin idempotent (never reject) while guarding the unload race.

title: Don't gate the crash stack trace behind import.meta.env.DEV — surface it in prod, scrubbed at the viewer boundary, scoped to stack only
summary: ErrorBoundary/ErrorFallback gated the "Technical details" stack trace behind import.meta.env.DEV, so production crash reports and the crash reporter shipped with zero trace — useless exactly where debugging is hardest. Surface the stack in prod too, scrubbed via reportScrubbers at the viewer boundary and scoped to the stack only.

title: macOS hardened-runtime entitlements rot across Electron majors; codesign --deep does not check per-Mach-O Team ID
summary: macOS release codesigning carries stale hardened-runtime entitlements in build/entitlements.mac.plist (e.g. allow-unsigned-executable-memory, unneeded since Electron 12) that survive major upgrades invisibly — they never fail builds, notarization, or runtime, only silently widen the security-relaxation surface; codesign --deep also skips per-Mach-O Team ID verification.

title: WebContentsView first-paint: inject skeleton CSS/JS on dom-ready not pre-loadURL, and thread projectId via additionalArguments not a URL query (preserves V8 bytecode cache)
summary: In ProjectViewManager's per-project WebContentsView cold-start path, inject first-paint skeleton CSS/JS on dom-ready rather than before loadURL (pre-loadURL injection is a silent no-op), and pass projectId via additionalArguments instead of a ?projectId= URL query, since query strings break V8 bytecode cache reuse across project switches.

title: VoiceOver drops aria-live updates outside the focused aria-modal subtree — use document.ariaNotify (Electron 41) with a co-located announcer fallback
summary: macOS VoiceOver silently drops aria-live announcements fired from the App-root AccessibilityAnnouncer while any aria-modal dialog is open — the DOM updates but nothing is spoken, with no error or failing test. Fix routes async status through Electron 41's document.ariaNotify with a co-located in-modal announcer fallback.

title: Hide a main-process WebContentsView by parking it offscreen (not removeChildView), and set its background before loadURL to kill the white flash
summary: PortalManager's main-process WebContentsView AI-host overlays: removeChildView destroys page state (scroll, streaming, WebSocket/SSE) on close/reopen, and missing setBackgroundColor before loadURL causes a white flash on first paint. Park the view offscreen instead of detaching, and set its background before loading.

title: Theme palette gates that constrain only OKLab L (lightness) leak chroma/hue drift — gate them warn-first, never hard-fail hand-tuned palettes
summary: Built-in theme palette test gates (`getSurfaceRampMetrics` ramp-monotonicity/ΔL-step assertions, OKLab accent-distinctness floor) that constrain only OKLab lightness silently leak chroma/hue drift, so retuning to pass them degrades hand-tuned theme identity (sidebar green tint, hue shifts); gate palettes warn-first, never hard-fail.

title: Batch multi-panel spawns at the store, not via Promise.all — Zustand's per-set() flush defeats React 19 auto-batching
summary: Multi-panel spawn batching (spawnPanelsFromRecipe, recipeStore.runRecipeWithResults): Zustand flushes synchronously per set() call, so each addPanel triggers its own React commit and CSS grid reflow — Promise.all does NOT collapse them past React 19 auto-batching. Batch all panelIds appends in a single store mutation.

title: insertCSS (user-origin) loses to renderer inline styles (author-origin); seed first-paint theme via webPreferences.additionalArguments → process.argv, not insertCSS
summary: Main-process first-paint theming via wc.insertCSS(cssOrigin:"user") loses the CSS cascade to the renderer's author-origin inline :root styles, so the wrong theme flashes on every cold start, project switch, and LRU view re-creation until async config resolves; seed the scheme through webPreferences.additionalArguments → process.argv instead.

title: Plugin unload cascade needs per-step try/catch — one throwing disposer strands later cleanup and leaks registry entries
summary: PluginService.unloadPlugin (electron/services/PluginService.ts) runs a teardown cascade across many registries without per-step try/catch, so one throwing disposer aborts later steps and leaks registry entries — notably orphaned *Impls entries that surface as duplicate-id errors on the plugin's next load; the renderer's plugin.invoke also swallows rejections, hiding throwing plugin actions.

title: Sliding-TTL security grants need a wall-clock ceiling from issuedAt or a caller can refresh them forever
summary: MCP server GrantCache "Approve once" grants use a sliding TTL: every dispatch calls refresh() to push expiresAt = now + 15min, so an agent calling the tool more often than the window never lets it expire — turning a one-shot approval into a permanent capability outliving its SSE session. Fix: clamp against a wall-clock ceiling derived from issuedAt.

title: Dev-server readiness needs a 5xx-warmup guard plus an HMR WebSocket handshake — HTTP 2xx alone is a false-ready
summary: DevPreviewReadinessProbe.waitForServerReady (electron/services/DevPreviewReadinessProbe.ts) treats any non-5xx HTTP response as ready, but 404/401/405 from history-fallback or warming auth proxies, and Docker port-forward 502/503/504 gateways that later resolve to 200, all yield false-ready panels pointed at error pages; even a clean 200 HTML shell can precede an HMR-handshake-ready bundler.

title: Every shell.openExternal must funnel through openExternalUrl's platform-conditional protocol allowlist — a renderer-supplied URL after a typeof check is a bypass
summary: Main-process shell.openExternal calls must route through the central openExternalUrl wrapper (electron/utils/openExternal.ts), which checks a URL against ALLOWED_PROTOCOLS; a renderer-supplied URL passed after only a `typeof === "string"` check (e.g. OAuth loopback authUrl) lets the renderer launch file:/javascript:/custom-scheme handlers via the OS, and every ad-hoc call site is its own unauditable bypass.

title: ready-to-show never gates first paint under WebContentsView-per-project — use appWebContents dom-ready, wired before loadURL
summary: Window first-paint under the WebContentsView-per-project architecture: because the React UI loads in a child `appView` rather than the BrowserWindow's own webContents, calling `win.show()` right after `loadURL()` reveals the window before the renderer paints, causing a blank-flash race; gate reveal on `appWebContents` dom-ready wired before `loadURL`, and don't let `DAINTREE_EARLY_RENDERER=0` mask it in E2E.

title: Strip E2E test backdoors from production builds via esbuild define + DCE
summary: Preload E2E backdoor bridges (`__DAINTREE_E2E_*` in `electron/preload.cts`) ship in packaged production builds because they gate only on a `process.env.DAINTREE_E2E_*` check, which is not a security boundary — any user launching the binary with the env var set unlocks IPC introspection and onboarding suppression; strip them at build time via esbuild `define` + dead-code elimination instead.

title: Stop processes holding a worktree directory open (dev server, terminals) BEFORE git worktree remove — Windows locks the dir
summary: Worktree deletion (`WorkspaceService.deleteWorktree` → `git worktree remove`) ignores independent main-process owners of the directory; a running `DevPreviewSessionService` dev server or open terminals hold an open handle, and on Windows the removal hard-fails (POSIX silently succeeds, masking it). Stop those processes before removal.

title: Vite-family dev servers ignore process.env.PORT — must inject --port via CLI flag, and --strictPort only on Vite/SvelteKit
summary: Dev Preview's DevPreviewCommandNormalizer mishandles Vite-family servers (Vite, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt): they ignore process.env.PORT and bind to framework defaults (5173/4321/3000), so the readiness poller hits the allocated URL and finds nothing — fix by injecting --port via CLI flag, adding --strictPort only for Vite/SvelteKit.

title: Dev-preview restart: a dead process does NOT free its TCP port — poll net.createServer().listen() before respawn (Windows TIME_WAIT)
summary: DevPreviewSessionService restart on Windows hits intermittent EADDRINUSE respawning on the same port because killing the dev-server PTY does not immediately release its TCP socket (TIME_WAIT), so the port lingers held; gate respawn on a net.createServer().listen() availability poll rather than process death.

title: xterm v6 screen-reader mode skips preventDefault on handled keys, so they bubble to Electron menu accelerators (F11/Tab passthrough)
summary: xterm v6 screen-reader (accessibility) mode in XtermAdapter's customKeyEventHandler returns true on handled keys without calling preventDefault, so bare accelerator keys (F11, Tab) bubble to Electron menu accelerators and Chromium focus traversal instead of emitting their PTY sequences on Linux/Windows; macOS escapes because its fullscreen accelerator is Ctrl+Cmd+F.

title: Wake suspended PTY processes with SIGCONT after SIGTERM so shutdown handlers run
summary: ProcessTreeKiller PTY teardown leaks dev-server ports and child workers when a descendant or shell was suspended via Ctrl+Z (SIGSTOP): a stopped process never delivers its SIGTERM/SIGHUP shutdown handler, so SIGCONT must precede SIGTERM to wake it before the sigkillSweep escalation.

title: Terminal panes must not intercept PTY-owned keys (Tab) for app navigation — it silently breaks shell/agent autocomplete
summary: xterm `customKeyEventHandler` in `XtermAdapter`: keys the PTY owns (Tab, Shift+Tab) must not be intercepted for app-level navigation.
